translations.Time for you to familiarize yourself wit: Time for you to familiarize yourself with the land and its animals. The key to spotting animals is learning their behavior and locating their need zones. That will give you a good start on you hunting experience. If you are having trouble finding any need zones, try visiting bodies of water. That gives you a clear line of sight when hunting as well.
translations.Use your hunting expertise to get close:
Use your hunting expertise to get close to the wildlife of Peru. The animal sanctuary needs a promotion picture for their website. Take a close up photo of an animal in the wild for them. Since you already have some Need Zones located, you now know when and where some of Peru’s animals will show up. 
Remember: To get close enough to take a good photo, you will have to be mindful of both wind direction and the noise you make.
translations.Now let’s put those target practice skil: Now let’s put those target practice skills to the test! Here are some hunting challenges that will help you master the pistol crossbow. Are you already feeling like a master hunter? Well, then try to complete all of them at the same time with just one shot!
translations.Got a moment? I’m texting you since Fred:
Got a moment? I’m texting you since Freddy does not need to hear this. We have received some anonymous complaints about how the reserve is run and an inspection will be launched. If you can perform 4 perfect ethical harvests, with the specified weapons that will show that only professional hunters like you are allowed in the reserve. An ethical hunt means that the animal was:

 …downed using the right type of ammunition for the animal class.

 …hit in the vital organs.

 …not hit with more than 2 shots.

 …has its trophy organs intact.
translations.María’s pet capybara, Pablo, is missing:
María’s pet capybara, Pablo, is missing after the attack. Help Freddy look for him!

REWARD: “His Majesty's Carriage” Multi-Trophy Mount
translations.María’s favorite capybara, Pablo, is mis:
María’s favorite capybara, Pablo, is missing after the attack. She has a “feeling” that he is still alive. You are asked to keep an eye out for him.

REWARD: “Her Majesty's Carriage” Multi-Trophy Mount
translations.The attack was a horrible learning exper: The attack was a horrible learning experience and if there is any substance to the rumors about a new jaguar, we have to act quickly. It is common that jaguar follow where the western mountain coatis go, because they are easy prey. So if we cull the coati population, that would drive away the jaguar.
translations.Look who made the news!! Everyone back h: Look who made the news!! Everyone back home is talkn bout u Peanut. and how you shoot that jaguar and saved the reserve. Brings me back to when I was in Peru. When I was traveling in that cloud forest in el celaje and cocha verde I told everyone that u are the stealthies of hunters. U could jus walk up to an animal and BAM kill them with 1 shot. Please.. show me that I did not just made that up??
translations.It is over. No more poachers will come h:
It is over. No more poachers will come here to destroy the eco-system now.

REWARD: “Peruvian Legends” Multi-Trophy Mount
translations.It is over. After having followed Baden’:
It is over. After having followed Baden’s disjointed clues, you have - after tremendous effort - finally tracked down all of the animals that keep the legends about these cryptids alive. Now you can present the true origin of these myths to keep inexperienced poachers out of Intisuyu. All that remains is getting rid of Baden’s notes, so that no one else can come across it and draw the same misguided conclusions.

REWARD: “Claws and Jaws” Multi-Trophy Mount

translations.Ahee, Warden. Njabulo says you’re quite: Ahee, Warden. Njabulo says you’re quite the hunter. Good enough to turn Vurhonga around even. That's good to hear. I lead a local group, the Vurhonga Sustainable Hunters Coalition. As it is, local villages have lost so many food sources, their only alternative is to buy poached meat. The VSHC supplies regional villages with legally harvested animals to solve that problem. With that in mind, our springbok supplies are low for this season, and the villagers tend to prefer the flavor of springbok who graze in Vuxa. Must be a little magic in their diet. Do you have time to harvest a springbok in Vuxa?
Those traps will not hurt anything now. Ndza nkhensa, Warden. I've got a challenging request from some elders hosting a burial feast. Seems their late relative was fond of hunting warthogs, and they want to share one to honor him. Trouble is, no one else in the village has ever hunted warthog before. Being that this is for a funeral, the elders have a specific requests: the warthog must die quickly, almost instantly. Best way to do that? Get in close and use a handgun. Think you can pull that off?
translations.Njabulo was right -- your skills are rem: Njabulo was right -- your skills are remarkable! Ndza nkhensa! Now we need your help on something else. The jackal packs are booming, and so are reports of canine diseases like rabies. We don't know the real extent of these problems, though. We need samples. Here's the twist with that -- we'd like to test for a variety of diseases within related bloodlines, so hunters are bringing us samples in pairs. Find a pack, spot a pair of jackals together, then harvest them both. Good luck.
translations.You are prolific, Warden. This next one: You are prolific, Warden. This next one is for a San family in the neighboring valley, the only traditional family left for 1000 km. They have no cape buffalo in their valley, but they will make use of whole animals if we provide them. Here's where the challenge comes: Being traditionalists, they prefer things done the old way -- with arrows. Bow or crossbow, it doesn't matter, as long as you avoid bullets. The healthiest buffalo live in N'walungu. Go there, track at least three different buffalo, select your favorite, and harvest it.
translations.Aweh, that was some buffalo you sent to: Aweh, that was some buffalo you sent to the San! While you're at N'walungu, we've noted some illegal traps in the area that could trouble the buffalo. These damn poachers never let up. Can you do me a favor? Before you disarm the traps, take a photo of one. I'll add that to our file for the police. Once you get the photo, go ahead and dismantle the terrible contraptions.
translations.One last mission for you at N'walungu. T: One last mission for you at N'walungu. That buffalo you harvested for the San? Word got around about your skill, and now, a family has asked if we could supply a buffalo for a farewell ceremony. They are sending their son to university in the city, and hope the buffalo's spirit will tell their ancestors to protect her. And of course, the buffalo will also be used for a tribal feast. You don't need to use a bow, but the animal must pass the harvest check to ensure it's food-grade. The family expressly requested a MALE animal - for recipes that require, I imagine, more "masculine" ingredients...
translations.That's a cover shot right there, Pal!! N: That's a cover shot right there, Pal!! Noyce. Njabulo hyped ur hunting skills big time, so I bet u know how to scout need zones & all that jazz... Let's see u TRACK & SPOT specific species!! Say… 1 BLUE WILDEBEEST & 1 LESSER KUDU. Then I'll know ur ready for BIG LEAGUE work!!
translations.This is how it's done, Chum!! Aight, nex:
This is how it's done, Chum!! Aight, next up I got a Variety Pack. Need CLEAR PHOTOS of these 3 animals, 1 each:
- Springbok
- Scrub Hare
- Lesser Kudu

Doesn't matter what order u take these pics in, they're all for the same story. Snap all 3, let me know, and then... MORE $$$!!
translations.Hot diggity dog, Partner!! U keep coming: Hot diggity dog, Partner!! U keep coming thru for me. Now… Wanna do some extracurricular hunting??? I'm putting together a museum diorama that recreates a South African hunting camp. It's gonna be LIT!! But! I'm short a few scrub hares. Can u harvest 3 for me? Any 3 SCRUB HARES. Use a SHOTGUN. My taxidermist can make it look like they've just been harvested!! Ever see those old cartoons with the hunter and the bunny that always gets away??? That's totally gonna be u, except u can actually CATCH ur rascally rabbits!!
translations.U ain't no joke, Hunter. I'll send u pic: U ain't no joke, Hunter. I'll send u pics of the finished diorama later. Now... Here's a more somber assignment -- U know about the accidents at the Plateau?? Course u do. Tourists ignore the signs, pass the Weeping Face, cross the bridge, slip, fall, and… that's usually the end. I'm writing a story on the site, the people who've died there, and Njabulo's earnest efforts to prevent more accidents. Can u get me up-to-date photos of the Weeping Face and the suspension bridge at the Plateau??
translations.Thanks, Matey!! Hopefully ur photos and:
Thanks, Matey!! Hopefully ur photos and my story will get a more tourists to read the signs on the Plateau, right?! Now… it's time for my BIG REVEAL!! Ur brother helped me rig cameras throughout the park. If u let me, I'd like to record u hunting and use it for an instructional video. I will pay u BIG $$$ for participating!!! All game goes to local tribes courtesy of Maria Mboweni. And all u have to do is HUNT for these goals:

1. Down ANY ANIMAL with a HEART SHOT & harvest it.

2. Down & harvest 2 SPRINGBOK w/ a SHOTGUN.

translations.Comrade, u are RAD!!! Ur gonna like this:
Comrade, u are RAD!!! Ur gonna like this next assignment, it's a vision test!! Ur mission, should u choose to accept it:

1. Down ANY ANIMAL for a QUICK KILL from at least {d:75} away -- using a SCOPELESS RIFLE. Harvest it. Awwwww yizzy!!
translations.Dr. Dana Martiz here. You're the new Sen:
Dr. Dana Martiz here. You're the new Senior Warden? Njabulo trusts you, so I should, but I didn't get where I am in life by trusting people. I got here with competency, proficiency, and a commitment to excellence, and I expect all of the above from the people I work with. As far as I'm concerned, you're unproven.

Thus I've arranged a series of tests for you. There are other hunting exams, but the Maritz Test is the most rigorous. Why? Because "good enough" isn't good enough. Do you want to be the best or be the rest?

We'll start with 4 objectives. Complete them in any order. I'll monitor you using the cameras your brother and Flip Ospreay planted around the park.
translations.I'm not going to praise just for trackin:
I'm not going to praise just for tracking and bagging Warthogs, they're extremely common game and not the least bit tricky to catch. Even a novice ranger can do that.

Let's start the more aggressive portion of the exam. Head to the swamps in Dzonga. Harvest any animal with a score of Silver or better. 

That's it. Easy bar to clear. Show me results! Don't get bogged down by carelessness like other hunters.
translations.Finally, you show me what I'm looking fo:
Finally, you show me what I'm looking for. But asking you for Silver or better doesn't meet the Maritz Standard. The Maritz Standard is Gold, always. 

Harvest any animal with a score of Gold -- and if you can do better, do better. Do your best or don't bother doing at all.
translations.You are hitting my quality bar and I lik:
You are hitting my quality bar and I like it. Keep this up, and I may just have a new favorite hunting companion. 

Next up: It's not just a hunter's skill that makes them the best. You need the best gear. And far as I'm concerned, when you're going for big game, the King of Rifles is the King 470DB. 

This gun is as useful today as it was in 1910. Hammerless sidelock ejector, rising third-bite, automatic safe with stalking-latch, sling-swivels, and chopper-lump barrels with matt sight-rib and open sights.

Harvest 3 animals with the 470DB. They don't have to be Cape Buffalo, but I'll be a Hell of a lot more impressed if they are.
translations.Big guns are clearly not a problem for y:
Big guns are clearly not a problem for you. Guns aren't enough out here in the bush, though. You need every tool in the kit.

Side-striped jackals can be elusive. Use your Jackrabbit Distress Caller to attract a jackal, then harvest it. 

This is trickier than it sounds -- you can't just let rip with the caller and expect a jackal to come to you. You'll have to find a need zone or other area that you know the jackals frequent, then use it. That's the real test here.
translations.We are now ascending to the top of the s:
We are now ascending to the top of the skill curve. This is rarefied air. Making it this far places you in the top 5% of my students. If you want to make the top 1%, don't slack off. Especially when dealing with the Widowmaker.

Your objective: Find and identify Cape Buffalo tracks, then track and harvest the buffalo. The challenge? You must bring down the buffalo with ONE SHOT that hits BOTH LUNGS for maximum lethality.

A buffalo's rib cage protects its vital organs from most angles. Pick your point of entry before you shoot. Have you studied buffalo anatomy yet? Now might be a time to refresh yourself.
translations.With any skill shot like that, you have:
With any skill shot like that, you have cause for pride, but don't get ahead of yourself. You still have to pass my final exam.

Equip the King 470DB if you're not already carrying it and harvest a Cape Buffalo with a Gold score or higher. The #1 quality a Maritz-approved hunter needs is integrity, so bring down the buffalo with a passed harvest check. 

This is how you show respect for the animal, respect for the land, and respect for yourself. Anything less and I don't know how people live with themselves. Good luck, Warden. Let's see your best work.
translations.Yo, Peanut. Good times havin u back. Gra: Yo, Peanut. Good times havin u back. Grandfather been driving me nuts. Sorry I haven't called -- texting is better. Who calls anymore, anyway? GRANDFATHER. ALL THE TIME. Anyway. Here's a crappy job, but u gotta do it. Collect DROPPINGS from 3 DIFFERENT SPECIES. It's for the local veterinarian. Why any 3 random species? Who knows. She's probably testing for rabies or something. Vurhonga's clean, but all around us? Outbreak. Full on. So u best go get that dookie.
translations.Never were afraid to get ur hands dirty,: Never were afraid to get ur hands dirty, Peanut. Please wash them before starting this next thing. It's a chance to show off ur hunting skills and I know how much u looooove that. Am I jealous? Of course I'm jealous. Grandfather worships u. But I also admire u, so, whatever. We need u to harvest a SIDE-STRIPED JACKAL using a BOW or CROSSBOW. Quick & clean. Not too hard for u, is that?
translations.Show-off. U make it look so easy. How ca: Show-off. U make it look so easy. How can I compare? All I've got is a university degree in computer science. Grandfather doesn't understand how important computers are these days. I think he's even afraid of them sometimes. Anyway. Next assignment will humble u. Go to the SWAMPS in Dzonga. Find TRACKS from 2 DIFFERENT SPECIES of animals. Txt me when ur done.
translations.Peanut, I'd thank u for ur work but that: Peanut, I'd thank u for ur work but that would only contribute to the ego that Grandfather is already intent on inflating ad infinitum so… Meh. Wanna do something else? We take random samples of animals at their watering holes to identify parasites and bacteria before they spread. Harvest ANY 2 ANIMALS and pass the HARVEST CHECK near a WATERING HOLE. I'm sure u won't disappoint us.
translations.Well, well, well, Peanut. Is this easy f: Well, well, well, Peanut. Is this easy for u? Just another day in the office? Ur about to meet ur match. Grandfather's superstitious friends are having a memorial feast in honor of Baden, and u have been chosen to obtain their meat. Go to the MOUNTAINS marked on your map at NIGHT and harvest ANY 2 ANIMALS with a BOW or CROSSBOW. Sure, u bagged a side-striped jackal with an arrow before. But did u do it while climbing a mountain in the dark? If ur scared, it's okay, u can admit it. At least give me that satisfaction.
translations.U are a true nightcrawler, Peanut, and I: U are a true nightcrawler, Peanut, and I begrudgingly admit that I respect u for that performance. Unfortunately, I must now listen as Grandfather openly refers to you as his "Favorite Grandchild". In front of me. What did I do to deserve this torture? Also, Grandfather wants me to go out and camp in some HUNTING BLIND to harvest an animal. Can u do it for me, and say it was me? ANY ANIMAL. Please. Next time we hang together, I'll jailbreak your HunterMate so it can do it all kinds of cool things. Deal? Deal.
translations.Know what, Peanut? U got Grandfather off: Know what, Peanut? U got Grandfather off my back about the hunting blind! He's proud of me and it feels good. Unfortunately, now he thinks I'm turning into an expert hunter like u… and he wants me to harvest 3 MORE ANIMALS with HEART SHOTS. Can u help me just one more time? Grandfather and I are having a breakthrough. Please do the hunting for me. Pretty please.
translations.It's Vicente, Carolina's nephew. Hope yo: It's Vicente, Carolina's nephew. Hope you are doing well, we have some formalities to run through before you are licensed and approved. To start harvest any animal in Prados de Lupinos. We'll submit your results to the Fauna Departmento for approval.
translations.This is Vicente, Carolina's nephew. Hope: This is Vicente, Carolina's nephew. Hope you are doing well out there! We have some formalities to run through before you are licensed and approved. For a start, harvest any animal in Prados de Lupinos. We'll submit your results to the Fauna Departmento for approval.
translations.Before that, they say the cove was used: Before that, they say the cove was used to store contraband. But I wouldn't know a thing about that.
translations.Yes, and it's thanks to hunters like you: Yes, and it's thanks to hunters like you! Someone has to cull the unhealthy animals... and buy our entry passes.
translations.Yes, of course! Could you visit the fami: Yes, of course! Could you visit the family and let them know that Old Scar is dead? They should be in the area.
translations.Good work. Is there anything else you ca: Good work. Is there anything else you can tell me about the area?
translations.Strolling across dazzling fields and thr: Strolling across dazzling fields and through soft rolling hills, this part of Iberia is a romantic setting for any reserve. It is no wonder that warden & custodian Alejandra considers her soul entwined to the very land itself, this hunting ground of kings. From the oddly graceful marble quarry, soft hills and crumbling monastery, to the meadows covered in sunflowers and lavender alike, Cuatro Colinas Game Reserve will take your breath away.
translations.You’ve hunted among the rolling hills of: You’ve hunted among the rolling hills of Hirschfelden and explored the iconic Layton Lake District. Now get ready to face nature’s most challenging conditions during a rare hunting expedition to Medved-Taiga National Park. Inspired by the harsh, frozen landscape of Siberia, you’ll traverse the unforgiving tundra, enter into the drunken forests and venture out on the frozen bay. Here, the weather can turn at an instant, leaving you swept in whirling snow and surrounded by cracking ice.
translations.You’ve wandered through valleys and hill: You’ve wandered through valleys and hills, savannas and frozen forests but now, it’s time to explore our latest reserve in South America. Parque Fernando has asked for your aid in turning an otherwise wild slice of Patagonia into world class hunting grounds. Roam through the gnarled trunks of the dead forests, traverse the swamps and hills, and make your way across the grasslands as you open outposts, build lodges and prove yourself to the reserve’s fierce owner, Carolina. Only time will tell if you can turn the reserve into a hunter’s paradise.
translations.Explore a sprawling archipelago that tee: Explore a sprawling archipelago that teems with life. Hunt waterfowl, ducks, and upland birds, in addition to larger game such as Brown Bear and Whitetail Deer. Gaze at the magical Northern Lights, and discover exciting new hunting opportunities in this region of the “land of a thousand lakes”.
translations.Nestled at the foot of the Southern Alps: Nestled at the foot of the Southern Alps, this paradise is home to both temperate beech forests and steep alpine peaks. While some are drawn here in search of Sika Deer, others come to trace its trails of history. You can rest easy knowing your next adventure awaits in Te Awaroa National Park.
translations.The reserve wardens Conni and Doc have r: The reserve wardens Conni and Doc have received a new shipment of equipment and thanks to Robert Sommer's connections, they were able to get their hands on a tent and a ground blind. These new items will make your hunting experience in both Hirschfelden and Layton Lake District even more complete.
translations.Our wardens have just received some heav: Our wardens have just received some heavy looking boxes containing exciting new hunting equipment. With this new pack, you will be able to create the perfect ambush using the Deployable Treestand and Deployable Tripod Stands. Through their more stealth-like approach to hunting, your impact on the environment will be reduced, ensuring that your hunting pressure is lowered. So pack your bags hunter, the wild beckons!
translations.Having explored the idyllic Layton Lake: Having explored the idyllic Layton Lake District, roamed the hills of Hirschfelden and hunted in the ice-cold forests of Medved-Taiga National Park, it’s time to head south to the Cradle of Life. Vurhonga Savanna is in need of your assistance, and it is up to you to answer the call. Traverse the scrublands, discover the riverlands and venture out into the lush savanna as you assume the role of a Warden and protect the lands from poachers and other potential misfortunes. Opportunities like this are few and far between, so pack your suitcase. Africa is calling!
translations.With the appearance of Hirschfelden’s fi: With the appearance of Hirschfelden’s first field fowl, the Canada Goose, it was time for Connie and Doc to order some new items for the store.
translations.Referred to by some as “The Last Frontie: Referred to by some as “The Last Frontier” and “The Land of the Midnight Sun”, it’s hard to deny that Alaska is a place of untamed natural beauty. Under the watchful gaze and devoted care of warden Jim Murray, Yukon Valley has become a haven for knowledgeable hunters and ecologists, looking to maintain the delicate balance of the ecosystem. With its breathtaking environments that stretch from the rolling hills of blood-coloured moss, to the snow-covered mountains framing the reserve; Yukon Valley is spectacular to behold.

translations.Fair hunter, you have won your reputatio: Fair hunter, you have won your reputation amongst us all. Even beasts and spirits will heed your call. Such is the joy of your presence. If you are inclined, I humbly request your presence tonight at Spreeberg Castle when rises the ruddy moon's imperfect round.
translations.But there is one who was fiend enough to: But there is one who was fiend enough to envy us in our joy: the lonely, wretched boar, Gesualdo. His envy begat curses upon my family and me for he wished for our separation. And since that day, we have been imprisoned. It is enough to drive me to despair!

translations.The most powerful specialist bird load p: The most powerful specialist bird load produced commercially. Heavier pellets offer more power over long distances. Perfect for hunting large birds such as geese or turkeys. Encased in an old-school brass shell this power packed load can also get you small game at closer ranges!

translations..223 high velocity bullet that combines: .223 high velocity bullet that combines the superior aerodynamics of a spitzer type bullet with the rapid expansion of a hollow-point. This allows for very flat trajectories, while the increase in penetration, compared to the soft-point variant, makes it ideal for long-range shooting of small to medium-sized game such as roe deer and coyote.
translations.A copper-pointed hollow-point bullet in: A copper-pointed hollow-point bullet in the classic .22 Long Rifle caliber. This hyper velocity hollow point is great for target shooting and small game hunting. The hollow-point design emphasizes expansion over penetration, and its enclosed based offers superior accuracy.
A truncated cone bullet in the classic .22 Long Rifle caliber. This hyper velocity bullet is great for target shooting and small game hunting. Compared with its hollow-point counterpart, the truncated cone design emphasizes penetration over expansion and fragmentation.
translations.A highly versatile polymer-tip bullet th: A highly versatile polymer-tip bullet that trades expansion for superior aerodynamics and penetration. The relatively low recoil of the .243 caliber, combined with enough power to take on most kind of deer, makes this a favorite for many that are new to hunting.
translations.A highly versatile soft-point bullet tha: A highly versatile soft-point bullet that trades penetration for rapid expansion upon impact. The relatively low recoil of the .243 caliber, combined with enough power to take on most kinds of deer, makes this a favorite for many that are new to hunting.
translations.The .25-06 is a necked-down version of t: The .25-06 is a necked-down version of the .30-06 cartridge, combining high muzzle velocity with the ballistic coefficient typical of .25-caliber bullets. The polymer-tip loading, paired with a premium propellant, increases the bullet’s velocity and terminal performance, ensuring excellent penetration on medium-to-big game.

The .25-06 is a necked-down version of the .30-06 cartridge, combining high muzzle velocity with the ballistic coefficient typical of .25-caliber bullets. The lightweight soft-point projectile has an especially flat trajectory and delivers well-controlled expansion, making it an excellent choice for medium game.
translations.A .270 caliber polymer-tip bullet that i: A .270 caliber polymer-tip bullet that is configured for high penetration and superior aerodynamics. The .270 caliber is a substantial step up in power compared to .243 which makes it a good choice for larger game such as wild boar and red deer.
translations..30-06 bullets with a polymer tip that p: .30-06 bullets with a polymer tip that provides superior penetration performance. Previously used in the military, this old but proven ammunition has found a second life in the civilian market. Its good ballistic performance and widespread availibility have made it a staple choice for big game hunting.
translations..30-06 bullets with an exposed lead poin: .30-06 bullets with an exposed lead point that provides superior expansion performance. Previously used in the military, this old but proven ammunition has found a second life in the civilian market. Its good ballistic performance and widespread availibility have made it a staple choice for big game hunting.
translations.A .300 magnum polymer-tip bullet that is: A .300 magnum polymer-tip bullet that is configured for high penetration and superior aerodynamics. The .300 magnum caliber is known for its high velocity and pinpoint accuracy, which makes it a good choice for long-range shots on very large game such as moose, elk, and brown bears.
translations.A .300 magnum caliber soft-point bullet: A .300 magnum caliber soft-point bullet that trades penetration for rapid expansion upon impact. The .300 magnum caliber is known for its high velocity and pinpoint accuracy, which makes it a good choice for long-range shots on very large game such as moose, elk, and brown bears.
translations.A hollow-point bullet in the classic .30: A hollow-point bullet in the classic .30-30 caliber. The aerodynamics are not on par with modern spitzer designs, but when used at close range this bullet can cause serious trauma. Compared to its soft-point counterpart, the hollow-point design emphasizes expansion over penetration.
translations.A round nose bullet in the classic .30-3: A round nose bullet in the classic .30-30 caliber. Compared to its hollow-point counterpart, the soft-point design emphasizes penetration over expansion.
translations.Designed and manufactured to perform in: Designed and manufactured to perform in all conditions; the .308 polymer-tip has excellent accuracy and penetration. A well rounded cartridge; it offers manageable recoil and is useful for a large variety of game. For these reasons, it has become one of the most popular cartridges in the world.
translations.Designed and manufactured to perform und: Designed and manufactured to perform under any conditions; the .308 soft-point has excellent accuracy and rapid expansion upon impact. A well rounded cartridge; it offers manageable recoil and is useful for a large variety of game. For these reasons it has become one of the most popular cartridges in the world.
translations.A massive .338 polymer-tip bullet that i: A massive .338 polymer-tip bullet that is constructed for superior aerodynamics and penetration. This caliber is very popular among guides and outfitters working in bear country, as it is one of the few calibers with enough power to reliably stop a charging bear. Ideal for most large and dangerous game.
translations.A massive .338 soft-point bullet that is: A massive .338 soft-point bullet that is constructed to expand rapidly upon impact. This caliber is very popular among guides and outfitters working in bear country, as it is one of the few calibers with enough power to reliably stop a charging bear. Ideal for most large and dangerous game.
translations.The small size of .410 bore shotshells m:
The small size of .410 bore shotshells make them advantageous for rapid, short-range shooting.

translations..410 bore is the smallest commonly avail:
.410 bore is the smallest commonly available shotgun shell. Most effective at close range.

Buckshot contains a small amount of medium sized pellets. Damage is higher than bird shot at the cost of a less dense shot pattern. This makes it suitable for taking down targets at close range.

translations.The Tufted Duck is a common species of d:
The Tufted Duck is a common species of diving duck found mostly in Western, Central and Northern Europe. It lives in marshes, wetlands and sheltered coastal areas where it feeds on molluscs, insects, crustaceans, roots and seeds.
Males have a peculiar tuft of feathers on the back of their heads, giving the species its name. Their black and white plumage is also very distinctive, making them easy to recognize among other ducks.
translations.The Tundra Bean Goose is a species nativ:
The Tundra Bean Goose is a species native to the Nordic European countries and Siberia. It is very closely related to the Taiga Bean Goose, and some specialists consider them separate species while others do not. Both also often coexist with the more widespread Greylag Goose, sometimes forming mixed flocks.
Like other grey goose species, Tundra Bean Geese gather in large flocks in preparation for their winter migration. These large groups can be seen feeding in grassy wetlands for most of the day in preparation for their journey south.
translations.The warthog is a member of the swine fam: The warthog is a member of the swine family, and is related to pigs, boars and hogs. Ironically, the thick growths of skin on the warthog’s face aren't warts at all, but patches that act as padding for when males battle each other for a mate. The female warthog, called a sow, is a social animal and lives in groups called sounders, with up to 40 members. Males on the other hand are often solitary and territorial.  Warthogs stand up to {d:0.85} tall and can be nearly {d:1.5} cm in length. They have large upper tusks that can extend to {d:0.63} at their largest. Being one of the most heavily preyed upon animals in Africa, they keep these tusks in constant use, fighting for survival, as well as the right to mate.
translations.The water buffalo is the largest member: The water buffalo is the largest member of the bovini tribe, making it a truly massive and intimidating animal. Feral herds of the water buffalo are present in many parts of the world, most notably in Australia, New Guinea, Argentina and Tunisia, after they were initially brought there for domestic purposes. Water buffalo can grow to be nearly {d:2} at the shoulder and frequently weigh over a tonne, making them visibly larger than the African Cape Buffalo. They use their massive horns to defend their herd, fight for dominance, or spar with other herd-mates. Feral herds pose problems to local communities because of overgrazing and territorialism and are difficult to fight off due to their imposing stature.
translations.The Western Capercaillie is the largest:
The Western Capercaillie is the largest of all grouse species. Similar to the Black Grouse it's known for the mating ritual. Males perform for females with with puffed out feathers, strutting and very distinct calls. During mating season the ritual can get very aggressive and males can end up killing each other.
Female and male capercaillie are easily distinguishable by their size and colouration. The male is much bigger than the female and their plumages are distinctly different. The female capercaillie live in flocks with their yearling chicks while the adult male are almost always solitary. 
The name Capercaillie comes from Gaelic “capul coille” which translates into “horse of the woods”.
translations.The Western Mountain Coati (Nasuella oli:
The Western Mountain Coati (Nasuella olivacea) is a small member of the raccoon family found in the cloud forests and páramo of the Andes in Colombia, Ecuador, and northern Peru. The animal has olive-brown fur, a pointed snout, and a long tail marked with faint rings.
It spends much of its time on the ground, digging through soil and leaf litter in search of insects, worms, and other small prey. Fruit is also eaten when available. The Western Mountain Coati is mostly active during the day and is often seen moving in small family groups. It is well adapted to the cool, damp conditions of high mountain habitats where relatively few other carnivores are commonly found.
translations.The whitetail deer is one of the most co: The whitetail deer is one of the most common native deer species in North America. It is a medium-sized deer, characterized by the white underside of its tail that can easily be seen when the deer is alarmed. Its fur color ranges from red-brown to grey-brown. Whitetail deer vary quite a lot in size. Bucks weigh in from {w:45} to {w:100}, and also develop medium-sized antlers that can branch into several points along one main beam. Whitetails are highly adaptive herbivores that live in forests, as well as more open prairielike environments. They do not pose a threat to humans, and can run up to speeds of 75 km (47 mi) per hour when scared. They can also leap over obstacles as high as {d:2.7}.
translations.Long the subject of folklore, the Wild H: Long the subject of folklore, the Wild Haggis is said to roam the misty slopes of the Scottish Highlands, swift, shy, and oddly fragrant. Accounts describe it as small, shaggy, and quick as a darting grouse; however, no two witnesses ever agree on the details. While science continues to roll its eyes, the legend remains woven into Scottish culture. The national dish, haggis, is often jokingly claimed to be made from this elusive creature—though in truth it’s a hearty mix of sheep’s offal and oats. Whether myth or marvel, the Wild Haggis endures as Scotland’s most elusive game.
translations.Also known as the wild swine or the Eura: Also known as the wild swine or the Eurasian wild pig, the wild boar is native to most parts of Europe and Asia. It is also one of the most spread and adaptable mammals in the world, characterized by their bulky bodies, coarse fur, and prominent shoulder hump. Their head is shaped and used as a veritable plow, allowing them to upturn considerable amounts of soil and rocks weighing {w:40} – {w:50}. A wild boar can run up to 40 km (25 mi) per hour and jump obstacles above {d:1.5}. Boar are highly social animals and tend to live in groups. Hunters should take considerable care as boars are very tough, and will not hesitate to defend themselves if threatened.
translations.Turkeys are native to North America, and: Turkeys are native to North America, and turkey hunting is big all across the continent. It's so popular that hunters are warned not to stalk them in case they might be heading towards another hunter's ambush. Turkeys are land roaming animals but are known to be able to fly around {d:400} in a single go. They can easily climb trees and enjoy using them as hiding areas from ground predators while they roost. They're known to be very unpredictable and extremely easy to spook. As part of the Galliformes bird order, they are closely related to other game birds such as pheasants, partridge, and quail. Males are called jakes, gobblers or toms, while a female is called a jenny.
translations.The wild yak, a native species of the Hi: The wild yak, a native species of the Himalayas, is a robust animal well-suited to its environment. With its broad hooves and strong legs, it can skillfully navigate steep and rocky slopes. These creatures are highly adaptable to freezing temperatures, enduring as low as -40 degrees F (-40 degrees C) by huddling together for warmth. Both males and females possess long, shaggy hair with a thick woolly undercoat on their chest, flanks, and thighs, providing insulation against the cold. They generally avoid humans, often fleeing for great distances if approached, but it is said that "Wild yak shooting is as dangerous as it is exciting, for a wounded beast, especially an old bull, will often attack the pursuer."
translations.The Willow Ptarmigan is a species of gam:
The Willow Ptarmigan is a species of game bird that is closely related to grouse, living in the Arctic and subarctic regions of Northern Eurasia and North America. It is the largest living species of ptarmigan.
Willow Ptarmigans are territorial birds. Males defend their territory fiercely during breeding season, in an attempt to attract females. In the fall, they become more gregarious and form large flock prior to their winter migration.
translations.The wood bison (Bison bison athabascae):
The wood bison (Bison bison athabascae) is a North American subspecies found mainly in Canada’s northern forests and plains. Once nearly extinct due to overhunting and habitat loss, conservation efforts have led to their recovery.
Wood bison are the largest land mammals in North America, weighing 400 to 1350 kg and standing about 6 feet tall at the shoulder. They have thick, dark brown fur with a mane around the head, helping them stay warm in cold climates.
These herbivores live in forested areas near rivers, feeding on grasses and shrubs. Known for their social behavior, wood bison often form small herds and are protective of their young.
translations.The wood duck is a colorful waterfowl na: The wood duck is a colorful waterfowl native to North America, often found in wooded wetlands, rivers, and lakes. These ducks are medium-sized, with males featuring vibrant plumage of iridescent green, purple, and white, while females have more muted brown feathers with a distinctive white eye ring. Wood ducks are excellent fliers and perching birds, often seen resting in tree branches near water. They primarily feed on seeds, acorns, and small invertebrates. Known for their unique nesting habits, they often use tree cavities or man-made nest boxes. Wood ducks are one of the few duck species that can perch on trees.
translations.The woodland caribou is a smaller subspe: The woodland caribou is a smaller subspecies, living in the dense boreal forests of Canada. They have a streamlined body and smaller, less branched antlers compared to other caribou. Woodland caribou are non-migratory, remaining in their forest habitats year-round and feeding primarily on lichens. Typically solitary or in small groups, they are known for their elusive nature and preference for remote, undisturbed areas. They are vulnerable to habitat fragmentation from logging and increased predation. As a result, they are considered a species at risk in many regions, with conservation efforts focused on protecting their critical habitat.
translations.The Woolly Hare is a high-altitude hare: The Woolly Hare is a high-altitude hare species native to Central Asia, the Tibetan Plateau, western China, and the northern mountainous areas of Nepal. It has adapted to the high altitudes of the region and lives in the range of 2500 to over 5000 meters above sea level, making it the species with the widest altitude range of any leporids. It is a relatively large hare with a thick and wavy pelage to shelter it from the harsh climate of the alpine region it inhabits. The woolly hare is a shy and typically solitary creature, and despite occasional daytime activity, it primarily operates at night, foraging for grasses and herbs.
translations.Where did you find this?! It's a medieva: Where did you find this?! It's a medieval artifact, dating back to the Kingdom of Mapungubwe, the first class-based society in Southern Africa. They were farmers, mostly, who built their lives around their land and their families, under the leadership of a king and tribal chiefs. This kingdom may have controlled ivory and gold in the region -- which is likely where the raw material for this little guy came from. But again, where did you find this? It belongs in a museum!
translations.Homotherium, or the Scimitar-Toothed Cat: Homotherium, or the Scimitar-Toothed Cat, was a variety of sabretoothed cat that lived in Africa until about 1.5 million years ago. They were a meter long and weighed nearly 200 kilograms, roughly the size of a male lion. Their "scimitar" teeth, like this one, were shorter than other sabretoothed cats, but flat, serrated and sharp enough to slice through the thick hide of Deinotherium, a prehistoric forebear of the elephant who also called Vurhonga home. Can you imagine hunting one of these? An original apex predator.
translations.Some people call these the \"false\" sab: Some people call these the "false" sabretooths because their canines are too short and not flat enough to qualify as true sabretooths, but they were plenty deadly. They were about the size of a jaguar, far smaller than their scimitar-toothed cousin the Homotherium. They still pursued mammoth-sized prey, but they had a taste for hominids, including our ancestors. We know this because when we find Dinofelis remains, we sometimes find hominid skulls nearby -- with holes in their heads that match the not-quite-sabreteeth canines of Dinofelis.
translations.The Great Escarpment runs for thousands: The Great Escarpment runs for thousands of kilometers across Southern Africa. Its features were formed from a seismic rift that slowly tore apart the super-continent, Gondwana, over hundreds of millions of years. Today, we get these beautiful views. This area of the Escarpment, where the plateau's elevation is highest, was dubbed the Drakensberg by the Dutch, uKhahlamba by the Zulu, Maluti by the Sotho. I call it whichever phrase is least likely to offend a particular person, which is good practice in general in Africa.
translations.My favorite hiking trail. You may not re: My favorite hiking trail. You may not remember, but I took you for this walk when you were still a toddler. Halfway through the hike, you sat on the ground and told me your legs were too tired to go on, so I had to carry you the rest of the way. Too bad I was already wearing a 20-pound pack. Eish! My back still hurts.
translations.Behold, the swamp! It has its own beauty: Behold, the swamp! It has its own beauty, I think. And it can be one of the most peaceful areas in the park, when the Tsetses aren't inhabiting it. Conserving wetlands is no easy task, and unfortunately, they are steadily eroding and drying up. In another few decades, they may not be here anymore.
translations.Across the river and over the hills, Vur: Across the river and over the hills, Vurhonga is surrounded by tribal villages. The threats that preoccupy us here at the reserve also do harm to the villagers. Drought and poaching, these are vast and systemic problems that we cannot solve. We can't protect everyone and everything in the world. All we can do is our best work, every day, with our best intentions, to protect Vurhonga. That is how you must approach this job, otherwise it may break your heart.
translations.Before the drought, poachers would cross: Before the drought, poachers would cross the river here in small boats. Now they often drive a truck right across the dry riverbed. The boundaries of the reserve are impossible to fully secure. All we can do is monitor them, and react as quickly as possible to problems.
translations.Vachellia xianthophloea goes by many nam: Vachellia xianthophloea goes by many names. Mwelele, kimwea, olerai, murera. But I like the English name for it: Fever Tree. Sangomas use the bark to induce divine visions. Inyangas use it to protect people from malaria. What's more, a Fever Tree Forest protects the area it covers from erosion. The only bad thing about this forest is Nsuna, the mosquitoes who thrive in the wet, shady terrain beneath the trees. They give you malaria. But! Once upon a time, colonizers blamed the trees for malaria, instead of the mosquitoes. That's why it's called Fever Tree -- when in reality, it can PROTECT you from malaria. To me, that story is a reminder that facts are important. Details matter. Remember that!
translations.When the river floods Theron Gorge, it g: When the river floods Theron Gorge, it gets all junked up with debris. Trees and rocks, mostly. Once the debris dries out, a lot of it can be useful as raw material. Dyambu is all too happy to shine for us. Eish, anyway! The rock layers in the walls date back to the Permian Period, 300 million years ago. We've found all sorts of amazing things here. Dinosaur fossils, desert rose formations, early human artifacts. You never know what you might find here.
translations.The Plateau looms over Vurhonga like a l: The Plateau looms over Vurhonga like a lion at rest. Many people have fallen to their deaths trying to climb here, over the years. We get all kinds of daredevils and sportsmen. It's enough to clamber upward, but to actually reach the top? You'd have to be mad to scale it hand over hand. And yet, I've seen it done! The ancestors give some people wings. Anything is possible!
translations.The Dutch call these rocky outcrops kopj: The Dutch call these rocky outcrops kopjes, which means "little head". They may seem like warts on the landscape at first glance, but they provide a range of benefits. For one, they collect water and provide shade to plants that grow around them. Some animals have even evolved limbs adapted to traversing the rugged terrain. Guests love to climb them. And more than once, I have discovered people having physical relations on them. I don't know what that's about, because a rocky hill, shady as it may be, is not exactly a comfortable place to lie on.
translations.The Eloko is a devil with a grudge again: The Eloko is a devil with a grudge against the living. I believe the Eloko was brought to Vurhonga by a Mongo ranger who was visiting from the Congo. There is nothing wrong with Mongo rangers, generally speaking, but this man was cursed with bad luck. He was mutilated while on patrol in Dzonga. Third month on the job. The marks on his body did not match any animal at Vurhonga. Before he died, this man chided me for my traditional spirituality. Told me it was time for Africa to be more prosperous and set aside the old ways. Back home, he said, he had heard strange bells in the forest. His traditionalist elders warned that the Eloko rang those bells as a warning because the man had ventured too far into the forest. Within days, they said he would be dead. Yet, he said, here he was alive at Vurhonga, safe and sound. Three days later? Mutilated.
translations.My Tonga friend, Banji, introduced Nyami: My Tonga friend, Banji, introduced Nyaminyami to me. We always joked about how foreigners could never understand that Xitsonga and BaTonga are completely different people, different cultures. I thought, why not appropriate some BaTonga to confuse them even more? But you know what, Nyaminyami has brought a flood to our gorge from time to time. Banji tells me it's because his ancestors are pleased to see us collaborating across ethnic lines.
translations.A basalt cliff 30 meters high, Jedidiah': A basalt cliff 30 meters high, Jedidiah's Wall is a favorite guest photo opportunity. Guests will ask if someone built the wall, but it's naturally occurring. Once, it held an entire lake behind it. When rainwaters flooded the lake, and the waters spilled over the dam, they carried mineral deposits down the river with them -- including quartz, agate, and diamonds. Guests love to hear about the diamonds. I also find this to be a lovely spot for a picnic. Or maybe I'm just writing this for you on an empty stomach!
translations.For thousands of years, the San have loo: For thousands of years, the San have looked to the stars and spun stories of their origins. The /Xam said the stars were people. Some !Kung said that stars are tiny porcupine-like creatures and their spines are the starpoints. Other !Kung said that stars are ant-lions with exceptionally bright eyes, scouting the Earth for ants to eat. Individual stars also had their own mythologies. What we call Antares, the !Xu called "the Fire-Finishing Star" because it sets late at night, when the camp fire is dying down. The /Gwi also have a "Fire-Finishing Star", but they refer to another star, Regulus. The circle of stars that form Corona Australis were said by the /Xam to be a group of men who were eating together. Innocently, apparently. Then a bewitched girl looked at them, and they all became stars! If looks could kill, right? Now, imagine you had no TV. No movies. No Internet. No games. All you have is the night sky and your imagination. What stories would you tell?
translations.I am superstitious, yes, but there are s: I am superstitious, yes, but there are superstitions to which I do not subcribe. One such belief is the lightning bird, a creature who sucks the blood of young women and slays men with thunder from its wings and lightning from its talons. The true identity of this mythical monster? The hamerkop, an actual bird that barely weighs half a kilogram, and would never harm a human, unless you tried to rob its nest. One positive consequence of the folklore surrounding the hamerkop is that locals tend to keep away from them -- including local poachers.
translations.These San paintings date back 10,000 yea: These San paintings date back 10,000 years, to about 8000 BCE. They show hunters and antelopes, naturally. Hunting was your only option for a career in those days. These paintings show that certain aspects of San life have persisted longers than any other civilization or society. But most remarkable is the fact that we can see these at all. Ancient humans, working with nothing but the plants and minerals around them, concocted a dye which has lasted centuries of weathering. How could we ever call such people primitive?
translations.Diamphidia is a tricky creature. As an a: Diamphidia is a tricky creature. As an adult, it seems like an ordinary beetle. But as larvae and pupae, diamphidia produces a toxin that destroys red blood cells in mammals. The San apply this poison to their arrows, enabling them to subdue larger game with a single well-placed arrow. That process can take several hours or even days, but the San are nothing if not patient -- they will track their game until it drops, on foot, even if they have to travel 70 kilometers on foot.
translations.The San (it's impolite to call them \"Bu: The San (it's impolite to call them "Bushmen") are the first Africans, and perhaps some of the first humans to survive beyond the first, core group of Homo sapiens. Time and again, they have been subject to genocide, but miraculously, remnants of San nations survive. Each San group is different, but they have many common traditions and practices. San women know every plant in the bush and every use for it. San archers are skilled hunters who make clever use of poison to subdue game. They have a relaxed, practical lifestyle and a relatively stress-free society, even though their life expectancy is shorter than ours, and daily survival is far more demanding and physically rigorous. Yes, there are ways that San people stand to benefit from "modern" ways. But instead of instructing the San, maybe we should be asking what we can learn from them, because their society has been around longer than any of ours, and that can't be an accident.

translations.The legendary blade has awoken once more:
The legendary blade has awoken once more...

An age of strife is upon us. Creatures of Darkness™ from a world beyond our own roam the land, doing the bidding of their evil master Namé. When her peaceful forest village is sacked, a young human named Aerona is taken prisoner and brought far into the mountains of the north. There she awakens to the power of the legendary Resplendent Sword and becomes a Bearer, assembling a rag-tag group of allies from all races to help her in her fight against the forces of darkness. But how far is she willing to go to preserve the world she loves? Will she be able to defeat Namé, or will she too succumb to the power of the sword she was destined to wield? 

From the renowned director of gripping period drama Our Daily Gruel and blockbuster hit The Retaliators™: Endless Strife comes this adaptation of R.J. Pine's classic novel Resplendent Sword. Experience a breathtaking fantasy world where the forces of good and evil clash in spectacular cinematic set-pieces. Marvel as the latest innovations in practical effects and CGI come together to create a Resplendia that exceeds your wildest imagination.

FILM BACKGROUND:
Aeons ago, the world of Resplendia was a series of bickering petty kingdoms too wrapped up in their own affairs to notice the encroaching threat from the Creatures of Darkness™. It was only after much cajoling from the Queen of Four Unities that the four races banded together to craft a weapon of legend to face them. Blueprints drawn up with much bluster by humans were realised with iron from the dwarves, forged in enchanted fire from the elves, and cooled with the purest water from the dwelling places of the merpeople. This legendary blade shone brilliantly at all times and came to be known as the Resplendent Sword. Wielded by the legendary warrior Bryn, it cut down the Creatures of Darkness™, banishing them to whatever shadowy realm they came from and restoring peace to the people at last.

translations.Salutations, followers and friends! My s:
Salutations, followers and friends! My sincerest apologies for the recent delay between posts. I have been out of contact some days after I lost my way in the ever-shifting forests of Resplendia. Permit me to elaborate.

I had assembled some spoils from Aerona's village the previous day, and my hope was to deliver tidings from the Battle of Stonecastle Valley the next, but my journey had wearied me and I required repose. So I set down in a humble shack not far from the site of the great battle, and set to sleep. This was far from any modicum of civilisation, human or otherwise, and my telephonic device was as a useless trinket. The next morning the heavens opened, and for days afterwards I could do nothing but sit and wait for the gods to look more kindly on my expedition.

By the third day I was restless, half-starved, but unwilling to leave; I had come so far, further than any man in his search for knowledge of what had transpired here. I decided to leave the shack and pursue quarry. Accompanied by my faithful longbow and shortblade, I cast my mind back to my youth and fashioned some rudimentary arrows out of the driest wood I could find. I was ready.

Then, what folly! A deer I found, but he was not well, and I was desperate. I shot him true, and killed him, and cooked his flesh. That foul supper left me ill some nights, no closer at all to my original purpose.

The rain had cleared at last, however, and I was able to journey to Stonecastle Valley, though I still felt the ill effects of that fateful meal. When I wandered back into the forest I saw something I can scarcely begin to detail: a terrifying creature, reared up on its hind legs against a tree, like the ghostly Dreadbeasts that dwell in the forests of Resplendia. Then I had had enough; I fled posthaste, and some of my hard-earnt spoils were left behind. 

So that is my tale. I apologise once again for the lack of updates, but expect more soon.

translations.Kiri,\n\nI've kept this from you for far:
Kiri,

I've kept this from you for far too long. I came up here because I wanted to make it right, and this was the last address I had for you. I had no idea everything had been torn down. Did you approve this? It seems so unlike you. But I guess that's not for me to say.

Anyway, I've held on to this for far too long, and I'm sorry. I'm sorry for this, and I'm sorry for what happened between us. I hope this gets into your hands. If you don't hate me after this, reach out, okay? Our hunting trips are still some of my fondest memories. 

- M.M. 

22nd Feb. 1985
My dear Kiri,

Things have come to a head. The others don't approve of me dating someone from the town, and they've made it their mission to get rid of me. I just wish you'd listen. I know that some townies haven't been nice to you, but that goes both ways: we've been monopolizing the forest, not letting them walk on public land. That's not a collective, Kiri, and we of all people should know that. It's bullying. 

Look, PLEASE contact me if you change your mind. I'll give Melanie the address, and this letter. I love you lots. 

Stay Safe,
Mum
translations.1 out of 5 stars\nNo running water, no e:

No running water, no electricity, no facilities at all, really. Don't trust the owner, Carolina. She promised pumas in the area. Been here 6 days, haven't seen a single cat. FALSE ADVERTISING! Worst so-called reserve I have ever visited in my life. I would give it zero stars but that isn't an option.
translations.THE PATAGONIAN ADVENTURES OF GILBERT BAD:
THE PATAGONIAN ADVENTURES OF GILBERT BADEN, ANIMAL WHISPERER

Excursion Day #14

Set up camp near my new friends over at the "Cave of Wonders" I found. Shared my last camping rations with them. They sure were hungry! 

Now that I'm out of rations, the only way to earn their respect here in the wild is to hunt down fresh meat. I've played 10,000 hours of hunting games on my computer, so I feel more than adequately prepared for this challenge. How hard can it be?

Of course, I won't be catching anything barehanded. I need a weapon. But do not fear, I'll find one! My new friends will see, when Gilbert Baden sets his mind on something, nothing can stop him.

My cause is just, my will is strong!

-G. Baden
translations.\"Thursday: 23:25 - Definitely more sign:
"Thursday: 23:25 - Definitely more signs of activity around the disused uranium mine. Footprints and some superficial damage to the mine entrance.

Saturday: 01:40 - Decided to camp out by the mine, and there's been no activity tonight. Going to stay up until dawn and will sleep until lunchtime.

Sunday: 00:15 - A truck just drove most of the way in towards the mine. It's black, with tinted windows. If I had to guess, the government are sending agents out to retrieve resources from the mine. Two guys got out and tried the entrance. They had knives but no real equipment for getting in. Were they testing the door to make sure that nobody could get in, or are they worried about something getting out? I couldn't see if they were armed, but if they're part of something big, they're almost certainly going to have pistols.

Sunday: 06:45 - Followed the truck to the edge of Silver Ridge Peaks, but I'm low on fuel and have to get back to camp. Is Allen Bradley aware of this? Is he IN ON THIS? I'm going to need allies if we bring this conspiracy to light, but first I need fuel and some breakfast. 

Sunday: 18:15 - If the government have kept the uranium mine going in secret, what else could they be hiding down there? I'm not leaving Silver Ridge Peaks until I find out."
translations.Gem. We are going back to Denver. We hav: Gem. We are going back to Denver. We have left some food for you. Please call the warden when you find this, so he can take care of you. You shouldn't be out here alone, but we're all too sick to go looking for you. Please bring our phones back to the office ASAP. - Patrice
I'm sorry that we had this disagreement. To remedy things, I am going to lead our next yoga session at the top of the mountain that we spoke about yesterday. Make sure you bring the map with the markings. Once you get back, grab your yoga mat and join me. I'll be meditating. - Gem
translations.\"The walk here was an absolute nightmar:
"The walk here was an absolute nightmare. I've lost my phone and my favourite water bottle, as well as absolutely ruining my brand new shoes trying to get away from a bear! When I hit it in the nose with the bottle I felt bad, but there was nothing else I could do. I wonder how the guys at APAR will feel about me throwing a water bottle at a wild animal? I hope they appreciate that it wasn't my first choice to encounter a bear in the first place.

I've been trying to meditate, but I am constantly distracted by what seems like animal sounds, coming from the trees nearby.

The accountants are taking forever! I've been waiting here for ages, and there's no sign of them. I'm definitely at the right spot. We picked this mountain as it stands out so much. I should be easy to find.

Really wish I hadn't thrown my water bottle. I haven't had a drink for hours now, and all I've eaten are wild flowers. Starting to feel a little woozy. I hope those accountants bring some snacks and a drink with them.

Just want to go home. This was such a promising idea; take an office on a yoga retreat, make some money and spend some time in the wilderness. It was almost perfect timing. Now I wish I'd never won the trip out here in the first place.

 I should think about heading back. Those sounds from the trees have only gotten louder."
translations.Alena,\nI am beginning to regret staying:
Alena,
I am beginning to regret staying on this expedition. My Huntermate broke when I crashed my ATV. Then the storm came... and came... and came. I know we are supposed to ration our food, but I was stuck inside and, well, what else could I do but eat? Now, I am all out. You know I suck at hunting, but lo and behold, I found a dead musk deer by the river, frozen fresh! What a miracle! Thanks to that meat, I am alive. Now I must get healthy. I've got this terrible cough, a fever, and no medication. I can't wait here any longer. I'll take all the musk deer meat I can and hike for base camp. I don't know how far I'll make it on the taiga. If you find this note, and I am not already safe and warm at base camp with a bellyful of reindeer stew, please send help.
- Gunther B.

translations.Now let’s talk about Hunting Pressure! W:
Now let’s talk about Hunting Pressure! Whenever you kill an animal, pressure will grow around the exact location where the animal dies. If too much pressure is generated in an area animals will avoid it and their Need Zones will disappear. That is called Dead Zone pressure. 
By using a bow the pressure will increase slower. So let’s test with some Class 3 animals, shall we?

translations.The rifle is the hunter’s most trusted a:
The rifle is the hunter’s most trusted and versatile weapon. With its long range you will almost always stand still while firing it. So why not take the opportunity to use one of our hunting structures?

Like with bows, the Hunting Pressure in the area increases more slowly when downing animals from a hunting stand or a ground blind. Also, if hunting deer, remember to use a caller to attract its attention just before the shot to increase your chance of hitting their vital organs.
