translations.Padre Abbas isn't related to us, but he': Padre Abbas isn't related to us, but he's been like family to both my father and myself. A cool, calm head in times of trouble, he has guided me through the roughest times when my father was too tied up in his own business. While he has responsibilities in town, he spends a great deal of his time wandering the reserve, taking notes for his book. He has found something special during his time here, and wants to share it with the rest of the world. He is an old man, however. I know he struggles to get around the reserve.
translations.Doña Alejandra Del Bosque Garcia is the: Doña Alejandra Del Bosque Garcia is the only daughter of Don Miguel Alejandro Del Bosque Escajeda and Doña Angelica Garcia. While she has taken on the role of caretaker and warden for the Cuatro Colinas Game Reserve, her father is still the official owner and operator. Despite only being 32, Alejandra has experience of living and working in many different cultures. Coming from a wealthy and well established family has allowed her to travel and study abroad, pursuing her passion for zoology. Despite her love of travel and adventure, she has always claimed to have a spiritual bond to Cuatro Colinas, which has pulled her home on many occasions. Her most recent trip home was spurred by family tragedy that has left her father a shell of his former self. While she has always seen Cuatro Colinas as her destiny, she has a great deal to learn about running the business. She would much rather be hunting in the reserve than trying to balance the books.
translations.Well, as you know, my name is Asmita Gur:
Well, as you know, my name is Asmita Gurung, and I'm one of the Conservation Officers working with the Sundarpatan Hunting Reserve. I'm married, I have two daughters who are still in school. My husband - he works in Qatar actually, so we haven't met for quite a long time. But we sometimes talk online, and that's better than nothing.
I really love this job, because this is the closest I got to what would have been a dream job: conservation biologist. Using science and technology to monitor and protect wildlife, that's my thing. I didn't get to study or become a scientist, but I'm proud to be able to do my part!
I also run a homestay, which is really good to bring in some more income. But I also love cooking and meeting all kinds of travellers, both from Nepal or abroad, so that's definitely scratching an itch in me. :)
translations.Paul Beatty was born to be on the move,:
Paul Beatty was born to be on the move, preferably on foot. He has traveled all over the world, but he always ends up returning to Layton Lake District, his home and birthplace, at least once a year. He is a huge admirer of the moose, and his father is a renowned hunter in the area. Paul has a close relationship with his dad, and they often come up with friendly but difficult challenges for each other and other locals.

Paul works as a tour and trail guide for visiting hikers in the reserve, and he usually knows the best hunting spots around, in addition to local landmarks and points of interest.
translations.There are two hunt clubs worth a mention:
There are two hunt clubs worth a mention here in Mississippi Acres, the Delta Big Game Club and the Delta African-American Hunting Club, and Betty’s the chairwoman of the former. The Big Game Club’s in her blood; her family have practically run the damn thing for four generations. She’s the first woman chair, and given that they actually only started admitting women in the late nineties, that’s no mean feat. 

Betty’s nice enough, but as Southern as all get-out, as they say down here. A traditionalist, you might put it. Not gonna lie, we had a bit of a run-in after I moved; her “boys” in the Big Game Club weren’t super enthusiastic about the prospect of some transplant from Chicago opening a summer camp here. But we’ve put all that behind us now; helping our community recover from this flood’s what’s important.
translations.Vinay Bhandari is a biologist, and membe:
Vinay Bhandari is a biologist, and member of The European Bison Advisory Organization whose goal is the reintroduction of bison in Europe.

Central Europe has been the focus of the group's efforts for 20 years since the project began. Bhandari has relocated to the Hirschfelden area to be able to study the population up close. Most of his time is spent in a lab running tests, but during the autumn season, he spends most of his time at his cabin in southern Tichenau.

The Bison Advisory Organization has done wonders for the species in the reserve and beyond. The bison population in Central Europe has increased dramatically in the last few years, to a point where Bhandari has recommended employing hunters for wildlife population control. This has become increasingly important as Bhandari's recent research has uncovered a rise in disease rates among the bison.
translations.About myself...\nMy name is Birendra Maj:
About myself...
My name is Birendra Majhi, I am 57 years old, and I have always lived in Pauwa, a small village in Terai.
I have a farm, some animals, and also I work as a Conservation Officer on the Hunting Reserve. So I work with Asmita sometimes, she is a good friend.
My wife died a few years ago, and my 4 children are now adults and have their own families.
I like reading, carving wood.
I have my dog, she is very important to me, and... I am sorry, my English is not so good, and I do not like to talk about myself. Let us talk more next time we meet in person.
translations.Allan Bradley is a 26 year old man, who: Allan Bradley is a 26 year old man, who has grown up in the shadows of the Rocky Mountains. For years, his father Joe has been preparing him to take over the stewardship of Silver Ridge Peaks. Unfortunately, due to complications from heavy metal poisoning after consuming contaminated water, Allan was forced to step into the role early, while Joe recovered. The problems with the contaminated water have been disastrous, and Allan is keen to look for alternative means of making money. He is currently putting his experience as an extreme sports instructor to work, adding rappelling and snowboarding to the list of reasons for people to visit the reserve. While capable as a hands-on warden, he is still getting used to the administrative side of running things.
translations.Your Brother is a genius. His worst prob: Your Brother is a genius. His worst problem is that he knows he’s a genius. He uses his intellect to excuse his laziness. That’s why I must be extra hard on him. I admit he does a variety of useful things for Vurhonga Savanna, everything from setting up cameras to monitor the reserve, to using drones to resupply outposts, to basic radio communications and even our website, which will hopefully attract more tourism. I know sometimes you two compete, but he can’t do what you can do, and you can’t do what he can do. If you work together, you are an unbeatable team.
translations.Carolina Vargas (67) is an entrepreneur,:
Carolina Vargas (67) is an entrepreneur, conservationist, philanthropist, and retired shooting champion. Born in Catalonia but raised on the Patagonian Steppe by her Argentinian father, Carolina emerged on the national stage from 1976—1977 as a two-time back-to-back champion in the 50 meter rifle, 3 positions. In 1978, she married ranching tycoon and conservationist Fernando Vargas.
In 1979, Carolina and Fernando purchased the land for a reserve that was then called Parque Dorado. Hailed as a hunters’ paradise, rich with diverse species of game imported from around the world, Carolina and Fernando planned to open the reserve for tours by 1985. Before work on Parque Dorado was complete, tragedy struck. Fernando died suddenly, leaving a grief-stricken Carolina in charge of his family business, Vargas Companía Industrial. She renamed Parque Dorado to “Parque Fernando” in her husband’s memory, but the vast wilderness remained closed to the public while Carolina focused on the family business. For decades, Parque Fernando was maintained as an exclusive retreat for Carolina and her family. Friends fortunate enough to join Carolina for hunts there often returned with record-setting red stag trophies, drawing international interest to Parque Fernando. But the world would have to wait… Until now. In 2016, Carolina delegated key responsibilities at Vargas Companía to the next generation of leadership, re-dedicating herself to opening Parque Fernando. Today, that work is nearly complete. Carolina is proud to finally fulfill the dream she shared with Fernando all the way back in 1979. She pledges that Parque Fernando will be nothing less than a hunters’ paradise.
(Official biography provided by Peak Hunting Outfitters)
translations.Hey there! You're talking to a proud mem:
Hey there! You're talking to a proud member of The Sasquatchers, or the finest group of Sasquatch watchers I've met. Every other weekend, we answer the call to investigate the sight of a potential sighting or some tracks or other, sometimes hours away from our homes. It's no big deal to us, though. We do it for the love of the great outdoors – and, of course, Sasquatch. You'd be surprised how many Sasquatch stories you hear from the other Métis and First Nations folk when you're on the hunt! I'd love to share them with you now, but Janine is telling me something about a "character limit". Kids and their computers, huh?

Anyway, when I'm not out in the wilderness, I'm usually behind my desk as the controller of our local agricultural partnership. Or I'm taking care of my wife Emma and our two boys. They've been pretty disinterested in Sasquatch so far, but recently they've been talking about joining me. Something about capturing video evidence for an app about clocks? Beats me.
translations.I doubt the history of the taiga is a su: I doubt the history of the taiga is a subject that interests most Americans, but archaeologist Dr. Columbus Neidell is so fascinated by the region, he is recognized as an authority on the matter -- even by Russian experts. Back in university, I interned for Neidell. It was his first expedition to the taiga. We hit it off so well, I became his assistant for the next two years. What drew me to Neidell was his drive to not only discover human history, but preserve it for future generations. As the permafrost thaws and the taiga erodes with it, there has never been a more critical time for such work.
translations.Emily Connors thrives in isolation as a:
Emily Connors thrives in isolation as a writer. She feels at home perched up in one of the many lookout towers spread throughout the Layton Lake District. Her subject matter often deals with mankind's relationship with nature, and there is a strong sense of existentialism in all of her writing. For the two seasons that she has worked as a firewatch at the reserve, she has been particularly drawn to the Roosevelt elk.

Even though she believes that humans should be able to coexist with animals, she recognizes the importance of hunters working in population control. In her free time, she likes to observe the Roosevelt elk and has taken valuable notes on their patterns and behaviors in her little notebook.
translations.Years ago, Juliana Ferrari was one of my: Years ago, Juliana Ferrari was one of my first sharpshooting pupils. We have been hunting partners and close friends ever since. Juliana and her family own an agency that caters to elite, foreign hunters and anglers. To deliver a steady stream of guests to our reserve when it opens, she’s putting together a package of promotional materials, booking our first tours, and suggesting quality-of-life improvements to ensure Parque Fernando is competitive with other locations in Patagonia.
translations.Albertina Fleischer knows everything the:
Albertina Fleischer knows everything there is to know about the red deer in Rotwald.

Her love for red deer was born out of an episode in her youth. She was separated from her parents during a hike in the woods and wandered around for several hours on her own, trying to find her way back to them. When she was about to give up, she happened upon a red deer stag, standing motionless a few meters away. After a tense silence, the deer continued on its way without paying her any notice.

For some reason, Albertina decided to follow the deer. Her small legs couldn't keep up with it at times, and the stag would stop and wait for her to catch up. Suddenly, the stag was frightened by the snapping of twigs in the distance and ran away. When Albertina stopped to listen, she could hear her parents calling for her in the same direction and ran to them to be reunited.

Nowadays, Albertina lives in a small settlement close to the top of Bohndorf Hill. She is good friends with a taxidermist named Finn, who lives in a city neighboring the reserve.
translations.Hello, and welcome to Salzwiesen! Have y:
Hello, and welcome to Salzwiesen! Have you visited us before? You might have met my father, he used to be the warden here. I'm not quite the hunter that he is, but I know every bit as much about our park.

Have you heard of our competitions? My father was the one who created them, but lately I've been adding in a little spice of my own. Our current competition is our best yet, full of exciting challenges and lots of prize money. You simply must join if you haven't already.

Come, take a look around! Though, if you're using a road vehicle of sorts, then please, be cautious. You wouldn't want to buy a brand-new sedan and rush out, late to a dinner date, only to have said sedan trashed by a demonic-looking pheasant. A pheasant, by the way, that appears from nowhere and vanishes before you can gather any photo evidence. Hypothetically speaking, of course.
translations.Name’s Freddy. Just Freddy!\nI’m the con:
Name’s Freddy. Just Freddy!
I’m the conservation officer at Intisuyu. If something breaks, disappears, escapes, or starts eating someone’s livestock… I’m the one who deals with it.

Most days I’m running around the reserve checking trail cameras, talking with locals, and fixing things before María notices they were broken in the first place. It’s a good system. She keeps the donors happy, I keep the jungle from eating everybody.

I grew up in the high Andes not far from here, so reading the land comes naturally. Tracks, wind, bird calls… they all tell you something if you know how to listen. Jaguars too… but if you’re close enough to hear them properly, you’ve probably made a mistake.

Luckily we have hunters like you around to help keep the balance.
translations.Oscar Freeman applied to work at Yukon V: Oscar Freeman applied to work at Yukon Valley when he was fresh out of college. His passion for ecology convinced me to bring him on as part of a six month trial. That was two years ago. Since he became our resident population ecologist, I've seen him go from strength to strength. He's become a real expert in his field, and an asset to the reserve. I know he loves this place, but I can tell that he's getting itchy feet. His contract is up in a couple of months, so I guess we'll see what he wants to do then.
translations.Tansi. I'm glad that you can assist us w:
Tansi. I'm glad that you can assist us with the preservation of Askiy Ridge. This area means a lot to to many of our community members, myself included, and I hope it soon means a lot to you too.

I'm Gabe Chatelaine, one of the many council members who protect the health and safety of Askiy Ridge. As Janine has likely told you, it's only been in recent years that we've reclaimed this land for our own people. Our Cree ancestors have spent thousands of years in these plains and forests, and today we have the pleasure of welcoming you onto its rich soil.

While the past holds deep meaning for us, we cannot neglect the future wellbeing of our residents. We are supported by the Albertan government, but our people yearn to one day become independent and secure their own living. The Askiy Ridge Ski Resort for us is a vital stepping stone on this path to independence. Once construction of the ski resort completes, I will be the first of many to welcome you back to Askiy Ridge and our home.
translations.Isla is an exceptional gamekeeper by tra: Isla is an exceptional gamekeeper by trade, who has worked the Roans’ grounds for over two decades. She has everything under control, fully aware that she’s best in the business by anyone’s metric, however, the only metric, measurement or method that matters is Isla’s own; something she’ll give to you for free, and frequently. Her desire to have more people see her work is fierce. She doesn’t need nor want the validation, she just loves to show off, and her Laird’s decision to limit who can come or go is starting to piss on her chips. Sooner or later, she’ll open the grounds, yelling to anyone with ears that “Isla McLachlan is her(e)!!”
translations.Señor Baden is a curious fellow. He has: Señor Baden is a curious fellow. He has arrived in the reserve with a collection of top-of-the-range weapons and gear. He claims to be on a European tour, with the aim of setting marksmanship records across the entire continent. I've no reason to doubt his ability, but when he was done listing his accolades, he paused for a second, as if waiting for applause. With any luck, he will enjoy his time here and pass on without upsetting anyone, including my father, who happens to hold most of our marksmanship records.
translations.There are some small sections of Cuatro: There are some small sections of Cuatro Colinas that are not owned by my family. This is government-owned land, which means our reserve has oversight from the local mayor. Jose Hernandez is a politician, through and through. His major concern is to keep people happy, but it's unclear if this is due to a feeling of civic duty or a desire to be re-elected next year. Regardless, he is feeling the pressure of a shaky economy, and he has already started asking questions about the option of selling parts of the reserve to help his bottom line.
translations.Cornelia \"Conni\" Holzer is a warden an:
Cornelia "Conni" Holzer is a warden and ranger at the Hirschfelden Hunting Reserve. Born in Maine, USA, she majored in Biology at Stanford University, and field studies for her doctorate took her all around the world, studying different biomes and biotopes. During a visit to the Layton Lake District reserve, she met Doc for the first time and they became friends. 

After a few years of traveling the globe, she eventually found love in Europe and decided to settle down. Having studied and loved nature all her life, she received a Wildhüter (game warden) degree, and eventually moved with her life partner to Hirschfelden, where she was offered a job as a reserve warden.

Conni is very friendly, knowledgeable, and professional, which makes visitors return every year to explore the reserve's beauty under its warden's oversight.
translations.Richard Hope moved into the Lake Distric:
Richard Hope moved into the Lake District region two years ago. His life was shattered when his son and wife died in a traffic accident while he was stationed overseas in the military. After the accident, he took himself off the grid and came to the Layton Lake District reserve. The only ties he wishes to have now are between him and nature.

Hope's years of living out in the wild has made him a full-fledged survivalist. He is completely self-sufficient, as he is able to find food, stay warm, and protect himself. Hope is also an expert hunter with a rifle, and is the local expert on the reserve's blacktail deer population.

He's had some confrontations with Jonathan Trampfine, who he believes to be out of his mind and likely to get himself killed at any minute.
translations.Hey! You know me, right? We got our hunt:
Hey! You know me, right? We got our hunting licenses together, way back when? Not gonna lie, you *really* weren’t much to write home about back then, but I’ve seen your socials. What a difference a couple of years makes! 

Anyway, I’m still a middle school teacher (social studies and history!), but a couple of years ago I bought up some land and moved from my hometown of Chicago to here in Mississippi Acres, the place my grandparents left behind. Since then, I’ve been laser focused trying to turn this into a home away from home for disadvantaged kids. It’s been tough, but last year, we finally opened Camp Haven. Now all we’ve got to worry about is the small matter of the worst flooding we’ve had in decades, plus whether or not certain segments of the community have it in for me… well, my folks *did* warn me about coming here. 

But at least my new counselor has my back, right?
translations.Gerlinde Jäger has hunted since she was:
Gerlinde Jäger has hunted since she was a child, and grew up with fallow deer on her doorstep in Hirschdorf. It wasn't until recently that her interest in them grew to an irresistible degree. She has become the local expert on the fallow deer population and their behaviors.

She mostly hunts fallow deer for the venison, as she knows how to harvest and make use of each part of the carcass. She extends this thoroughness to her preparations for the hunt, which involves selecting the right ammunition and placing her shot carefully. Gerlinde now lives with her son Erik in Rathenfeldt, on fallow deer land. When not hunting, she focuses on writing. Her content matter is, of course, the fallow deer.
translations.Tansi! (That means Hello in Cree.) I'm g:
Tansi! (That means Hello in Cree.) I'm glad that you could make it. I'm Janine Armstrong, and I'm the sole Land and Resource officer for Askiy Ridge. This place has been my home ever since I was a little girl, so I'm more than happy to be sharing it with you.

Hmm, what else? Oh, both of my parents are Métis, or a mix between First Nations people and the first Canadian settlers. I've spent my whole life growing up in the nearby Métis settlement and exploring this area come rain or shine. As soon as Askiy Ridge Hunting Preserve was formed, I knew that I wanted to get my master's in environmental conservation to protect it. This place is my home, and I hope it becomes yours too and put the word yours in italics. I want our hunter to feel welcomed when they arrive. Did you get all that? Thank you! Please don't forget to cut this part out at the end.
translations.Jim Murray has been the warden of Yukon: Jim Murray has been the warden of Yukon Valley for 18 years. His passion for the natural world was instilled in him as a young boy, growing up in rural Washington State as the son of a tree surgeon and a zoologist. This passion gradually evolved into the study of biological science, with a speciality in conservation biology. After leaving university, he spent the next decade of his life travelling the north-west corner of the United States, studying climate change for the US government. When the opportunity arose for Jim to become an Alaska wildlife trooper, he took it, knowing it would give him a chance to have a more direct, hands-on approach to fighting climate change. Within two years, Jim's knowledge and passion for maintaining Yukon Valley's ecosystem made him the obvious choice to succeed the retiring warden. Nowadays, he spends most of his time flying between jobs across the reserve, dealing with both human problems and issues that could hurt the local wildlife. This busy lifestyle makes it difficult for him to spend time with his wife, or to visit his two daughters, who study in Anchorage.
translations.Kayla Johnson has been hunting big game: Kayla Johnson has been hunting big game since she was thirteen. Now that she is in her mid-twenties, she is a famous face in the hunting community, with a very popular hootube channel. Her success has also caused her to grow tired of hunting with modern-day techniques, so she continually challenges herself to hunt with limited supplies, often using just a bow. An undeniably competent hunter, but her ego can get out of control.
translations.Look, I don't like to go on about myself: Look, I don't like to go on about myself. Long story short: I was born and raised just west of the mountain range here under what you might deem rather unconventional circumstances, got my education out in the bush, and took over as park warden after my predecessor retired about twenty years ago, with a commitment to making this place a role model for conservation practices on the South Island. I live for korimako singing their noisy dawn chorus and wandering through the forest gathering plants for tea. I've a few vices, too: like Saturday evening rugby, and tall tales told around campfires. But mostly I'm just an ordinary Kiwi doing what she can for the nature she loves.
translations.Colton Locke, nicknamed \"Doc,\" is the:
Colton Locke, nicknamed "Doc," is the warden of the Layton Lake District reserve. He is a self-taught game warden, and has been a hunter all his life. Having grown up in the Pacific Northwest, he knows the region by heart, but has spent many years away working at other reserves, most recently the Evergreen Hunting Reserve. Now, he has returned to his roots in the Layton Lake District.

Doc loves to dig into hunting topics with anyone willing to lend their ear, and he is well-respected by the locals, even when he has a hard time keeping the peace with all of the reserve's personalities.
translations.My old man? You know him as \"Doc\", but:
My old man? You know him as "Doc", but his ID says Colton Locke. As you may remember, he's the Warden of the Layton Lake District reserve in the Pacific Northwest - that's where I was born and raised. Lovely place... He also used to lead the Evergreen Hunting Reserve before that, I don't know how he managed it all, plus raised me.

My Dad's getting older, but he's still quite fit... and stubborn as a mule, so I don't think he's about to retire any time soon. To me, it feels like he knows everything there is to know about hunting, and every nook and cranny in our reserve back home. 

He and I don't meet as often as we'd like: usually only during the holidays, since Thanksgiving is not the best time to take a longer vacation when you're a Warden... Anyway, years of nagging are finally paying off now, because he's coming to visit this year. He's not much of a talker on the phone, and he's terrible with tech, so here's hoping we'll go beyond small talk this time. Fingers crossed!
translations.Dr. Luna is, according to her grant subm: Dr. Luna is, according to her grant submission, “studying the varieties of medicinal plants found throughout Patagonia, building upon her research on the regional Mapuche-Tehuelche community and their traditions of therapeutic applications for local flora.” I provided a generous grant for Dr. Luna and her team to study the reserve and identify such medicinal plants, assess threats to those plants, and recommend measures to preserve them.
translations.My name is María del Carmen de la Rosa S:
My name is María del Carmen de la Rosa Solórzano, but please, call me María. Intisuyu is more than a reserve to me. It is a promise that the wildlife of Peru can still have a future if people are willing to care for it properly.

The Andes and the Amazon are home to extraordinary creatures. These animals lived here long before us, and I believe it is our responsibility to ensure they remain long after we are gone. 
And then there is Pablo, my capybara. He pretends to be very dignified, but he is secretly quite dramatic.

Some people find it strange that a hunting reserve speaks about conservation. But ethical hunting has long been part of the relationship between people and the land in the Andes. When done with respect, it helps preserve the delicate balance of nature.
translations.Matmat is an artist from Buenos Aires wh: Matmat is an artist from Buenos Aires who had his first gallery show at the tender age of 17. I met him there and since that first show, I’ve been his #1 patron. He simply has a style and an attention to quality that other artisans I’ve commissioned can’t match. Matmat specializes in taxidermy, leatherwork, and handcrafted jewelry made from sculpted bone. I’ve hired Matmat to decorate the Lodge and craft unique gift items for guests using local game.
translations.Maria Mboweni is a local Tsonga hunter a: Maria Mboweni is a local Tsonga hunter and leader of the Vurhonga Sustainable Hunters Coalition. She is a widow; her husband was a ranger at Vurhonga Savanna. He was shot on duty by poachers. Since his death, Maria has waged war on poachers by legally providing game to local markets at rock bottom prices. Her team of volunteers– two-thirds of them women – are the best and bravest hunters in the region, even assisting the police on raids against poacher gangs. She is a true hero.
translations.My father has been taking care of Cuatro: My father has been taking care of Cuatro Colinas for the last 35 years. When he first took over from my grandfather, he would work with my mother to ensure that Cuatro Colinas was not only a holiday destination for the wealthy, but accessible and safe for anyone who wanted to visit. Since my mother's passing, he has struggled to stay on top of his responsibilities, which is why I have taken over the day-to-day running of the reserve. I rarely see him nowadays, and he never leaves his wing of the Castillo.
translations.Beverly Parker has been herding reindeer: Beverly Parker has been herding reindeer across the Yukon for almost twenty years, having started when she was just 15. Bev is one of the toughest people I've ever met and is determined to uphold her culture's traditions, despite dropping populations of both people and wildlife in Alaska. I have established a working relationship with her, but I worry that my job as chief law officer puts me at odds with her independent nature. She doesn't like asking for assistance, but times are difficult for everyone in Alaska, and we should do what we can to help.
translations.I've been friends with Hank Pepper for w: I've been friends with Hank Pepper for well over a decade now. He's been teaching rookies and experienced hunters how to shoot for a long time, and his clients always leave great reviews. As much as he's a good teacher, he's an even better hunter, and he's not above a little friendly competition, now and then. He's bringing a lot of business and respectful visitors to Yukon Valley, so I owe him a favour or two.
translations.Robbo? He's the most passionate conserva:
Robbo? He's the most passionate conservationist and wildlife educator I've ever met! What I can tell you is that he found his calling watching Steve Irwin when he was a teenager - he even had a phase where he spoke like him!

After uni, he worked for zoos in Brisbane and other places for a few years, and that's where he met and fell in love with Lizzie. Can't wait for you to meet her, she's so kind and supportive. For Robbo and I, it wasn't easy to keep in touch during that time: there's only so much you can share with a friend if you never get to make new memories together.

When he was like 32 I think, his wife and he moved back here and took over his folks' old station. They worked so hard for years to make their dream a reality, and now it's a really lovely wildlife sanctuary. I gotta say, I'm so happy for him that he found a way to do what he loves for a living.

Now he just needs to find a way to do that AND not burn out.
translations.Sandy and I have been Yukon Valley's car: Sandy and I have been Yukon Valley's caretakers for eighteen years, now. She does a wonderful job as the reserve's resident education specialist, and she also supervises all of the research that takes place here. If she isn't traveling to some college to discuss our findings, she's taking a guided tour through the forests. Sandy's also great at putting on fun events for the locals where they can learn about the environment. It's an effective way to ensure the youngest generation appreciates how much help Alaska needs right now.
translations.Jonathan Trampfine has an unrivaled fasc:
Jonathan Trampfine has an unrivaled fascination with black bears. He has spent several years in the Layton Lake District living in proximity to the bear population. Doc has expressed concerns that Jonathan is endangering himself by trying to "befriend" the wild animals, but it has fallen on deaf ears. Instead, Jonathan attempts to document all of his close encounters and observations on film. He will never hunt his so-called "friends."

Trampfine and Richard Hope often clash over their views, as Trampfine believes Hope's survivalist methods are destroying nature rather than aiding it. So far, it has amounted to no more than a heated exchange of words across distant landscapes, but Doc worries things could escalate further.
translations.Marwin Tressler owns \"Star Hunting Tour:
Marwin Tressler owns "Star Hunting Tours" in Central Europe, which caters to clients looking for a premier boar hunting experience. Hirschfelden hosts a high population of wild boar that cause some damage to agriculture and forestry at times, but their reputation and valuable meat are very attractive to hunters, and has brought much business to Star Hunting Tours.

Tressler is an eccentric individual, and his thriving business has led him to butt heads with other landowners in the reserve, particularly with Robert Sommer. Tressler's hunting tours often carry over into Spreeberg, which is under Sommer's jurisdiction.

The situation escalated recently when Tressler and Sommer were found tussling with each other in a mudpile near Tressler's residence.
translations.Me? Well, I'm Trevor, I'm the Head Warde:
Me? Well, I'm Trevor, I'm the Head Warden here. Turning 40 next year (40!). I've worked for almost 20 years, ever since I left my native Layton Lake District. I was in this kind of rebellious phase, and I wanted to start over somewhere, "find my own path" or something. But at the end of the day, this was my calling as well.

I've been out in nature with my old man my whole life - hunting, fishing, hiking, camping, you name it. Never thought that like him, I'd be lucky enough to get paid to do what I love: protect nature and educate people.
In addition, I write popularization articles and videos, I've even given a couple of talks at conferences on hunting. Anything I can do to spread the word, really.

What else? I'm in a relationship; Sam and I have been together for 7 years, and we live in an old house that we're renovating almost from scratch (very demanding, not going to lie).
translations.Fiona Vualez works for the Pacific North: Fiona Vualez works for the Pacific Northwest Varmint Wildlife Control. There have been recent reports of coyote sightings in nearby towns to the reserve, and the townsfolk have grown increasingly anxious about encounters with them. Because peak hiking season is during the summers, Doc has enlisted the help of Vualez and her organization to thin out the coyote population. Their work is not yet finished though, and they often employ reserve hunters to aid in the effort, and provide both compensation and valuable insight on the coyote population in return.
translations.Remi Warren is an experienced guide, hun: Remi Warren is an experienced guide, hunter and social media personality who's been invited by Allan Bradley and the reserve board to do some solo hunting and film content in Silver Ridge Peaks. He's a confident and easygoing guy who loves nothing more than sharing his passion for hunting with fellow outdoor enthusiasts. Expect to hear from him out in the backcountry, whether you're stalking mule deer, calling turkeys, or just planning your next hunt.
translations.A fierce-looking canine tooth from a Eur: A fierce-looking canine tooth from a Eurasian cave lion.
translations.There are hundreds, well, thousands of y: There are hundreds, well, thousands of years of history in this place. It's been touched by everything from the sandals of Roman legionnaires to the treads of World War II tanks. Every year, new historical artifacts are found by people in the reserve. Perhaps you'll be lucky enough to find some of your own.
translations.Look at that, you found an historical ar: Look at that, you found an historical artifact! Now, according to local law it belongs to the state, but there is an arrangement where anyone submitting an authentic artifact will receive a finder's fee. That way, we can ensure it's preserved and put on display at a museum for others to appreciate our history.
translations.Look at that, you found a shed. I've alr: Look at that, you found a shed. I've already got a big enough collection back home, so I've started selling any new ones I find. People often buy them for handicrafts, you know, knife handles and such. I once sold a really nice moose antler for 500 bucks!
translations.The harvest is not taxidermized or saved:
The harvest is not taxidermized or saved.
The latest unsaved harvest can be saved later from the harvest manager
translations.You have reached the maximum number of s:
You have reached the maximum number of saved harvests.
You can overwrite or taxidermize an existing saved harvest to make space for this.
translations.Remember that your scent travels along t: Remember that your scent travels along the wind and can alert animals, even if they can't see or hear you. Look at the wind indicator in the compass and the sway of the plant life to find out which way the wind is blowing.
translations.You'll find the infamous crossroads wher: You'll find the infamous crossroads where legendary blues men supposedly sold their soul to the devil in exchange for mastery of the guitar here, at the intersection of some corn fields in the east. Not gonna lie, I think a lot of people were happier to buy into that mythology than admit that some poor Black kids from Nowheresville, Mississippi could be just *that* good. Of course, the musicians themselves were happy to indulge them. Anyway, we get a lot of tourism here in the late summer, even though there isn't so much as a sign left. And who knows - maybe the devil offers mastery of the rifle too? Only one way to find out!
translations.The name of this area derives from a Cho: The name of this area derives from a Choctaw word meaning "cotton", and unsurprisingly, that crop dominates. Cotton's no longer king here, and agriculture as a whole only makes up a tiny fraction of Mississippi's gross product, but the cotton crop is still around 475,000 acres every year, and Magnolia Farms is one of the largest cotton producers in the state. That's a lot of people's livelihoods we have to consider...
translations.I have zero idea who Felton is (was?) Ma: I have zero idea who Felton is (was?) Maybe it's just a bad pun? They call the adjoining forest Felton Woods, so I could be on to something. Anyway, logging used to be big business here. Loblolly pines grow super rapidly and tolerate a lot of different biomes. Unfortunately there's a glut of supply in the South, and a lot of timber businesses in Mississippi Acres have had to close recently.
translations.Half Hills, half Delta, all crazy - and: Half Hills, half Delta, all crazy - and these are those hills. I'm sure you've seen taller, but you won't find a better spot for hunting whitetail or black bear south of the Mason-Dixon line. This is where the Big Game Club members hang out when they're not sipping sweet tea in their lodge.
translations.This is where all those slow, stagnant t: This is where all those slow, stagnant tributaries meet the mighty Mississippi. The bayou here is a great place to hunt alligator, but you'd better bring some rubber boots. If you'd rather not get your feet wet, you can find black bear and whitetail hiding in the hickory forests to the north.
translations.The abandoned paper mill in the eastern: The abandoned paper mill in the eastern part of this region's a little eerie, especially at night. Well, I say abandoned... I sometimes see cars driving in and out, so I guess there's some life in it yet. Along the horseshoe bend itself you'll find some of the most fertile land the preserve has to offer.
translations.The ultimate in transportable camouflage:
The ultimate in transportable camouflage concealment. Designed for waterfowl hunting, this blind provides excellent visual reduction while providing an unrestricted view of the sky.

Notable features include the ability to be deployed almost anywhere and decreased visibility.
translations.Deploy these decoys at lake shorelines t: Deploy these decoys at lake shorelines to increase the chance of flying wood duck landing nearby. Deploying multiple decoys will increase the probability of birds landing. The effect of multiple decoys in the same area stacks up to a max of 20 decoys. Best used in conjunction with the WOOD DUCK CALLER
translations.A versatile instrument, this beautiful w: A versatile instrument, this beautiful wooden caller can authentically replicate a large host of bean goose vocalizations. The caller will help grab the attention of flying bean geese when used in feeding fields and along shorelines. Geese are more likely to land when this caller is used in conjunction with the appropriate decoys.
translations.This short reed Canada goose caller was: This short reed Canada goose caller was handcrafted by CMS Sweden’s master craftsman, Charlie Sandin. A complex and versatile instrument, this caller can authentically replicate a large host of Canada goose vocalizations. The short reed caller is useful for both short and long ranges and will help grab the attention of flying Canada geese when used in feeding fields, such as farmlands.
translations.This deer caller generates an authentic:
This deer caller generates an authentic bleat of a doe in estrus every time it is turned. Simple to use, and irresistible to any nearby bucks and does.

The bleat call has a low range, but a high chance of attraction.
translations.Rich and natural sounding, this deer cal:
Rich and natural sounding, this deer caller will pique the curiosity of any dominant buck or amorous doe nearby, and draw them into your line of fire.

The grunt call has a high range, but a low chance of attraction.
translations.This acrylic duck caller produces a powe:
This acrylic duck caller produces a powerful long range call and easily cuts through high winds and rain. 

Use this caller near lake shorelines to grab the attention of flying ducks and increase the probability of them landing nearby. Ducks are more likely to land when this caller is used in conjunction with the appropriate decoys.
translations.This high quality duck caller can reprod:
This high quality duck caller can reproduce the calls of the eurasian teal. 

Use this caller near lake shorelines to grab the attention of flying eaurasian teals and increase the probability of them landing nearby. Ducks are more likely to land when this caller is used in conjunction with the appropriate decoys.
translations.This high quality duck caller can accura:
This high quality duck caller can accurately reproduce the calls of the eurasian wigeon. 

Use this caller near lake shorelines to grab the attention of flying wigeons and increase the probability of them landing nearby. Ducks are more likely to land when this caller is used in conjunction with the appropriate decoys.
translations.This high quality duck caller can reprod:
This high quality duck caller can reproduce the calls of the gadwall. 

Use this caller near lake shorelines to grab the attention of flying gadwalls and increase the probability of them landing nearby. Ducks are more likely to land when this caller is used in conjunction with the appropriate decoys.
translations.A versatile instrument, this handcrafted: A versatile instrument, this handcrafted wooden caller can authentically replicate a large host of greylag goose vocalizations. The caller will help grab the attention of flying greylag geese when used in feeding fields and along shorelines. Geese are more likely to land when this caller is used in conjunction with the appropriate decoys.
translations.The DELUXE Magpie Goose Caller is design: The DELUXE Magpie Goose Caller is designed for both short- and long-range calling, which makes it the perfect fit to lure in Magpie Geese as they fly from feeding fields. With this trusty tool by your side, you can expand your options and simply focus on the hunt.
translations.This high quality duck caller can reprod:
This high quality duck caller can reproduce the calls of the northern pintail. 

Use this caller near lake shorelines to grab the attention of flying northern pintails and increase the probability of them landing nearby. Ducks are more likely to land when this caller is used in conjunction with the appropriate decoys.
translations.When you're out there on the hunt, you n: When you're out there on the hunt, you need something that draws them in, not just catches their attention—this call does exactly that. Perfect for feeding fields and shorelines, this call works best when paired with the right decoys, ensuring those flying snow geese can’t resist landing right where you need them.
translations.This high quality duck caller can reprod:
This high quality duck caller can reproduce the calls of the wood duck. 

Use this caller near lake shorelines to grab the attention of flying wood ducks and increase the probability of them landing nearby. Ducks are more likely to land when this caller is used in conjunction with the appropriate decoys.
translations.The blacktail unisex urine instantly att:
The blacktail unisex urine instantly attracts any blacktail deer in and around your area. Fire out a couple of puffs and wait. Scents last longer than calls, so it's a great choice for lure hunting.

Effective range depends on wind condition. High wind speeds create narrow and long scent cone while low wind speeds create wide and short cone.
translations.99.8% pure Roosevelt elk urine, in a spr:
99.8% pure Roosevelt elk urine, in a spray can. Guaranteed to attract both genders. Since scents last longer than calls, this is a great choice when lure hunting.

The effective range depends on current wind conditions, with high wind speeds leading to a narrow and long scent cone, while low wind speeds create a wide and short cone.
translations.Irresistible scent that can be used to a:
Irresistible scent that can be used to attract both moose bulls and cows. Since scents last longer than calls, this is a great choice when lure hunting.

The effective range depends on current wind conditions, with high wind speeds leading to a narrow and long scent cone, while low wind speeds create a wide and short cone.
translations.Use this mule deer urine to attract mule:
Use this mule deer urine to attract mule deers during the rut. Fire out a couple of puffs, and wait for them to stop by. Since scents last longer than calls, this is a great choice when lure hunting.

The effective range depends on current wind conditions, with high wind speeds leading to a narrow and long scent cone, while low wind speeds create a wide and short cone.
translations.Lure the red deer to you using this spec:
Lure the red deer to you using this specialized scent spray. Since scents last longer than calls, this is a great choice when lure hunting.

The effective range depends on current wind conditions, with high wind speeds leading to a narrow and long scent cone, while low wind speeds create a wide and short cone.
translations.Strong scent that can be used to attract:
Strong scent that can be used to attract both roe deer bucks and does. Since scents last longer than calls, this is a great choice when lure hunting.

The effective range depends on current wind conditions, with high wind speeds leading to a narrow and long scent cone, while low wind speeds create a wide and short cone..
translations.Potent scent that can be used to attract:
Potent scent that can be used to attract Siberian musk deer of both genders. Since scents last longer than calls, this is a great choice when lure hunting.

The effective range depends on current wind conditions, with high wind speeds leading to a narrow and long scent cone, while low wind speeds create a wide and short cone.
translations.The whitetail unisex urine is an instant:
The whitetail unisex urine is an instant attractor to any whitetail deer in and around your hunting area. Fire out a couple of puffs, and wait for the whitetails to stop by. Since scents last longer than calls, this is a great choice when lure hunting.

The effective range depends on current wind conditions, with high wind speeds leading to a narrow and long scent cone, while low wind speeds create a wide and short cone.
translations.Lure nearby wild boars with this particu:
Lure nearby wild boars with this particular scent spray. Since scents last longer than calls, this is a great choice when lure hunting.

The effective range depends on current wind conditions, with high wind speeds leading to a narrow and long scent cone, while low wind speeds create a wide and short cone.
translations.This compact camera is perfect for snapp: This compact camera is perfect for snapping pictures of nature. Its small size and excellent weatherproofing mean it can tough it out in the rain and mud, and with 5x zoom, you'll always be able to capture sharp, lifelike photos.
translations.The FOXPRO X360 high-tech remote electro:
The FOXPRO X360 high-tech remote electronic caller offers unparalleled flexibility to avid ambush hunters. It comes with an expansive bank of recorded calls to attract any callable species, while the remote control allows the user to operate it from an advantageous shooting position up to {d:200} away. 

Its FOXFUSION functionality allows hunters to attract two different animals at once. Hunters can also enable its FOXBANG option to make the caller stop playing calls after perceiving a gunshot.
translations.Lock onto targets with unmatched accurac: Lock onto targets with unmatched accuracy. Its 33mm objective lens offers excellent brightness, clarity, and lasting durability. Specially engineered for getting quick target acquisition. This scope can be used on both handguns and shotguns!
translations.This sight helps hunters overcome the bi: This sight helps hunters overcome the biggest challenge when bow-hunting: distance estimation. With the press of a button {KENNEL_RENAME}, the Brightsight Rangefinder Bow Sight calculates the distance of the target and projects a precise, virtual LED pin that is only visible to the archer, without the clutter of multiple physical pins.
translations.The Marksman Exakt is the sight of choic: The Marksman Exakt is the sight of choice for medium and close-range hunts where success hinges on lightning fast reflexes and pinpoint marksmanship. This precision-crafted reflex sight is waterproof, fog-proof and built to withstand incredible recoil.
translations.A modified version of the Marksman Exact: A modified version of the Marksman Exact reflex sight, tailor-made to fit Davani semi-automatic pistols. It is the sight of choice for medium and close-range hunts where success hinges on lightning fast reflexes and pinpoint marksmanship. This precision-crafted reflex sight is waterproof, fog-proof and built to withstand incredible recoil.
translations.A highly durable, robust sight that prov: A highly durable, robust sight that provides an unlimited field of view. This red dot sight is 100% parallax-free, which allows for extremely fast target acquisition without losing awareness of peripheral action. This makes it the perfect choice for anyone serious about flushing and driven hunts.
translations.Quickly dial in your shots from a distan: Quickly dial in your shots from a distance with this premium, custom-made scope for the GRELCK DRILLING RIFLE. Weatherproof and built to withstand shot after shot of high-powered cartridges and shells, this scope covers has you covered for most hunting situations.
translations.Featuring a high-quality image intensifi: Featuring a high-quality image intensifier tube, a compact design and waterproof battery compartment, the GenZero 1-4x20 Night Vision Rifle Scope will allow you to see beyond the expected in night-time conditions. A long-range IR illuminator completes the package allowing you to acquire your targets from safe distances; but be aware that the effectiveness of this technology is particularly affected by fog and adverse weather conditions.
translations.An expertly crafted scope that makes slu: An expertly crafted scope that makes slug hunting easier when fitted on any single-barreled shotgun. This 5" eye relief is ideal for hard-hitting slugs, while the fully multi-coated lenses provide excellent light transmission and low-light performance.
translations.A recommendation of what size of animal: A recommendation of what size of animal this ammunition is best suited for. This is a balance between the ethical need to kill the animal as quickly as possible to minimize suffering and the need to prevent unnecessary destruction of flesh. In the harvest screen, these factors are illustrated by the trophy integrity and quick kill bonus.
translations.The width of the light cone generated by: The width of the light cone generated by this light device. This affects the area in which clues are highlighted at night.
translations.The average range at which this scent ha: The average range at which this scent has a chance to attract animals. Scent radius is affected by the wind speed and direction. High wind speeds create a narrow and long scent cone, while low wind speeds lead to a wide and short cone.
translations.The length of time a scent lure is activ: The length of time a scent lure is active and has a chance to attract animals after being used.
translations.The length of time that scent is conceal: The length of time that scent is concealed after the scent eliminator has been applied.
translations.The amount of scent concealed after the: The amount of scent concealed after the scent eliminator has been applied.
translations.Projectile trajectories are affected by: Projectile trajectories are affected by gravity, but sights can be configured to compensate for this, so that the target is hit when the sight is centered on it from a particular distance. This is called the zero distance. If a projectile is fired closer or farther away from this distance, the shooter needs to compensate for bullet drop by either aiming below (closer than zero distance) or above (farther away than zero distance) the target.

A big double that demands respect from even the most skilled hunters, the King 470DB lives up to its name in stature, efficiency, as well as cost. With enough firepower to instantly take down nearly any animal, the King is designed to give hunters a fighting chance when pit against animals that wouldn’t be phased by more traditional ammunition. Quick to load up, incredibly powerful and double-barreled to even out any hunter’s odds in the perilous African wilderness.
translations.Contemporary bow-making techniques and f: Contemporary bow-making techniques and flexible but sturdy materials make this stunning take on an ancient self bow effective even for modern hunters. A single stave of hickory and bowstring combine to form a silent but deadly weapon that epitomizes the resourcefulness of the peoples who used it to conquer prey.

translations.AVALANCHE STUDIOS GROUP AB – PRIVACY POL:
AVALANCHE STUDIOS GROUP AB – PRIVACY POLICY
Last updated on: April 8th, 2025
1. INTRODUCTION
Who are we?
Hello! We’re Avalanche Studios Group. If the name rings a bell, it may be from high-octane AAA action games where stuff blows up left and right, like Just Cause and Mad Max. Maybe you’ve just discovered the equally explosion-laden gem that is Generation Zero. Or, you’re more of an outdoorsy type, in which case you’re probably more familiar with theHunter: Call of the Wild and Call of the Wild: The Angler. Either way, thanks for exploring those massive open worlds with us!

We take player privacy and security very seriously. And no wonder, because it’s the bedrock for all the fun stuff we build on top. It’s also exactly what we’ll discuss below. So if you’re anything like us (and our lawyers,) you’re surely chomping at the bit to get started!
But before we get into the nitty-gritty, a few details for the record. Regarding Personal Data collected and processed under this Privacy Policy, Avalanche Studios Group AB (corporate identity number 556675-1748) is the data controller. Our registered address is Box 11238, 100 61 Stockholm.
What’s a Privacy Policy exactly?
We’ve already mentioned that your privacy matters to us, but how does this Privacy Policy help ensure it?

Personal Data is any information that can identify an individual, directly or indirectly. This could be your name, location, or online identifiers (like IP address, web browser version, that sort of thing). The purpose of this document, then, is to help you make sense of how we collect, store, use, transfer, or disclose your Personal Data.
This Privacy Policy applies to the video games we bring you as the player. It also applies to related services such as our customer service, our websites and the Avalanche Apex Connect service. We’ll call these games and services “Properties” throughout this document.
Ready to proceed to level 2? Sorry, chapter 2. Just one more thing. We

3. THE DATA WE COLLECT AND USE
Below, we describe the Personal Data we collect and how we collect it. Furthermore we set out the reasons we process your Personal Data (the purpose of processing) and the legal basis for our processing.

3.1	The Personal Data we collect from you
a. We collect Identity Data. This includes your names, usernames, or similar identifiers as well as your titles and preferred genders.
b. We collect Contact Data. This includes your home address, email address, phone number and other data you provide Expansive Worlds with for the purpose of enabling contact.
c. We collect Transaction Data. This includes Details about payments you have made in or in association with the Properties and other details of products and services you have accessed or used throughout the Properties as well as purchases or orders made by you. We do not process or store any credit or debit card information or details on our servers. Such payments and information are processed by our trusted third parties on their payments servers and their privacy policy applies.
d. We collect Technical Data. This includes your internet protocol (IP) address, your login data, browser type and version, hardware information, time zone setting and location, browser plug-in types and versions, operating system and other technology on the device you use to access the Properties or communicate with us. In cases of the Properties malfunctioning on your device, technical data may also include specific device information, such as the location of the file on your device.
e. We collect Profile Data. This includes your username, password, preferences, feedback and survey responses.
f. We collect Usage Data. This includes information about how you use the Properties, such as time spent playing and which games.
g. We collect Marketing and Communication Data. This includes your preferences in receiving marketing and communications from us and our third-party partners.

translations.8. CHILDREN\nThe Properties are not dire:
8. CHILDREN
The Properties are not directed to children under the age of 16. We do not knowingly collect Personal Data from children under 16 years old in the Properties or in connection therewith. If you are under 16 years, please do not use or access the Properties. 
We believe it is important to safeguard the privacy of children and encourage parents to regularly monitor their children’s use of online activities. If you are a parent and believe that your child under the age of 16 has accessed and/or used the Properties and provided Personal Data to us, please contact us through the mailing address at the end of this Privacy Policy and we will work to delete that account and any such personally identifiable information.
If we learn that we have collected and processed Personal Data of a child under the age of 16 years, we will take reasonable steps to ensure the erasure of the Personal Data from our systems. This may require us to delete the child’s account to the Properties.

9. HOW TO CONTACT US
If you have any questions, complaints or comments regarding how we process your Personal Data or our Privacy Policy, please contact us at:
