translations.We care deeply about your right to priva: We care deeply about your right to privacy and want you to know why we are collecting your data and how we use it. We collect crash report data to ensure quality and to improve the gameplay experience for all users. To help support our game, we ask for your optional consent to the collection of your crash report data.
translations.This shelter can be used to rest and wak:
This shelter can be used to rest and wake up at a specific time by adjusting the alarm clock. 

The cost for resting increases with each use temporarily, but is eventually reset after a period of time.
translations.Tapionvuori contains the highest mountai: Tapionvuori contains the highest mountains in Revontuli Coast. It is named after Tapio the forest god in Finnish mythology. Hunters used to pray to him before and after the hunt. If you can't find the diamond you are looking for it might be time to pay your respect to Tapio.
translations.The hills of Koittomäet are known to man: The hills of Koittomäet are known to many travelers as the last round in the fight against mosquitoes. The region hosts swarms of mosquitoes but is therefore also known for the many species of animals that eat insects. The well-prepared hunter can use this to his advantage.
translations.The Korpimaa region is filled with mires: The Korpimaa region is filled with mires and lakes flanked by conifer trees. Hunters should remind themselves to pack heavy duty boots and an extra pair of socks if they plan on hunting in this region. While laughed at, losing a boot or a shoe is a common occurrence.
translations.The central region of Revontuli Coast is: The central region of Revontuli Coast is known for its large lakes and the main camping ground. Fishermen all over the world travel to these lakes to try their luck. Whether you are a fisherman or a hunter, Tyynijärvet is a great place to start your excursion.
translations.The ravines and striking landscape of Ty: The ravines and striking landscape of Tyynirotko is a reminder of the impact the last ice age had on Finland. Even the astute hunter will need to stay focused as the ravines create a natural echo chamber making it extremely difficult to locate the source of a call.
translations.Campers and hunters alike enjoy Sumulaht: Campers and hunters alike enjoy Sumulahti or "Fog Bay'' for its picturesque lakes and unique land formations. Every hunter that visits this region has their own favorite hunting spot to hunt waterfowl.
translations.Salzwiesen is the uncut gem of North Ger: Salzwiesen is the uncut gem of North Germany, and pound-for-pound possibly the best waterfowl hunting reserve in the entire world. You can expect to find the elusive Red Fox, the wily Ring-Necked Pheasant, and all manner of ducks and game fowl, here and ripe for the plucking. A highlight of this particular area is a clay pigeon shooting range which you can use to hone your skills.
translations.Port Whisky is a historic fishing villag: Port Whisky is a historic fishing village, still boasting a baby's handful of inhabitants actively working the water. They were originally responsible for feeding the township, however have been known to smuggle contraband into the estate since, including whisky ran from the Isle of Man and beyond the Hebrides.
translations.The Piper's Pit is the mouth of an under:
The Piper's Pit is the mouth of an underground tunnel network spanning the depths of Tòrr nan Sìthean. 

It was likely used by Rodney Roan as an escape route, providing him with an opportunity to flee the conflagration of Caisteal an Eilein, however in more recent times it has gained infamy for those who cannot leave. 

Legend says a little boy was tasked to march through the passage playing his pipes, and those above ground would chart his course based on the sound. Progress continued until nightfall, and as the full moon rose in the sky, the warbling of his pipes faded. Neither dog nor man could find a trace of the boy. When the moon is high, and as full as that final night, his defiant warbling can be heard once more.
translations.The Future Heritage Forest is the latest: The Future Heritage Forest is the latest victory in a string of efforts aiming to restore ancient rainforest to Scottish soil. Before evictions and clearances punctured the highlands, this area was chock-full of many such sacred sites; Oak, Birch and Hazel raising their hands to the heavens, basking in the warmth of a friend they've known since birth.
translations.The Standing Stones are an extraordinary: The Standing Stones are an extraordinary cross-shaped setting of menhirs erected over 5000 years ago, predating the English Stonehenge monument. It's hard to divine their original purpose, but they make a perfect stargazing platform for the moon skimming low over the hills.
translations.Ceum a Deas is the southern part of the: Ceum a Deas is the southern part of the central hill ridgeline, with a slight lower elevation than the north central sub-region.
translations.Do you want to grant Avalanche Studios t: Do you want to grant Avalanche Studios the permission to gather anonymous gameplay data to improve the quality of the game in future updates? You can enable or disable anonymous data gathering at any time through the privacy option in the settings menu.
translations.Disabling Social Features will disable a:
Disabling Social Features will disable all multiplayer features in the Trophy Lodge! Upon disabling Social Features, you can no longer visit other players' trophy lodges, your friends and lobby visitors can no longer visit your lodge, your trophy lodge data will no longer be saved on the cloud, and you will lose access to Challenges!

Are you sure you wish to disable Social Features?
translations.The privacy policy has been updated. Do: The privacy policy has been updated. Do you want to grant Avalanche Studios the permission to gather anonymous gameplay data to improve the quality of the game in future updates? You can enable or disable anonymous data gathering at any time through the privacy option in the settings menu.

The privacy policy has been updated. Do you want to enable Social Features? It allows you to participate in events, competitions and more! It enables Avalanche Studios to track your in-game actions and achievements in order to calculate rewards, tailor individualized messaging, and more to create a customized experience. Social Features can be enabled or disabled at any time through the settings menu.
translations.The Labrador Retriever is a breed of dog: The Labrador Retriever is a breed of dog known for its friendly and playful demeanor. It has excellent temperament as a companion dog as well as excellent capabilities as a hunting dog. Its readiness to follow orders and soft mouth makes it superior at carrying and retrieving game. It also has webbed paws making it a strong swimmer. The Labrador Retriever can retrieve Class 1 animals.
translations.The Tony Coal Mine is famous for trigger: The Tony Coal Mine is famous for triggering a considerable landslide, a result of settlers digging too greedily and too deep, despite multiple warnings from native residents. The town was originally named after the chief prospector's dog, Tony, their most precious family member and a prominent survivor of the disaster.
translations.The central Amisk Lodge and Tea House si: The central Amisk Lodge and Tea House sits upon Le Lac des Rêves, a still and mystical lake bordering on the serene. The tea house was originally created as a refuge for hikers, in collaboration with the local Métis nation, and remains a welcome refuge from the harsh winter without.
translations.This Cosmic Ray mapping station was buil: This Cosmic Ray mapping station was built in a cluster of 10 other stations across Canada, however has been granted the greatest cultural cache of the bunch, due to its high elevation allowing it to capture more data than any other. It was eventually decommissioned, however the site was preserved and granted local landmark status.
translations.Peculiar rock formations and granite bou: Peculiar rock formations and granite boulders balancing precariously above the forest canopy is a strange but common sight in this region. Enjoy a walk through the area as you enjoy otherworldly rock formations created by millions of years of natural landscaping.
translations.Part of the heritage left by British cul: Part of the heritage left by British culture is tea drinking and tea consumption is part of everyday life in Australia. Although the tea production is comparably small - tea fields can still be found in Australia.
translations.Standing at {d:250} high, Stonefather Pe: Standing at {d:250} high, Stonefather Peak has an imposing presence in the area. While formidable and intimidating to us humans, a great amount of animals and insects make its cracks and crevices their home.
translations.Mount Matron is the highest volcanic plu:
Mount Matron is the highest volcanic plug in the region; created as magma hardened within the vents when she was an active volcano.
Although she has a volcanic past, today she is mostly known for her comforting characteristics in keeping a comforting eye on the animals and people that seek refuge in her shade.
translations.The Triplets are an iconic mountain form: The Triplets are an iconic mountain formation that people all over the region travel to. The outcrop is famous both because of the numerous picturesque hiking trails around its base but also because it gives the impression of three siblings standing forever watching the horizon.
translations.Ernsdorf Cave is situated in the western: Ernsdorf Cave is situated in the western part of the reserve and should not be entered by just any curious amateur. Spelunkers are fascinated by its deep and dark tunnels inhabited by, amongst other animals, the olm or proteus that are usually found in more southern parts of Europe.
translations.Troll's Crack is one of the marks the la: Troll's Crack is one of the marks the last Ice Age left on Finland as it carved its way through the landscape. This wondrous natural phenomenon creates an interesting effect as sound bounces of the walls and echoes. The astute listener can pickup every sound the forest makes from this landmark.
translations.The Routakivi is a 16 m high glacial err: The Routakivi is a 16 m high glacial erratic. A glacial erratic is a rock that differs from the native rock in the area. They get their names because they have been carried by glacial ice, sometimes across hundreds of kilometers. Routakivi is one of Revontuli Coast's largest glacial erratics.
translations.A 1,200 km long line of defense is what:
A 1,200 km long line of defense is what Finnish commanders planned as the tension between itself and its giant neighbour was at an all time high. The threat of Soviet invasion called for the largest construction in Finland's history. The construction included field fortifications, bunkers, trenches, fueling stations, weapon depots and more. Today, The Bunkers are visited by tourist and those interested in war history. 

These fortifications are now battling nature, a battle The Bunkers can't win.
translations.Rock formations in the area create a uni: Rock formations in the area create a unique geological landscape. The major rock faces are composed of welded tuff, or compressed volcanic ash.
translations.The old Northern Pacific Railway crosses: The old Northern Pacific Railway crosses the landscape along the Layton Lake shoreline. This was the main source of transportation during the second half of the 19th century, and forever changed and expanded the possibilities of long-distance traveling. The railroad went out of operation in 1970.
translations.Located in the higher reaches of the Pur:
Located in the higher reaches of the Purbi Pahad region, this natural cave has filled the Nepali people with wonder for centuries - and now amazes tourists as well.
In Nepali, "Him" is short for "snow/mountain" and "gufa" means "cave".
translations.Ban Gufa is a natural cave located in th:
Ban Gufa is a natural cave located in the Paschima Ban region, in the Terai. Although it has now also become a famous tourist attraction, the cave and the shrine in it have been a sacred site for Hindus, Kirati and Buddhists alike, and is an important pilgrimage site in Eastern Nepal.
In Nepali, "Ban" means "forest" and "gufa" means "cave".
translations.Jhulunge Pul (literally meaning \"hangin: Jhulunge Pul (literally meaning "hanging bridge") is one of the longest of its kind in Eastern Nepal. Historically, the Pahad's deep valleys and mountains have deeply shaped the numerous cultures that have developed there; even in modern times, drivable roads are not always possible, a hanging bridge can sometimes be the only connection to some hard-to-access areas.
translations.Hindu shrines are a key landmark in the: Hindu shrines are a key landmark in the Nepali landscape and are usually located near the village centers. They are normally named after the god that is in it, and usually feature a ghanta, a prayer bell that the devotee rings in order to let the deity know they have arrived.
translations.\"Him Taal\" (literally meaning \"a lake: "Him Taal" (literally meaning "a lake in the mountains") is located in the far reaches of Chauri Himal, and is not easy to access, due to the absence of roads. However, finally seeing the panorama makes the long hike worthwhile for both pilgrims and tourists.
translations.Culminating at 6,785 m, Swargadwar Himal: Culminating at 6,785 m, Swargadwar Himal is part of the Himalayas, and is the highest peak in the Sundarpatan region. Its name means "Gateway to heaven".
translations.Besi Khola, or the Besi River, is a larg: Besi Khola, or the Besi River, is a large but shallow river that irrigates most of the southern parts of the Sundarpatan Hunting Reserve. It plays a key role in agriculture, and has supported the lives of farmers and livestock herders for centuries.
translations.In Buddhism, stupas are structures that: In Buddhism, stupas are structures that sometimes contain relics and have been used for meditation and commemoration. To tourists, even smaller stupas can be well-known landmarks in the Himal region.
translations.Tunnel farming is a common sight in Tera: Tunnel farming is a common sight in Terai; the so-called "veggie tunnels" are simple tubular-shaped greenhouses that offer protection to vegetation in all seasons, and allows farmers to drastically improve their yields and also grow plants off-season. It has been an important tool in increasing the local community's income and improving their living standards.
translations.The Smith Scenic Railroad is a heritage:
The Smith Scenic Railroad is a heritage railroad passing through the southern lowlands of the reserve. It still uses the original vintage locomotive and cars, and is one of New England's most beloved tourist attractions.

It's named after its founder, a former employee of the local railway company who purchased a section of the railroad slated for abandonment in the 1960s.
translations.Located deep in the Greeley Wilderness A:
Located deep in the Greeley Wilderness Area, Tocqueville Cave is a bit of a hidden gem. This open-pit mine goes all the way through the ridge, with one of its entrances leading into Edward Ravine.

It was first operated commercially during the Industrial Revolution, then was opened to the public from the 1960s until the 2010s. During those years, it was not uncommon to cross paths with couples or children with a hammer and a few minerals in their hands.

The mineral deposits found in its tunnels are thought to be around 350 to 400 million years old. A wide variety of minerals have been unearthed here, primarily mica, but also quartz, amethyst, feldspar and beryl.
translations.Located in the gorgeous Retz Notch, the:
Located in the gorgeous Retz Notch, the "Old Toad" is one of the many glacial erratics scattered across New England. Unlike other similar rock formations, it's still preserved in its original state, in large part thanks to the efforts of the reserve's "croo" to prevent any vandalism.

The current consensus among geologists is that the modest present-day Retz Brook used to be a glacier around 20,000 years ago, carrying boulders like this one over massive distances.
translations.Pumpkin fields are a favorite among visi:
Pumpkin fields are a favorite among visitors to New England, especially around harvest time (between the end of August and the end of October).

Once they turn from green to orange, pumpkins are considered ripe; it's then recommended to pick them to allow other pumpkins to grow on the same vine. If stored in the right conditions and inspected regularly for signs of rot, pumpkins can have a shelf life of a few months.
translations.The Conway Pond Trail is a beautiful nat:
The Conway Pond Trail is a beautiful natural site nested in the foothills of Champney Ridge, not far from Mount Alcott. Its high walls are made of Conway granite, a type of granite found in abundance in the New England Mountains reserve. 

After its re-discovery in the nineteenth century, it became a very popular natural site, which eventually started causing damage to it. Access to Conway Pond is now restricted to paid visitors for only a few months each year.
translations.The Favreau Boulder is a massive granite:
The Favreau Boulder is a massive granite rock preserved in the New England Mountains reserve, known as a "glacial erratic". 
At an estimated 4,500 tons, it's one of the largest in the United States. It's even larger than it appears, with roughly one third of its mass being buried underground.

Glacial erratics (from the Latin verb "errare", "to wander") are defined as rocks that have been carried by glacial ice over large distances (sometimes hundreds of miles). Their size can vary greatly, from small pebbles to huge boulders, and have among others helped geologists better understand the last glacial retreat in prehistoric times.
translations.Norden was the main region for mining du: Norden was the main region for mining during the early 20th century. Although active mining shut down in the 1930s, the remains of the operations can still be seen.
translations.Along the southwestern path of the reser: Along the southwestern path of the reserve, you can find the opening to Rinderland gorge. It stretches into the mountainous area of Rinderland, and is a great starting point for hikers that want to continue west towards the Bürgen area.
translations.The Soil Kliffs are one of the most impo: The Soil Kliffs are one of the most important geological monuments in all of Germany, stretching for almost 2 km around the North-Eastern Coast. The Kliff is comprised of a number of layers of different soil, including 5-7 million-year-old Glimmerton, which includes fossils such as snails, mussels and crabs; 4-5 million-year-old Limonite; and 2-3 million-year-old Kaolin sand deposits from Scandinavia containing fossilized corals, sea lilies and sponges. Despite the many historical attempts to mine the Kliffs, they have been a nature preserve since 1923.
translations.Germany is among the global leaders in W: Germany is among the global leaders in Wind Power, and Schleswig-Holstein is one of its most prolific regions, generating more power than it consumes. The region contains a number of wind energy plants and offshore wind farms.
translations.Тусида or \"Without fire.\" The Nenets r: Тусида or "Without fire." The Nenets regard the ground itself as sacred, which is why we don't allow digging or blasting on the expedition. This whole region is our hallowed ground. Conduct yourself accordingly.
translations.Old Чекуровской or \"Chekurovka\" is a f: Old Чекуровской or "Chekurovka" is a fishing village that was once occupied by Russian allies to the Nenets. These peasant fishermen were displaced by larger fishing operations long ago, leaving this village a ghost town. Still a good fishing spot for those who enjoy their solitude.
translations.Чучуна or \"Chuchunya.\" Locals -- Nenet: Чучуна or "Chuchunya." Locals -- Nenets and Russians -- claim that before the fishermen left, near Chekurovka, there was a big, hairy Chuchunya stealing all the fish. Harassing the reindeer. Finally eating one. 30 years later, a team of hunters claim they shot this very Chuchunya, but it escaped to the river. Its body was never recovered. Hoax or fact? I am inclined to be skeptical.
translations.Пустотелая гора is the \"Hollowed Mounta: Пустотелая гора is the "Hollowed Mountain," named for the many caves its steep climb hosts. Hunters have died here trying to take on the brown bear. And there are persistent rumors of this "Chuchunya" creature. Sane people keep out of this territory.
translations.CAVE WARNING Area Caves Contain Historic: CAVE WARNING Area Caves Contain Historically Significant Native Artwork. Those Who Dare Deface or 'Graffiti' These Sites Will Be Subject to the Maximum Penalty of 30 Years in Prison.
translations.The sabertooth tigers would have compete: The sabertooth tigers would have competed with these men for cave real estate. The early humans respected their competitors. If they claimed an animal's life, even a vicious predator, they made use of it in every way, wasting not one bit of gristle or fur.
translations.Spreeberg Castle is possibly the reserve: Spreeberg Castle is possibly the reserve's most famous landmark situated on the eastern side of Spreeberg Lake at the center of the reserve. The castle was the seat of the lords of Königsberg. It appears to be first mentioned in sources, indirectly, beginning in 1225.

translations.Amukelani was a sangoma -- a spiritual h: Amukelani was a sangoma -- a spiritual healer, and a friend of mine. She is the one who told me that you had Noyi blood. Amukelani used this hut regularly for a few decades. She brought people here for treatment. A private retreat, especially for people who were burdened by devils. Here, Amukelani said she could set the devils free without hurting anyone else. I asked her where the devils went wfter she set them free in the forest. She looked me in the eye, dead serious, and said, "They're still here." Then she giggled, having fun with me, and saying not to worry, this forest could take care of itself. But still, I always wonder if there was some truth to what she said...
translations.Uncle Rhangani loved to come up here, wh: Uncle Rhangani loved to come up here, where nobody would bother him. I do not share his affinity for the Plateau, but this being his favorite place, we named it for him when he died. It was a cape buffalo that killed him, you know? He was guiding some guests on a hike and they came across two large bulls. No big deal, but one of the guests freaks out, starts threatening them -- and the bulls charge. Rhangani saved that guest from the first bull. Shot it with his rifle. He had legendary skills, like you and me. But the second bull struck him hard, leaving Rhangani broken and bleeding. At the hospital, Rhangani didn't blame the buffalo for what happened. He said he felt remorse for having to kill one under those circumstances. He was wounded beyond repair, so after slipping in and out for a night, he joined our ancestors. Here, I remember him and the things he taught me. How to track. How to shoot. How to be a good warden. Things I like to think I am passing down to you.
translations.Sol Plaatje was a writer and a founding: Sol Plaatje was a writer and a founding member of the South African Native National Congress, which became the African National Congress we know today. Here in this hut, awake at night, surrounded by the sounds of the forest below, I read Sol Plaatje's novel -- the first written in English by a black South African. The book is entitled Mhudi, an epic of South African native life a hundred years ago. It is a masterpiece! I should give you my copy. Broaden your mind, as they say.
translations.Xitshembhiso means \"promise\". This is: Xitshembhiso means "promise". This is the oldest hut in Vurhonga. It's named for the promise we make as wardens, a promise made not just to our ancestors, but to every animal, every tree, and every rock in the savanna. That promise is, "We will preserve this land for our descendants." Though so much has happened in Vurhonga's past, your most important concern is Vurhonga's future. That's why my most important concern is YOU, Grandchild.
translations.I have never seen a play performed in a: I have never seen a play performed in a theatre, but if I did, I would want to see a play by the Serpent Players, the legendary team behind plays like Sizwe Bansi is Dead and The Island. I once heard an audio recording of The Island, very low quality, but the show was so good it didn't matter. I ordered the books, the texts of their plays, and read them here. I think it was 1979. Performing them in my mind over and over. You may not understand unless you know all the history, but my awareness of myself and this nation was heightened by these plays. They changed me. So, that's why I named this hut after the Serpent Players.
translations.The lakes in the region have had many na: The lakes in the region have had many names in our history. This one was renamed by me. Timanga means "peanut", and you must admit, the shape is a match. Peanuts are one of my favorite snacks when I'm out in the bush.
translations.Patu Makumu sits at the edge of this reg: Patu Makumu sits at the edge of this region, which is where it gets its name, the road's end.
translations.Do you remember the meaning of Xihlovoma: Do you remember the meaning of Xihlovomananga? It's "oasis". Technically any lake in the savanna is an oasis, but to me, this particular lake has an extra buzz to it. You can feel the energy of life all around you here. When you dream of Africa, perhaps this is what you dream of.
translations.Thvakile means \"dirty\", and it used to: Thvakile means "dirty", and it used to be one of the most polluted sites in the region. The rangers and local villagers came together to clean it, and for their efforts, Thvakile is now clean. Perhaps as Senior Warden, you can advocate for renaming it to something more respectable.
translations.Ridaka Hansi translates to \"mud floor\": Ridaka Hansi translates to "mud floor", which is exactly what you'll find in this lake. When I first started at Vurhonga, rains and overflow from the river carried excess silt here, to the detriment of the animals who used the lake for drinking water. We've attempted multiple clean-up operations over the years, but when it's stirred up, this is still the murkiest water in Vurhonga. The silt runs at least a meter deep.
translations.The ironically-named Prosperity is a gho: The ironically-named Prosperity is a ghost town established in 1870 at the height of the Silver Boom. In its heyday, it boasted a general store, a saloon, and even a school. These days all that's left is this collection of scattered buildings, high up in the hills where Rocky Mountain elk and mule deer visit almost as much as tourists do.
translations.I can't really say I blame people for wa: I can't really say I blame people for wanting to explore this cave, even though it's my official policy to advise against it unless you really know what you're doing. There's just something about the experience of seeing those cave paintings up close and personal that you don't really get with a computer screen. Maybe it's the dankness, and that plip-plop of dripping water.
translations.Pitchblende Pit was established just bef: Pitchblende Pit was established just before the Second World War to mine the region's rich uranium ore deposits. Uranium extracted from here was used in the Manhattan Project and throughout the Cold War, but the site has been sealed since the late 1980s. These days it's kept a close eye on.

translations.Camping Rules and Guidelines\n\n- Campin:
Camping Rules and Guidelines

- Camping is prohibited within 150 feet of any trail or stream.
- Dispose of human waste in a dug hole 6" to 8" deep and at least 150 ft. from water or campsites.
- Do not use soap to wash yourself, clothing, or dishes within 150 ft. of water.
- Fires should be built in designated fire pits or fireplaces if provided.
- Removing plants, rocks, fossils, or artifacts from state land without a permit is illegal.
- The use of bear-resistant canisters is required for overnight users.
translations.The whitetailed deer is a ruminant. Its: The whitetailed deer is a ruminant. Its stomach has four chambers for digesting food. In the first two chambers, food is mixed with bile to form the cud. The cud is regurgitated and rechewed and swallowed. In the omasum, the water is removed. Finally, the food enters the abomasum, where it is sent on to the small intestine where the nutrients from the food are absorbed.
translations.In certain parts, Layton Canyon stretche: In certain parts, Layton Canyon stretches almost 10 miles wide, and was carved out by the waters of Layton River. In the 1860s, gold was discovered in river bars near the present-day Layton Canyon National Recreation Area, and miners soon populated the canyon. There wasn't enough found to be profitable here though.
translations.Königsberg Lake is Central Europe's thir: Königsberg Lake is Central Europe's third largest lake, and its deepest point measures 180 meters (591 feet). There are stories that King Ludwig II of Bavaria had plans to build yet another castle on the shores of Königsberg, but never got around to it before his death.
translations.Go north. Take the first left. Follow pa: Go north. Take the first left. Follow path to the ruin, and search the area.
translations.Robert Sommer is one of the potential he: Robert Sommer is one of the potential heirs to the noble family of Königsberg. He issues hunting permits and is responsible for the area of Königsberg and its vicinity.
translations.\"Here, dad helped me spot the first moo:
"Here, dad helped me spot the first moose I ever harvested. It was a warm, summer day, August 19, 1990."

—P. Beatty
translations.\"The buffalo was everything to us. We c:
"The buffalo was everything to us. We could not live without it. We ate its flesh, and it made us strong. Nothing was thrown away. Their horns became spoons. We made tipis out of their skin, used it for bedding and winter clothes. We collected water in bags made out of their hide. When they were killed, we were killed."

—Robert "Strong Elk" Fog
translations.The Wildlife Varmint Control is operatin: The Wildlife Varmint Control is operating in the area to address the problem of hungry, wandering coyotes in nearby towns and cabin villages. There are many ethical considerations involved in wildlife management. Before initiating any wildlife control activities, an individual must become familiar with applicable federal, state, and local laws.
translations.\"The dark wild boar was slain but there:
"The dark wild boar was slain but there is still one evil boar out there. They call him 'Würst.' Sausage."

—Dr. Otto Canella
translations.Known as the “conservationist president,: Known as the “conservationist president,” Theodore Roosevelt established 150 national forests, 51 bird reserves, 4 national game preserves, 5 national parks, and 18 national monuments during his presidency from 1901 to 1909. He also gave his name to the Roosevelt elk.
"You have to think about that one shot. One shot is all it takes. A deer's gotta be taken down with one shot."

—Unknown
translations.\"It was here where I first laid eyes on:
"It was here where I first laid eyes on him, October 11, 2015. Mr. Black. It was love at first sight."

—J. Trampfine
translations.The surrounding larger area is believed: The surrounding larger area is believed to be home to approximately 80,000 wild boar.
translations.Early fire detection became a priority f: Early fire detection became a priority for the Forest Service after the devastating fires of 1910. Fire lookouts soon appeared in national forests all over the country to help aid detection. Lookout operators reported fires using telephones, carrier pigeons, and heliographs. While the Forest Service carrier pigeons have all been retired, a number of the fire lookouts are still in working order and are manned during fire season. Once the fire season passes, the lookouts become available to the public for overnight stays.
translations.\"I was engaged to my girlfriend Lisa he:
"I was engaged to my girlfriend Lisa here. On the shores of Tichenau Lake, 4th of May 1977."

—Unknown
translations.Doc is a reserve game warden. State gove: Doc is a reserve game warden. State government agencies often require a bachelor's degree in disciplines such as animal or environmental science, biology, zoology, ecology or criminal justice to qualify for a game warden position. Employers also require applicants to undergo medical, physical, and psychological assessments. Game wardens spend a large majority of their time in the field, enforcing laws related to wildlife. They also educate the public about environmental protection and laws within their jurisdictions.
translations.1.5 kg is a perfect amount of deer roast: 1.5 kg is a perfect amount of deer roast, serving about 8 mouths. In larger deer roasts, over 2 kg, there'll be overly chewy bits, while small venison steaks around 1 kg translate to smaller cuts, which are more difficult to cook carefully and results in more wastage of meat.
translations.Rumors say that you can find a spruce tr: Rumors say that you can find a spruce tree in the area that dates back to 1000 BC.
translations.Deer bucks either have a typical or atyp: Deer bucks either have a typical or atypical antler arrangement. Typical antlers are symmetrical and their points grow straight up off the main beam. Atypical antlers are asymmetrical and their points may project at any angle from the main beam.
translations.Alligators have long been feared and res: Alligators have long been feared and respected in Mississippi. The Choctaw tell the tale of a hunter who saved an alligator in need and was rewarded with wisdom: which deer to leave and which to harvest in order to become the greatest hunter. Overhunting led to them being designated an endangered species in Mississippi in the 1960s. Juvenile alligators from Louisiana were handed out in bags at the Mississippi State Fairgrounds, and by the late 1980s they were no longer listed as endangered in the state. Instead, the burgeoning population began to be seen as a nuisance.
translations.Holt Collier was born in 1846, into a fa:
Holt Collier was born in 1846, into a family of enslaved people that served the powerful Hinds family in Jefferson County, Mississippi. The young Collier attended Howell Hinds' young son and provided meat for the workers at the Plum Ridge Plantation, located in a rugged, thickly forested area. He shot his first bear at the age of 10. 

Collier joined his masters on the Confederate side of the civil war. A couple of years after the war, he returned to Mississippi and lived the rest of his life as a hunter and sportsman. He was famously asked to accompany president Theodore "Teddy" Roosevelt on a hunt and single-handedly subdued and tied up an adult male bear using only the butt of his rifle and some rope. Roosevelt refused to shoot the animal, and when the incident made it into the papers, an enterprising toy manufacturer created a stuffed animal design based on "Teddy's bear".
translations.Although the history of hunting in Missi:
Although the history of hunting in Mississippi is almost certainly as old as the place itself, with evidence of hunting practices dating from at least the past twelve thousand years, it wasn't until the early twentieth century that formal hunt clubs were introduced to the state. These were formed by settlers engaged in the gigantic project of clearing the still largely forested Delta to make space for farmland. They hunted black bear, turkey, and small game like squirrels or foxes. Deer weren't widespread in the state until the massive repopulation efforts of the last forty years.

Hunt clubs were places were people of all races and social classes could bond over a shared hobby. Formerly enslaved people like Holt Collier often hunted alongside white doctors, lawyers, and prominent businessmen. Women traditionally weren't admitted.

Today, the vast majority of Mississippians hunt on private land. Women make up around 12% of the hunting population of the state, and many of these participate in women-only hunts. Camp clubhouses range from simple trailers to upscale lodges.
translations.An oxbow lake is a horseshoe-shaped lake: An oxbow lake is a horseshoe-shaped lake that forms when the wide meander of a river is cut off. The slow-moving Mississippi is famous for its oxbows, but recent studies have found that the backwaters that form these incredibly important wetland habitats are beginning to disappear. Human activities like intensive farming, deforestation, and soil misuse increase the rate of sediment infilling in the oxbows. If this sediment remains trapped within the river by levees instead of running out onto the floodplain during seasonal flooding, the oxbows will gradually fill and eventually be gone for good. This would forever alter the unique ecology of the batture, the woods and wetlands that run along the Lower Mississippi.
translations.The name \"Mississippi\" derives from an: The name "Mississippi" derives from an Ojibwe word meaning "great river" or "father of the waters", and many Native American tribes have historically called Mississippi home. The Choctaw were most likely the original Mississippians and remain the most populous tribe to this day, but between 1500 and 1800 over 21 tribes lived in the area, including the Chickasaw, Natchez, Yazoo, and the Biloxi. From the 1830s onwards, members of the so-called Five Civilized Tribes were forcibly displaced from their ancestral homelands east of the Mississippi to make way for white settlers. Thousands died from disease or starvation. Today the Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians is the only federally recognized tribe in the state of Mississippi. It numbers about 10,000 people.
translations.If you're not concerned about calorie co: If you're not concerned about calorie counts, you'll be fed well in the Delta. Fried catfish, Delta-style tamales (smaller and spicier than their Mexican counterparts), slug burgers, and pies of various kinds are some of the local delicacies. Rural residents hunt and fish to put food on the table, so expect to be treated to venison or whatever's in season when you pay a visit. More adventurous types can try fried alligator bites.
The Mississippi River floods regularly. The flood of 1927 was the greatest in modern memory, with numerous levees breaking and inundating towns along the 2,340 mile (3,770 km) length of the river. Residents of the Mississippi Delta suffered greatly, especially African-Americans; many made the decision to move to the cities in the north permanently rather than continue a life of back-breaking labor. As a response to the flood, the federal government built an elaborate system of levees and floodways along the Mississippi. The spring floods of 2019 were the most damaging in 25 years, and scientists predict that future floods will be ever more volatile and unpredictable as a consequence of biome replacement and climate change.
translations.Fannye A. Cook pioneered conservation pr: Fannye A. Cook pioneered conservation practices in Mississippi. She was a researcher and scientist who formed the Mississippi Association for the Conservation of Wildlife and led a grassroots movement to reform game laws and overhaul the state's dated, county-based system of conservation management. "Miss Fannye", as she was affectionately known, ran traveling exhibitions throughout the state which featured her personal collection of mammals, bird, and aquatic life samples. Her efforts led to the formation of the Game and Fish Commission in 1932. Despite being eminently qualified to head the Commission, she was regulated to a background role in educational work. A collection of specimens gathered in a Commission survey headed by Cook formed the foundation for the Jackson state museum's scientific inventory, and Cook spent the rest of her working life as museum director. The Mississippi Museum of Natural Science was named by Fannye A. Cook Memorial Museum in her honor.
translations.Although the highest point in Mississipp: Although the highest point in Mississippi is only 807 feet (246 m) above sea level, the Hills region nevertheless looms large in Mississippi popular history. It's seen as a place of smaller farming settlements and a primarily white population, in contrast to the expansive cotton plantations and powerful white minority of the Delta. The Chickasaw made their home in the Hills for generations until they were forced out as a result of the 1830 Indian Removal Act. Those that settled in their place were mostly small farmers, and the region had Mississippi's lowest percentage of slaves in the 1860s. Following reconstruction, it remained primarily agricultural until industrialists began to build factories there in the 1930s. The Hills area is known for its writers and musicians, producing luminaries such as William Faulkner, Tennessee Williams, Elvis Presley, and Tammy Wynette.
translations.Cuatro Colinas' road network contains la: Cuatro Colinas' road network contains large sections which were previously dirt tracks that were created to aid in the moving of marble from the quarry, out to waiting barges on the river. During the renaissance, marble was a highly sought after commodity, and the work force here was massive.
translations.This region of Spain was hotly contested: This region of Spain was hotly contested during the Reconquista. Christian Visigoths of the Iberian peninsula set out to reclaim Spain from the Muslim kingdoms that had been established some years previously. Both sides built their own fortifications, and the ruins of these watchtowers and forts still remain.
translations.Our watchtowers are built on the foundat: Our watchtowers are built on the foundations of military outposts that used to oversee this region. While these sites were originally chosen for their strategic placement and their potential to spot approaching forces, they are now perfect vantage points for hunters and tourists alike.
translations.A lot of Spanish olives go towards makin: A lot of Spanish olives go towards making Olive oil, but many of our farmers cure their olives and sell them to upmarket restaurants. We don't have a huge footprint in the food market, but our farms have a very good reputation in cities like Madrid and Barcelona.
translations.It isn't always easy, running a game res: It isn't always easy, running a game reserve that happens to include large patches of farmland. It's a unique arrangement, where we take care of the pests that a farmer normally has to deal with, but we still cultivate animal populations in the area. When everyone pitches in, the arrangement works.
translations.Once this region had been secured by Chr: Once this region had been secured by Christian forces, many of the towers and fortifications were built. Rivalries between individual kingdoms made things politically unstable, regardless of religious inclination. Many unlikely alliances rose from this quagmire.
translations.The civil war was a dark period for all: The civil war was a dark period for all of Spain, and that includes my family. One night, a small militia broke into the Castillo with the intention of killing or capturing my great-grandfather and his family. He grabbed his rifle to defend the house, but fortunately my great-grandmother was able to convince him to hide up here in the cloister.
translations.These days, no farmers actually live on: These days, no farmers actually live on the reserve. Most of the owners actually live in the city and have hired farmhands to take care of most of the hard work. I doubt they make a great deal of profit, but many of the current owners inherited their farms and see it as a source of prestige to own a farm that's part of Cuatro Colinas.
translations.While there is no longer any military pr: While there is no longer any military presence in the region, I am glad that these watchtowers are still here in some form. They give us a glimpse back at a time long before Spain even existed, when the Iberian peninsula was divided into squabbling kingdoms.
translations.I struggle to picture this reserve witho: I struggle to picture this reserve without the influence of the river, cutting across the landscape. Not only is it stunningly beautiful when the sun hits it at dusk, but it is so important to everyone's livelihoods out here. It's been making lives easier out here for millenia.
translations.As well as the military ruins that are s: As well as the military ruins that are scattered throughout the region, there are many sites that have important historical significance. Many of the pilgrims who came to visit the monastery would also spend time in what they considered a "holy well", hoping for a cure to their ailments.
translations.Música norteña, \"northern music\", ofte: Música norteña, "northern music", often called norteño in English, is a style of regional Mexican music that originated in the nineteenth century as a blend of Hispanic oral traditions and the folk music of German, Polish, and Czech immigrants, especially the music that accompanied polka and waltz. The accordion and the bajo sexto, a string instrument in the guitar family, are its characteristic instruments. Norteño is particularly associated with corridos, narrative ballads with a strong social or political message. Topics encompass everything from love to the oppression of immigrants and the working class, and corridos have succeeded in keeping up with the times; so-called narcocorridos, which chronicle the misadventures of drug smugglers, are popular along the U.S./Mexico border.
translations.The Sonoran Desert is the hottest desert: The Sonoran Desert is the hottest desert in Mexico. It straddles the border with the U.S. states of Arizona and California, encompassing 310,800 square km (120,000 square miles) of territory between the Baja California Peninsula to the west and the Chihuahuan Desert to the east. The Sonoran Desert is famous for its saguaro and organ pipe cactus populations, but its pattern of summer monsoons and winter rains has resulted in it being home to more unique species of vegetation than any other desert in the world. The main threats to its biodiversity come from cattle ranching and urbanization.
translations.The vast majority (68 percent) of the la: The vast majority (68 percent) of the land within Mexico's conservation areas is not federally managed; most land is either owned by ranchers or managed collectively as part of an ejido or comunidad, two types of rural farming structures. This has necessitated a conservation strategy that differs from that taken across the border. Conservation groups buy up key habitats in northwestern Mexico and pay landowners not to use the land for logging and grazing. Still, most conservation groups active in the region recognise the necessity of cooperating across borders, and there are a number of organizations such as the Tucson, Arizona-based Sonoran Institute that operate binationally.
translations.The Mexican Revolution was a complex, bl:
The Mexican Revolution was a complex, bloody event that spanned over a decade. At the beginning of 1910, Mexico was a highly centralized state ruled by President Porfirio Díaz, who had been in power for seven terms, and his cadre of technocrats, los científicos. Discontentment with Díaz's regime was widespread among both the rural poor, roughly half of whom lived a semi-feudal existence working on haciendas, and the growing middle classes, who resented having to pay taxes to the central government. 

The breakthrough came when Francisco Madero formed a political party opposing Díaz's reelection. This launched a wave of rebellion, particularly in the northern states. Díaz was forced into exile, where he issued the ominous warning "Madero has unleashed a tiger. Let's see if he can control it". Elections were called and Madero was elected.

The next few years prove that tiger difficult to tame. A series of conspiracies, assassinations, and continued in-fighting test the leaders of the fragile revolution. Madero is overthrown and assassinated during the "ten tragic days" of 1913, replaced by the hated general Victoriano Huerta. New factions rise, the Villistas in the north and the Zapatistas in central Mexico. By 1920, a new constitution is in place and the bloodiest years of the revolution are over. 

The legacy of the Revolution is felt in Mexico to this day, especially in the dominance of the Partido Revolucionario Institucional, which held uninterrupted power in the country from 1929 until 2000. Many argue that its promises have yet to be realized.
translations.A wide range of indigenous peoples call: A wide range of indigenous peoples call Sonora home. The Mayo or Yoreme are the largest of these, with approximately 40 to 80,000 members living in the fertile Valle del Mayo. They speak the Mayo language, an agglutinative language and close relative of Yaqui, another indigenous language spoken in the valley of the Río Yaqui. Further to the north, the Tohono O’odham, meaning "desert people", have inhabited the Sonoran Desert region for centuries. They traditionally spent summers in "field villages" at the mouth of an arroyo and winters in "well villages" near a spring. They are a binational people, with populations in both Sonora and Arizona in the United States.
translations.The chupacabra, or \"goat-sucker\", is a: The chupacabra, or "goat-sucker", is a mysterious vampire-like creature that drains the blood of livestock. Some reports describe it as bipedal, with large eyes, spikes down the length of its back, and razor-sharp claws. Others liken it to a hairless dog. It was first sighted in Puerto Rico in the mid-nineties, and the urban legend soon spread throughout Latin America and the southwestern United States, aided by the growth of online messageboards. While supposed chupacabra carcasses have been revealed to be racoons or dogs that died from sarcoptic mange, and chupacabra victims merely animals that have been attacked by dogs, the myth has taken on a life of its own, with reports as far afield as India and Russia.
translations.The Mexican-American War was a two-year: The Mexican-American War was a two-year long conflict that led to a decisive U.S. victory and a serious loss of prestige for Mexico. Following the United States' annexation of Texas in 1845, then de facto independent but claimed by Mexico, U.S. congressmen began to drum up support for a war. A claim was made that Mexican troops had crossed the Rio Grande and "shed American blood on American soil". The war that followed would lead to a huge loss of life in Mexico and the cession of 1,300,000 square km (500,000 square miles) of territory.
translations.Different deer species were introduced t: Different deer species were introduced to New Zealand in waves throughout the nineteenth century. By the early twentieth century, the population of red deer in the southern South Island had exploded, threatening native flora and leading the government to encourage decisive action against the deer menace. From the 1960s, professional hunters shot and extracted deer from helicopters in remote regions of the South Island. High venison prices led to an extraordinarily competitive industry for those brave -- or foolish -- enough to sign up. Hunters would jump from the helicopters straight onto the deer and twist their necks, the so-called "bulldogging" technique. Unsurprisingly, the industry was poorly regulated and accidents, sometimes leading to death, were common.
translations.\"Kaitiakitanga\" is a Māori word that c: "Kaitiakitanga" is a Māori word that can be translated as "guardianship" or "preservation". A complex concept, it refers to methods of safeguarding resources for future generations through preserving the "mauri" or life force of the land. Some examples include: enforcing rāhui or restrictions on the harvesting of food in certain seasons or areas, taking only what's needed, and hunting and fishing for food rather than sport. Conservationists in New Zealand work closely with iwi and hapū -- tribes and sub-tribes -- to uphold kaitiakitanga. The philosophy can be summarised in the Māori saying "ko ahau te awa, ko te awa ko ahau" - "I am the river, the river is me".
translations.Many colonized countries had gold rushes: Many colonized countries had gold rushes in the nineteenth century, and New Zealand was no exception. The Otago Gold Rush beginning in the early 1860s attracted veteran prospectors from as far away as California and Victoria, Australia. Thousands of diggers, including men from China, flocked to the region to make their fortune. Later rushes on the West Coast followed. Environmental and safety concerns were essentially non-existent, but the gold rush kick-started the fledgling colony's economy and to this day gold mining remains a small but lucrative industry in New Zealand.
translations.The use of the pesticide 1080, the brand: The use of the pesticide 1080, the brand name given to the synthetic form of sodium fluoroacetate, is controversial in New Zealand. Many conservationists maintain that it is the most efficient and effective way to cull populations of invasive mammalian pests like possums and stoats while preserving native species, but animal rights activists consider it a cruel and inhumane solution and hunters argue that it often inadvertently targets valuable game populations.
translations.The kiwi is a hairy, flightless bird end: The kiwi is a hairy, flightless bird endemic to New Zealand, the smallest living member of the ratite group which includes ostriches, emus, and rheas. Found primarily in temperate forests, habitat loss and intrusion by invasive mammalian predators have forced them to adapt to grassland and non-native forest. Kiwi have lent their name to the common nickname for New Zealanders and, as an unlikely national icon, are a priority for conservation efforts in the country. Studies have shown that only a small fraction of chicks, five to ten percent, survive to adulthood without management.
translations.The imposing limestone formation here is: The imposing limestone formation here is, as the name "Stonecastle" suggests, reminiscent of an old European castle. It's no surprise that the site has formed the backdrop for climatic battle scenes in several films, including Resplendent Sword. Kūmara or sweet potato was once widely cultivated here, and the region is of special significance to the Ngāi Tahu iwi. They ask that visitors refrain from biking, dog walking, or using drones.
translations.This extensive limestone cave formed fro:
This extensive limestone cave formed from the gradual erosion of the karst landscape, diverting the river from its original course. The cave harvestman, a rare species of arachnid, is found in the cave's "dark zone". It is only known to live in two caves on the West Coast.

The cave is passable if the water is low, but visitors are warned to exercise extreme caution if the stream is abnormally high or discolored.
translations.The cave paintings in Broken River Cave: The cave paintings in Broken River Cave are some of the oldest found in New Zealand, living evidence of a presence in the area that stretches back as far as the 14th century. These peoples lived a hunter-gatherer existence and this is reflected in the delicate, semi-abstract scenes of fishing and hunting that decorate the walls here, daubed in red kōkōwai and charcoal: paddling a waka (canoe), confronting a taniwha (water spirit), holding a spear.
translations.A marae is a communal meeting place in P: A marae is a communal meeting place in Polynesian culture. Meaning "free of trees" or "free of weeds", it's generally an area of flat, cleared land bordered with stone or wooden posts, centered around a wharenui or meeting house. Marae are important spiritual and community centres and host ceremonies and celebrations of all kinds.
translations.Filmmaking is a lucrative industry in Ne: Filmmaking is a lucrative industry in New Zealand, with annual screen revenue of over NZ$3 billion in 2018. Profit is highly concentrated; the Auckland region accounts for over 50 percent of screen revenue in a given year. The majority of revenue is still generated by domestic contracts, but this is steadily decreasing: in 2016, about a third of gross revenue was international business, with 90% of this coming from North America. Tourism has grown in kind, with sleepy rural areas featured in films transformed into major attractions almost overnight.
translations.The willow tree curving gently out of th: The willow tree curving gently out of the lake here had an inauspicious start, beginning life as a single branch nailed to a fence post eighty years ago. These days the throngs of visiting daytrippers trying to capture an isolation that no longer exists makes for a somewhat ironic sight, and to many local photographers the mere mention of #thatwakaititree, as it's known on social media, elicits a sigh followed by a laugh.
translations.The Ngāi Tahu iwi is the principal Māori:
The Ngāi Tahu iwi is the principal Māori tribe of the South Island. Their trace their ancestry back to Paikea, who, fleeing his brother's murderous rage, left the Polynesian homeland Hawaiki on the back of a whale and arrived on the North Island. The iwi takes its name from his descendent Tahupōtiki. 

In the eighteenth century, a group of Ngāi Tahu established a foothold on the South Island and over successive generations of war and intermarriage with neighboring tribes eventually took control of much of the South Island, including valuable regions of pounamu/greenstone cultivation. The tribe sold land to the British Crown in the mid-nineteenth century, but the Crown reneged on its promises to keep some of the land in their hands and to provide schools and hospitals. Their claim was finally settled in the 1990s, including the return of the sacred mountain of Aoraki.
translations.The only mammals native to New Zealand a: The only mammals native to New Zealand are bats and some marine species. Māori settlers brought dogs and rats in the thirteenth century, but it wasn't until Europeans arrived that new species were released en masse, especially from the nineteenth century onwards with the popularity of acclimatization societies, voluntary bodies that encouraged the introduction of non-native species in hopes that they would acclimatize and adapt. This did happen, often to disastrous effect. Pests like stoats and possum continue to threaten native wildlife, while even game animals can cause destruction unless their numbers are regulated.
translations.Titanosaurs were the last of the long-ne: Titanosaurs were the last of the long-necked sauropods to roam the Earth. Among the titanosaurs discovered in this area, there are Patagotitan and Argentinosaurus, estimated to be the largest animals to have ever walked the Earth. Imagine hunting game that weighs over 70 tonnes!
translations.North Americans have cowboys, we have ga:
North Americans have cowboys, we have gauchos. The golden age of gaucho life ended with the 19th century, but today, gauchos like the Cabrera family still tend the horses, herds, and flocks at my estancia, and across the continent. Rugged nomads, master horseman, they drive hard and live simply. 

Gauchos don't all wear ponchos and bombachas these days, but they still carry a lasso, whip, and facón, their signature knife. Most gauchos are men, but you can find many gauchas like Beatriz Cabrera. Don't believe every stereotype you read.

As tourism becomes more profitable than farming, I expect most of the gauchos at my estancia will transition to work at Parque Fernando. You will find them genial guides and magnificent cooks for asado. Their vital connection to the land gives them an edge over most folk. Their way of life is disappearing, but they are all champions.
translations.While many species in Patagonia are inva: While many species in Patagonia are invaders who were introduced in the last century, the trees and shrubs of the Nothofagus genus (commonly called "southern beeches") are Patagonia natives -- and by natives, I mean we have fossils indicating they've been here since the Cretaceous period. These evergreens can be found all across the reserve. Their nuts are edible when properly cooked.
translations.This \"Lair of the Pampered Pumas\" was: This "Lair of the Pampered Pumas" was once a den for Pequeña Eva, my most beloved puma of all time. I saved her from many hunters and overzealous bagualeros. She saved me from a lot of bad men in return, viste? Now, her succeeding generations make use of the den. Sometimes I wonder if they know she was there. Do they pick up a certain scent, feel a tingle in their spine, and remember their previous life as my Pequeña Eva? Who is to say they don't?
translations.This pass connecting the Bosque Muerto w:
This pass connecting the Bosque Muerto with the swamps, I named "Pass of the Changing Winds". Why? Because sometimes, the winds are not in your favor, mala leche! Everything is going wrong. 

You track a beautiful red stag for over an hour, then one wrong step on a twig, CRACK, and the trophy of a lifetime spooks and bolts in a flash. 

You shoot a water buffalo, but you strike shoulder blade, and the wounded buffalo charges off over a hill. By the time you reposition, the animal has disappeared into a forest, and you have to spend the rest of the afternoon tracking it down while it slowly bleeds out. 

Hunting can be hard. Life can be hard. But the winds always change, and so will your luck, as long as you keep fighting... and keep a few pampered pumas on hand, just in case you need them. Mala leche won't last forever. Remember that.
translations.This breathtaking stretch of road was bl: This breathtaking stretch of road was blasted out of the side of a mountain to create a route between the mining hubs of Prosperity and Silverville. Drivers are warned to be on their guard; hairpin turns and narrow lanes are frequent, there are no barriers or railings, and the drop into the gorge below is steep.
translations.Prosperity is one of over 700 ghost town: Prosperity is one of over 700 ghost towns scattered throughout the state of Colorado. A silver mining community established at the height of the rush to the West in 1870, in its heyday it boasted a general store, a saloon, and even a small school. The repeal of the Sherman Silver Purchase Act in 1893 put the brakes on the Silver Boom and spelled the end for the fledgling settlement, the promise of its name becoming a bitter irony. Now all that's left are a few lonely cabins. There are stories of noises in the night and unexplained lights, but they're probably just old wives' tales.
translations.Pitchblende is another name for uraninit: Pitchblende is another name for uraninite, a major ore of uranium. Uranium from Pitchblende Pit was used in the Manhattan Project to create the first atomic bomb, and during the Cold War it became one of the major "yellowcake" hubs of the region as demand skyrocketed. The site has been sealed since the 1980s.
translations.The dramatic scenery of the Colorado Roc: The dramatic scenery of the Colorado Rockies has attracted many a Hollywood filmmaker. In particular it's served as the setting for numerous westerns, most famously John Wayne's 1969 True Grit, as well as How the West Was Won and Tribute to a Bad Man.
translations.Dinosaur Hill is the highlight of Silver: Dinosaur Hill is the highlight of Silver Ridge Peak's palaeontological wonders. In this bed of Cretaceous Dakota Sandstone you can observe almost perfectly preserved tracks from over 30 individuals, mostly iguanodon, large, duck-billed herbivores, and theropods, a smaller type of carnivore with an ostrich-like appearance. The tracks were created by dinosaurs migrating across what was then the shoreline of a vast shallow sea extending across much of the present-day United States.
translations.The last grizzly bear recorded in the st: The last grizzly bear recorded in the state of Colorado was killed by one Tom Sharp in September 1979. According to Sharp's extraordinary version of events, it occurred when the then outfitter was out archery elk hunting in the San Juan wilderness and was suddenly charged by a 400 pound female grizzly. When she knocked the bow out of his hands, he instinctively grabbed the nearest arrow and plunged it into her chest, hitting a jugular and killing her almost instantly. In hospital Sharp was arrested under the Endangered Species Act. He maintains he acted in self-defense to this day.
translations.The Southern Rockies are dotted with geo: The Southern Rockies are dotted with geothermal sulfur hot springs. These were used by the Ute tribe for medicinal purposes, and when European colonists arrived their presence, in combination with the snow-capped peaks and glacial lakes, led them to dub the region "The Switzerland of America".
translations.Tipi rings are found all over the Great: Tipi rings are found all over the Great Plains and Southern Rocky Mountains. The indigenous peoples of the region used the stones at these circular encampments to ensure that their tipis stayed level with the ground. They are often located near promising hunting sites or travel routes.
translations.The Bear Dance is an annual event celebr: The Bear Dance is an annual event celebrated by the Ute people to mark the emergence of the bear from hibernation at the first thunderclap of spring, marked by ten days of courtship dances, feasting, games, and horse racing. The legends tell that the dance was taught to a young hunter by a bear, and to this day it's performed as a way to let off steam after the long darkness of winter.
translations.The narrow-gauge funicular railway here: The narrow-gauge funicular railway here dates from the turn of the 20th century. It was originally used to transport materials up to the settlements at the top of the mountain, but quickly became a popular tourist attraction. These days it's been repurposed as a formidable hiking trail, boasting a steep incline and some great views of the surrounding scenery.
translations.These red mountains are called the Sun S: These red mountains are called the Sun Sisters by the Native inhabitants of the region, and Burnt Rocks by the descendents of colonial settlers. They get their coloration from the iron ore deposits that dot their surfaces. The summits offer incredible views out over the rest of the reserve, so high up you can almost touch the clouds.
translations.The Ute people have inhabited this regio: The Ute people have inhabited this region for centuries. Sharing a language and culture, the twelve bands stretch from Utah in the northwest to Colorado and New Mexico in the southeast. The Uncompahgre Ute band lived here as nomadic hunter-gatherers, moving up into the Sun Sisters mountains to hunt in the summer and wintering in the valleys. They are known for being one of the first peoples to harness triboluminescence: ceremonial rattles made from translucent buffalo skin are filled with quartz crystals that produce flashes of light under mechanical stress when shaken.

translations.Nenets come to the Dikiy coast to fish i: Nenets come to the Dikiy coast to fish in the warm months. They eat the fish raw and freeze what they can preseve when the cold returns. The unique Nenets diet of reindeer, fish, and berries contributes to their excellent health as a community.
translations.This lake feeds fresh water to the Nenet: This lake feeds fresh water to the Nenets and their reindeer, and for that, they give thanks and sacrifice to the lake, and to their ancestors who traveled this land before them and shared this lake. The Nenets share a bond with their ancestors, the reindeer, and the land that is rare in modern times.
translations.The forests south of the lake are danger: The forests south of the lake are dangerous, yet the Nenets must cross them in order to make their journey to the coast and back to graze the reindeer and gather resources. The Nenets have become adept at tracking brown bears to avoid leading their reindeer into the path of hungry predators.
translations.As people who revere nature, the Nenets: As people who revere nature, the Nenets respect the cosmos as well. The sun is of paramount concern to them. They move their herds according to the seasons. From up here, where the sunset is so beautiful, the view of the southern valley makes this an ideal site for the Nenets to devote their prayers to the sun.
translations.Sacred sites near feeding zones can be a: Sacred sites near feeding zones can be a way of honoring the animals hunted there by the Nenets. They can also honor an ancestor, who may have favored this area to hunt. Without a shaman to confirm it, we can only guess.
Here, one feels at the top of the world. The Nenets come here for a variety of reasons, but for this region in particular, they are probably honoring the bears and the moose who live in this area. The Nenets do not rely on either game as a resource, but they mind the reindeer herd overgrazing the same land as the moose, and avoid tempting hungry bears from attacking the herd.
translations.Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 3:\nB:
Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 3:
Beautiful day of hiking and mountain climbing. No sign of bears. Weather dry and sunny. Crew confidence is high. Camping in the hills tonight!
translations.Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 4:\nW:
Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 4:
We left a boar roasting on the fire overnight. Scent drew a hungry bear to the camp. We had to abandon camp. Many supplies lost.
translations.Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 5:\nS:
Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 5:
Supply issue is more dire than we thought. Weather pounding the coasts. We will need to head south and east to return to base camp.
translations.Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 6:\nT:
Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 6:
The Gateway to the Underworld is a haunting sight, but this crew does not believe in ghosts. They are, however, getting hungrier as supplies dwindle and rations get smaller. Hungry people are not always reasonable.
translations.Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 8:\nT:
Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 8:
Temperature dropped 10 degrees today. Crew pushed on. We’ve taken temporary refuge in the mountains. This time, we will not roast boar overnight, or otherwise leave any food out to attract bears.
translations.Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 7:\nT:
Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 7:
The wild boars are less plentiful around here. Moose are a more difficult game to claim. We must move quickly. Air temperature dropping 5 degrees per day. Crew frightened.

translations.Caused by hunting. When pressure reaches: Caused by hunting. When pressure reaches Dead Zone, animals will avoid this area.
translations.Caused by hunting. Animals will avoid th: Caused by hunting. Animals will avoid this area.
translations.The lake here (\"Jewel Lake\" in English: The lake here ("Jewel Lake" in English) is a great respite from the summer heat, but rumor has it that it's named for more than just its crystal-clear waters. Pancho Villa's band of outlaws are said to have "reclaimed" a large amount of treasure, one million pesos in solid gold pieces, from a manor house in Hermosillo belonging to the deserter Thomás Urbina. They hid this treasure somewhere between Hermosillo and Chihuahua City, and there are all sorts of theories about where that "somewhere" is. Personally I wouldn't rule out a small, secluded lake in difficult country...
translations.The name of this remote valley derives f: The name of this remote valley derives from the Mayo language and means "New place in water". It's a difficult trek through thick, hilly Chihuahua pine forest to reach it. If you'd prefer to stick to lower ground, the open grassland further down the valley is a good spot to hunt deer.
translations.Some of the highest points in the ranch: Some of the highest points in the ranch jut out from the spiny mountain peaks here. If you're willing to take a hike, you'll be rewarded with spectacular sunsets out over the desert. Back when he was still spry, my bisabuelo Javier would take us kids up the smaller peak to the east of the casa grande. "I can see my house from here!" he'd say every time.
translations.Los Charcos, \"The Puddles\", is maybe a: Los Charcos, "The Puddles", is maybe a bit of an unkind designation for the many interconnected lakes in this lush, hilly region. They're vitally important watering holes for the local fauna, deer and coyotes as well as turkeys. I've even seen the occasional pheasant make the journey here.
translations.There are a lot of Soto family stories a: There are a lot of Soto family stories about unlucky travelers accosted by bandits on the dirt path that winds through this mountain pass. "Descamisados" literally means "shirtless", and although these days it's more used metaphorically to describe a poor or unfortunate person, I can imagine most of the people who passed through here and lived to tell the tale ended up very literally being robbed of the shirts off their backs.
translations.Padre Eusebio Kino was a missionary acti: Padre Eusebio Kino was a missionary active in the seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries. He traveled extensively in the region then known as Pimería Alta, modern-day Sonora and Arizona, meeting with representatives of indigenous peoples and preaching the Gospels. You'll find plenty of places in Sonora named for him, especially in cattle country; it's said that the herd of twenty cattle he imported into Pimería Alta grew to 70,000 in his lifetime.
translations.Eighty five percent of desert animals de: Eighty five percent of desert animals depend on riparian forest like this for some phase of their lifecycle. But activities that divert groundwater resources like cattle ranching cause the trees to become degraded and eventually wither away. We're doing everything we can to ensure the survival of what little we have left, I assure you.
translations.This region marks the original extent of: This region marks the original extent of my family's estate. "Hacienda", as I'm sure you know, is a versatile word: it can mean both the estate itself and the manor house at the center, what we call "la casa grande". The land here is lusher than the surrounding xeric desert; it's prime cattle country, or at least it used to be. These days way too much of it is buffelgrass.
translations.This is the driest part of the ranch. Li: This is the driest part of the ranch. Little wonder the people who named it thought of it as a place of rest and contemplation; when the heat really hits you there's not much to do but find shelter and wait it out. My abuela told me there's a small shrine to Our Lady of Guadalupe somewhere in the area, but I've never come across it.
translations.Someone with an overactive imagination g: Someone with an overactive imagination gave the hills here the poetic title "Hump of the Devil". They've got some sparse brushy tree cover, but the area below is real desert country: nothing but miles and miles of saguaro and ocotillo and palo verde. Come here if you're looking to get lost.
translations.Dear Warden Shabanangu,\nLast night I ha:
Dear Warden Shabanangu,
Last night I had the pleasure of drinking beer with some of your friendly local hunters. I must have drank too much, because when I woke up, I had lost a lot of gear, including my radio batteries. No worries! As long as I have my camera, my mission continues! Those hunters tipped me off some local fungi that may help me see the Eloko, so I'm off to look for buffalo dung. I promise to check in with you A-S-A-P.

translations.A second-hand edition of an old illustra:
A second-hand edition of an old illustrated children's book based on the folk song "Waltzing Matilda".

We've had a tradition with Soph all over the years: buy each other silly, fun presents to celebrate our friendship anniversary. It started with Year 5 I believe. The unspoken rules are: 1. they should not be expensive 2. whoever bought the losing present owes the winner a barbie.

I bent the rules a bit this year: Soph used to love this book when she was a kid, but she lost it at some point. She hasn't mentioned it in years, but I knew this tidbit might come to good use some day.

The bad news is, I've had that bloody song stuck in my head for 3 days straight.
translations.My wife Lizzie read this article in our:
My wife Lizzie read this article in our local paper the other day and saved it for me, as I'm kind of the go-to guy for salties in the area. 

"Stevie" was the nickname for a saltie that wreaked havoc a couple of years ago. I managed to catch him - that was rough, believe me.

Obviously this isn't the same saltie, but it's still bad news if they start venturing outside their natural environments.

translations.Public Saunas are usually between 60-100: Public Saunas are usually between 60-100 degrees Celsius (140-210 Fahrenheit), while private ones are known to reach 70-110 degrees Celsius (160-230 Fahrenheit). While in the Sauna it's customary to use dried or fresh birch to whip oneself. It acts as a massage and increases blood flow. The birch can also be placed on the heater unit to release its aromatics into the air.
