Itinerary:

1. Welcome Señor Torres & Señor Molina.
2. Refreshments. (Rosa has taken care of this. They should be ready to go.)
3. Highlight the need for tourism in the region.
4. Show projections for current economic downturn, if no investment is made in local tourism.
5. Cede the floor to Señor Molina, so he can give his presentation on Vista España's current offer.
6. Seal the deal by highlighting the immediate windfall that will be gathered by selling the public land to VE.
7. End with an inspection of the outpost and immediately surrounding areas.
translations.Tourism Giant Under Investigation Follow:
Tourism Giant Under Investigation Following Manslaughter Allegations

Police are looking into multiple cases of manslaughter, as well as a range of other crimes that may have been perpetrated in the previous two years by agents on the behalf of the Vista España tourism conglomerate.
The body of Pedro Alvares (38) was discovered shortly after police were made aware of a conspiracy to sabotage the Cuatro Colinas game reserve. Alvares is believed to have been killed while acting on behalf of Vista España.

While Vista España have denied all allegations at this time, their stock price has taken a considerable dip. This is due to investigations being opened into other recent acquisitions by the tourism powerhouse who have a diverse range of tourist destinations across Spain. While the Cuatro Colinas business deal was far from a done deal, local residents have reported that they were approached by representatives who asked pointed questions about their relationship with the De Bosque family, who have historic ties to the region, and have overseen some form of hunting reserve in the region for over three centuries.

Vista España have yet to give any statement, other than a denial of the allegations. However, industry insiders are in agreement that Vista España's recent withdrawal from negotiations over the acquisition of several cruise liners is a strong indication of fear over the future of the company's finances. After last year's reported profits exceeding two-billion euros, it's unclear just how problematic this lawsuit will be for Vista España as they attempt to regain their reputation for being responsible, ethical and family-friendly.
translations.Wolf Hunt Notes\n\n(Day 1 - 17:50) Follo:
Wolf Hunt Notes

(Day 1 - 17:50) Following signs that indicate a wolf might be in the area. Currently struggling to see anything conclusive, but my camera trap definitely caught something in this region two nights ago.

(Day 2 - 19:40) I have set up a site in the open, baiting it with some wolf feces and urine.
(Day 2 - 21:00) I've had the wind with me all night, and still no sign of the wolf out by the site.
(Day 2 - 21:20) I keep seeing what looks like a moving shape in the tree-line, but I can't tell what it is. It's little more than a shadow.

(Day 3 - 06:30) The camera trap I set up at the edge of the tree line caught the wolf three times last night. It knows that something is up. I don't think a baiting site is going to work in the open.
(Day 3 - 15:00) Took my mind off things with a hunt elsewhere, but this wolf has me curious. Just how smart is it? TIme for a new strategy tonight.
(Day 3 - 20:35) I set up more camera traps in the woods and was able to spot the wolf as it dragged a fox from the open, back into the cover of the woods. It's smart, and it's already eaten tonight.

(Day 4 - 20:00) I've set up the lure much closer to the treeline, now. The shot will be difficult and it will move quickly, so I need to get closer than I'd like.
(Day 4 - 21:20) I was so close! I saw it through my scope for the first time, but the wind was changing and I couldn't draw a bead on it quickly enough. It disappeared, chasing a hare into the trees.
translations.Señor Alvares,\n\nV.E. has another job f:
Señor Alvares,

V.E. has another job for you. You need to extract sensitive assets. Enclosed are the following:
* Tranquilizing rifle and five (5) darts containing xylazine solution
* Two (2) cages appropriately reinforced to contain the assets
* One (1) GPS tracker tuned to the sub-dermal chips of the assets

Instructions from our veterinarian: 
Solution in darts is to be applied intermuscularly, so aim for the chest or upper thigh; a single dart will take between 1 and 15 minutes to act and cause incapacitation lasting several hours. Note that these animals have been raised to foster aggressive traits and are thus extremely dangerous - DO NOT UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES ATTEMPT TO CAPTURE WITHOUT FIRST APPLYING THE APPROPRIATE LEVEL OF SEDATION. 

Tracked assets:

* Specimen IW01 - Channel A
          Fur color: Black
          Known activity: Hunting at night
          Last seen: Date of insertion in reserve.

* Specimen IW02 - Channel B
          Fur color: Common
          Known activity: Feeding on nearby cattle
          Last seen: Marking territory near abandoned monastery

* Specimen IW03 - Channel C
          Fur color: White
          Known activity: Deceased
          Last seen: Terminated by third party
          DO NOT RETRIEVE OR ATTEMPT TO LOCATE.

Assets are to be extracted from Cuatro Colinas Game Reserve at the earliest opportunity.

Regards,
Daniel Garrido Ruiz 
Chief Operating Officer

P.S. Take measures to ensure that all traces of our operation, including this letter, are destroyed IMMEDIATELY.
translations.SOTO SON MISSING\n\nLast Seen Grazing Ca:
SOTO SON MISSING

Last Seen Grazing Cattle. Fighting Erupts on Rancho del Arroyo

Raúl Soto del Bosque, second son of Manuel Soto Campos, the proprietor of the Rancho del Arroyo hacienda, has been reported missing. The nineteen-year-old was last seen by his elder brother Javier as they brought cattle to graze on their typical route along the eponymous arroyo, several weeks previous. Señor Soto recovered a white neckerchief he believes belongs to his brother from the desert a week later, and is hopeful that he will be found alive. The Soto family has offered a handsome reward to the public for any information on the young man's whereabouts. Speaking from the family's apartment in Hermosillo, the Soto patriarch appealed to his son to give up any revolutionary aspirations he may harbor and come home. 

He also made a plea for the end of hostilities in the region. Continuing political unrest has left its mark on the hacienda, with Villista troops attacking nearby villages under the control of the Constitutional Army and violence spilling over into what has been a hitherto largely unaffected pocket of Sonora. A spate of disappearances of U.S. Americans in the region has also caused diplomatic consternation. READ MORE ABOUT THIS ON PAGE 4
translations.August 1916\n\nWe just got done moving t:
August 1916

We just got done moving the cattle and I'm holed up in Bosque Alto. Javier didn't want me to come with him. Mother begged him: "take your brother too, he needs to learn". Then he spent the entire damn journey talking about how wrong I am. About how I'm chasing a fool and now that that dog Huerta's been exiled, we should be focusing on the country's stability. 

"Join the Zapatistas if you want land reform; Villa's only about filling his own officers' pockets." 

Maybe I will, get away from this damn ranch. Sometimes I have no idea what we're fighting for anymore. 

September 1916

Javier keeps telling me that I need to put the struggle behind me. "We both wanted change," he says, "and we've got it." That tyrant Díaz is gone, Huerta's gone. What's the use in fighting ourselves? Says he's being "pragmatic". But he'll never admit that our own damn family has overseen this brutal and ineffectual system. No matter how good we told ourselves we were to our peones, everything works to our favor. It makes me sick to hear Javier and Father defending it. As if we had some God-given right to this land we probably stole in the first place!

Javier only armed himself because Díaz was taxing us to death. Now he's gone back to Hermosillo with Mother and Father to wait it out. We only see each other when we need to move the cattle.

I've been reading a lot lately. I can hear the shelling and gunfire out west sometimes, but up here it's quiet.

October 1916

I got into another fight with Javier. He's taken my gun. ¡Pinche Javier! How does he expect me to survive out here? 

Honestly, I'm more afraid of him than I am of bandits sometimes. At least I fought on the same side as some of them. Javier won't listen no matter what I say.
translations.That's called a stone arch bridge, I bel:
That's called a stone arch bridge, I believe. I read they built a lot of them in New England during the 19th century, in order to replace the old wooden bridges with something a little sturdier.
 
Just looking at it, you can tell the expertise and precision that went into cutting these stones... The stones all had to fit perfectly to make the bridge stable.

No wonder those bridges have been recognized as a historic civil engineering landmark in New England.
translations.TREV and I were on a long hike a few yea:
TREV and I were on a long hike a few years ago and took a break there. It's a small upland lake, with the mountain ridge in the distance.

It's one of the many views that made him fall in love with this region, and convinced him to take a full-time job here... If I remember correctly, that place also has a personal significance for him and SAM.
translations.A very good fishing spot. That pier is l:
A very good fishing spot. That pier is located on one of the largest lakes in the reserve I think, so it's home to many fish species. And even more important.... it's quiet. When TREV brought me here for the first time, I was pleased to see he clearly knew what I like - and what I don't like.

Can't remember how the lake was called, though. I think it was named after a famous writer, or painter, from New England, like a lot of places out here.
translations.The Golden Eye eats crustaceans, insects: The Golden Eye eats crustaceans, insects and molluscs. Evolution-wise, it went from being a fish, to a landwalking animal, then to a bird. And at this moment in time, it's a flying bird that feeds by diving underwater. Funny how it went all full circle in a way.
translations.The sign is a bit on-the-nose, but I had: The sign is a bit on-the-nose, but I had to put it up for the more... extreme tourists. We had this one guy from Medici, he came in one day, unguided, and started climbing every tower and cliff and WOOSH! -- jumping off in a wing suit. He could soar like an eagle... for about thirty seconds. Then crash -- BOOM! This maniac took down FOUR lookout towers in one afternoon, without cause! Can you believe that? Put himself in the hospital and I tell you, he deserved every last broken bone! His ridiculous stunts cost us a fortune in repairs. [sighs, shrugs it off] So, that's why the sign.
translations.This Xipene, you call it the gemsbok or: This Xipene, you call it the gemsbok or South African oryx, is a major target for hunters and poachers. Their horns fetch a deluxe price. Despite that threat, they've lost so many natural predators, their population is booming at an unsustainable rate.
translations.Bagging a Rocky Mountain goat is a chall: Bagging a Rocky Mountain goat is a challenge even for experienced hunters. Like bighorn sheep, they tend to stick to mountain faces above the timber line where they're difficult to pick off. Try scouting them when they graze the meadows during the daytime.
translations.There's nothing quite like bighorn sheep: There's nothing quite like bighorn sheep hunting. They have incredible eyesight, can detect movement over great distances, and are equally comfortable in alpine meadows and mountain slopes, so it's always difficult, but those horns are worth it. My advice is to stay well back and catch them unaware on lower ground before they have a chance to disappear up the tree line.
translations.I've been hunting mule deer for twenty y: I've been hunting mule deer for twenty years, but let me tell you, they still find ways to surprise me. They'll hear you coming from a good way off, if they haven't already picked up your scent. Lucky for us, it's hard for them to camouflage themselves in the green meadows of Colorado.
translations.There should be a great view of the surr: There should be a great view of the surrounding area from up on this tower.
translations.Did you know that elk used to have tusks: Did you know that elk used to have tusks? There are two little teeth that hunters call ivories in the upper jaw, an evolutionary remnant. One day I came across the skull of a winterkill. The antlers were gone, but I noticed it still had the ivories.
translations.Of all the things that can kill you out: Of all the things that can kill you out here, you wouldn't think trees would be at the top of the list, but you can't scare off the elements like you can with a bear. If you see a lot of blowdowns, watch out. Out in western Montana, where I guide, I've had a couple of close calls with trees after windstorms.
Nice to sit down and have a bite to eat. I've spent days rationing food but it's definitely not something I'd advise you to do if you can avoid it. Out in the backcountry, you have to make sure you can fit enough into your backpack to keep you fed for the duration of your trip.
translations.I went off on a solo mule deer hunt once: I went off on a solo mule deer hunt once having only packed enough for three days. The first day I did 4000 feet in elevation gain, and continued for a few days on a calorie deficit. When I finally harvested a buck, I was so hungry I ate some of the heart raw. I wouldn't recommend it, but it did give me enough energy to get back down.
translations.Is it a pig? Is it a skunk? Well, neithe: Is it a pig? Is it a skunk? Well, neither actually. But it is tasty! At least in my estimation. Just make sure you don't burst the scent gland.
translations.The southern part of the Rotwald region: The southern part of the Rotwald region is called Jonsdorf and its great for hiking. We get a lot of summer tourism up there. Not as much this time of year, but we discourage people from coming during hunting season.
translations.Now there's some good hunting to be had: Now there's some good hunting to be had in Willipeg for sure, but this part of the reserve seems to get more spelunkers than hunters, especially during the summer season. That's on account of the old Willipeg cave system that stretches out under Mount Kraken. You should stop on by if you get the chance.
translations.Chopeeka was an important area to the in: Chopeeka was an important area to the indigenous population before the frontier expansion and smallpox epidemic. The descendants have a reservation elsewhere today, but the reserve has worked with them to raise some totem monuments to honor these grounds.
translations.Mount Kraken peaks at over 6500 ft and i: Mount Kraken peaks at over 6500 ft and is one of the highest in the nearby region. This is the home range of our local black bear population, and we're very careful about keeping the outposts and Lookout towers free of food scraps, so as not to attract any bears. Oh, and you should check out the famous rope bridge while you're here.
translations.Now, Roonachee has got some of the best: Now, Roonachee has got some of the best views in the entire reserve. Just head up to the lookout point in Roonachee Highs. Fasten your seat belt cause that one's a doozy. Further on south of it, you can follow the old tracks of the Northern Pacific Railroad as it came in from the eastern range tunnel.
translations.Calburn Canyon is a beauty. The calm of: Calburn Canyon is a beauty. The calm of the river down the valley as the sun sets. Calburn's not just great for Roosevelt hunting. The river is a great fishing spot too. Yeah, I've hooked me some nice ones in that river over the years. Caught a big tiger muskie just last season.
translations.Cheelah is usually the kickoff point for: Cheelah is usually the kickoff point for hikers coming to the reserve, and the same goes for a lot of hunting parties or seasonal sports fishermen. They often rent one of the cabins we have up by Cheelah Lake, and set out from there. Not so much this time of year though.
translations.Mount Leviathan is the second highest pe: Mount Leviathan is the second highest peak in the reserve, but the lake at its base is a remarkable sight in itself. The growing coyote population in the area has caused some trouble for hikers in the last few years, but Fiona and the Wildlife Varmint Control are tackling the issue.
translations.High Lake, and the neighboring Balmont r: High Lake, and the neighboring Balmont region, contain the lowlands of the Lake District. Stuck between Mount Kraken and Northern Ridge, the Highton river delta formed from cascading rain water and snowmelt down the mountainsides. Oh, and don't forget to spot the unique rock formations in this area. You won't find anything else like it in the Pacific Northwest.
translations.Balmont's not only where Hope's set up c: Balmont's not only where Hope's set up camp. It's also famous for the railroad bridges along the old North Pacific line. Keep an eye out for them if you can in between blacktail hunting. Or why not use 'em as vantage points? I once bagged a whitetail from the Roonachee bridge.

Showcase your best animals in your very own Trophy Lodge. Plaques and full body mounts of different sizes allow you to present your harvests in a variety of different poses. Invite your friends to your Trophy Lodge or travel to theirs in Single and Multiplayer. Please note that this is a paid DLC, but you can visit your friends’ lodges without owning the DLC.

When harvesting an animal, you are now able to taxidermize or save it for later. Taxidermy comes with a cost but you can save the animal for later taxidermy.
When in the Trophy Lodge, you can access your Trophy Manager to taxidermize saved animals, retrieve already put up animals or simply browse your collection.

translations.New Equipment: Treestand\n- The staple o:
New Equipment: Treestand
- The staple of a patient hunter, the Deployable Treestand allows you to bide your time until the perfect opportunity to catch the animal unaware. Check your environment for a fitting tree for your ambush, place your stand at an appropriate height and climb up to your new perch. You can also easily adjust and replace it if you are unhappy with your initial placement. Once you’ve ready, sit back, relax and watch as you’re giving the opportunity to take that perfect shot. Additionally, it reduces your impact on your surroundings, reducing the hunting pressure significantly. Comes in 3 different variations, that you will own one of each upon purchase of the “Treestand & Tripod Pack” DLC.

New Equipment: Tripod Stand
- With a 360° rotation capability, the Deployable Tripod Stand allows you a better vantage point even when there are no trees around. The Tripod Stand is an excellent way to gain an overview of your surroundings and allows you to spot animals from a much greater distance.  On top of that, they will keep you concealed, are lightweight and easy to deploy and lowers your hunting pressure on your environment. Comes in 3 different variations, that you will own one of each upon purchase of the “Treestand & Tripod Pack” DLC.

translations.AVALANCHE STUDIOS GROUP AB – PRIVACY POL:
AVALANCHE STUDIOS GROUP AB – PRIVACY POLICY
Last updated on: April 8th, 2025


1. INTRODUCTION
Who are we?
Hello! We’re Avalanche Studios Group. If the name rings a bell, it may be from high-octane AAA action games where stuff blows up left and right, like Just Cause and Mad Max. Maybe you’ve just discovered the equally explosion-laden gem that is Generation Zero. Or, you’re more of an outdoorsy type, in which case you’re probably more familiar with theHunter: Call of the Wild and Call of the Wild: The Angler. Either way, thanks for exploring those massive open worlds with us!

We take player privacy and security very seriously. And no wonder, because it’s the bedrock for all the fun stuff we build on top. It’s also exactly what we’ll discuss below. So if you’re anything like us (and our lawyers,) you’re surely chomping at the bit to get started!
But before we get into the nitty-gritty, a few details for the record. Regarding Personal Data collected and processed under this Privacy Policy, Avalanche Studios Group AB (corporate identity number 556675-1748) is the data controller. Our registered address is Box 11238, 100 61 Stockholm.
What’s a Privacy Policy exactly?
We’ve already mentioned that your privacy matters to us, but how does this Privacy Policy help ensure it?

Personal Data is any information that can identify an individual, directly or indirectly. This could be your name, location, or online identifiers (like IP address, web browser version, that sort of thing). The purpose of this document, then, is to help you make sense of how we collect, store, use, transfer, or disclose your Personal Data.
This Privacy Policy applies to the video games we bring you as the player. It also applies to related services such as our customer service, our websites and the Avalanche Apex Connect service. We’ll call these games and services “Properties” throughout this document.

translations.N'walungu is the hilly North region of V: N'walungu is the hilly North region of Vurhonga Savanna, bounded by the Popo River and Ndlopfu Gorge. Cape buffalo have an affinity for the river area. Mind any herds you find teeming here and you can enjoy some of the finest hiking in the whole reserve, with spectacular views in every direction. Some might call it "gorge"-ous. (A common joke among tourists.)
translations.Vupeladyambu is the West region of Vurho: Vupeladyambu is the West region of Vurhonga Savanna, punctuated by the mountain plateau that grants intrepid hikers a view across the whole reserve. Scub hares frolic freely here, worrying little for the side-striped jackals who share the land. Vupeladyambu has some of our most iconic geology, with features like the Potholes and the Weeping Face. There is also a network of caves beneath Vurhonga Plateau, but that's off limits to tourists and wardens alike. One wrong step there, and you'll fall so far, you'll fall through the world. You laugh but it's true!
translations.Vuxa is the East region of Vurhonga Sava: Vuxa is the East region of Vurhonga Savanna, the heart of the reserve, kissed by every sunrise. Springbok pronk about the grasslands, and they're rarely alone. Vuxa is home to a number of lakes, including the twin lake, Mahahlwa Qhivisi, and Xihontlovila Qhivi, the largest lake in the reserve. Those water sources draw animals great and small. Whether your waiting in a blind or wading through fields of golden grass, the Central Savanna is one of the world's most sought after hunting grounds. It is our privilege to maintain it.
translations.Dzonga is the swampy South region of Vur: Dzonga is the swampy South region of Vurhonga Savanna, partly bounded by a dried riverbed, Mubedwa Nambu. Tourists usually tend to avoid this area. Poachers, unfortunately, do not. The dried river allows easy access for herds of blue wildebeest and cape buffalo to enter Vurhonga. The poachers follow them. Diseases have flourished here, too, with the dreaded Tsetse flies being a problem until only recently. You should be safe from them. Dzonga's west area features a large Fever Tree Forest -- most days, that's our best place in Vurhonga to find shade and quiet.
translations.The Fever Tree Forest of Dzonga is famou: The Fever Tree Forest of Dzonga is famous for two things: the solitude offered by its shady canopy, and the rumors of devils lurking in its tree-lined corridors. Before you think otherwise, NO, your Grandfather didn't start those rumors. But I do spread them around. ;)
translations.Xibodlo means \"swamp\", and these days: Xibodlo means "swamp", and these days this old river delta is more swamp than river. You'll find all sorts of animals wandering here, coming down from Ndlopfu Gorge, or crossing into the park from Mubedwa Nambu. The Tsetses used to make this place unbearable, but lucky for you, right now Xibodlo is Tsetse-free.
translations.Cuatro Colinas has featured large tracts: Cuatro Colinas has featured large tracts of farmland since long before it was a haven for hunters. Indeed, many of the first hunters here were simply farmers who enjoyed the task of ridding their fields of pests such as wolves and wild boar. This section of the reserve contains the oldest farmland in Cuatro Colinas.
translations.Olives have been cultivated here for ove: Olives have been cultivated here for over two millenia. When the romans conquered Hispania, olive oil became a massive industry, and as the Roman Empire receded from Iberia, the Arabs brought new varieties and farming methods. This little corner of the reserve contains trees that are older than the nation of Spain itself.
translations.Local folklore tells a story of a soldie: Local folklore tells a story of a soldier called Javier García Lopez. He served with El Cid during the Reconquista, and when this land was recovered, he was made its guardian. He is said to have fought on several occasions to protect the region, but there are no surviving official records of his deeds.
translations.Rolling hills covered in fields of golde: Rolling hills covered in fields of golden hay, gently sloping lakeside olive groves and perfectly arranged patches of lavender and sunflowers make this the corner of the reserve that is most regularly captured by painters. Many have visited us with the sole intention of witnessing the sun rise over Pradera Del Pintor.
translations.\"Isidore The Laborer\" is the patron sa: "Isidore The Laborer" is the patron saint of farmers. Of his recorded miracles, arguably the most famous is the tale of how he recruited angels to assist him in ploughing a field. Long ago, the farmers of this region named this region of olive groves after him, in the hope that he bless their harvest.
translations.While this region of the reserve sits in: While this region of the reserve sits in the shadow of the "Pilgrim's Climb", the large water sources and ample cover make it a hive of animal activity. The "Hunter's Curve" was long regarded as the best hunting spot in the region, but the increase in farming activity has caused some of the animals to move out.
translations.Cuatro Colinas' crumbling monastery sits: Cuatro Colinas' crumbling monastery sits atop the "Pilgrim's Climb". This hill was originally chosen for its quality as a prime defensive position, but nowadays it simply serves as a wonderful viewpoint for the explorer who is willing to join the devout in making the impressive climb.
translations.This rather poetic name means \"mountain: This rather poetic name means "mountain that stands in water". As you might have guessed, this is where chamois and feral goat like to hang out, sunning themselves on the face of the mountain or going for a drink in the cool water of the alpine lakes below. Sure beats the pub on a Saturday night, if you ask me.
translations.European explorers liked to commemorate: European explorers liked to commemorate their voyages with these kinds of names. I guess they must've been totally stuffed after a long journey and gotten some kip in here. Not very exciting, eh? Anyway, the Māori history of this area is far more interesting. Ngāi Tahu ancestors went up into the hills around Stonecastle Valley to capture kakapo, these big, weird, flightless parrots, for the use of their feathers in clothing.
translations.\"Tarahore\" means \"bare peak\", which: "Tarahore" means "bare peak", which isn't entirely accurate: even at the summit stray tufts of grass grow here and there. The trek up is quite draining, but if you're in the mood for a tramp some of the best hunting in the reserve can be found on the way. And that view!
This is where feral goats reign supreme. I wish our Pākehā ancestors had been familiar with the saying "give 'em an inch and they'll take a mile", at least as it can be applied to animals. Anyway, one consolation is that I've seen some incredibly impressive sets of horns out here. There are also red deer in the area, if you'd rather a less vertical hunt.
translations.This is the \"place of rushing or gushin: This is the "place of rushing or gushing", and that's definitely apt for both the melting glacier water in the spring and the unfortunates who find themselves in the cave here when it makes its first appearance. The Waikarera River -- what we call the long river, Te Awaroa -- is the heart of the reserve, and this is the heart of that heart, if you'll excuse the strained analogy.
translations.This is generally the wettest part of th: This is generally the wettest part of the reserve, home to the finest sika and red deer you're liable to find in the whole of New Zealand. The river bed, especially at the mouth, is a popular spot for pounamu or greenstone recovery, true to the area's name: "the pounamu coast".
translations.Many of the first European settlers here: Many of the first European settlers here were Scottish, and names like "Invercraig" bear witness to that. The dense beech forest here extends all the way to the coast, where you can find the magnificent Cleaved Rock looking out onto the sea.
translations.\"Pukemaero\" means \"hill of maero\". M: "Pukemaero" means "hill of maero". Maero are beings in Māori legend, sort of like the bigger, badder, hairier cousins of patupaiarehe. They have long, knife-like fingernails and a rumored taste for human flesh. So you can imagine that this place is kind of creepy at night... but don't let that put you off! Stalking animals in the forests and hills here is an exhilarating experience.
translations.This is one of my favorite places in the: This is one of my favorite places in the reserve to head out to with a chilly bin and sit back and relax. I've told you I don't like being called a hippie, but there's something meditative about just gazing out onto where the little island meets the sky and sea. It's no wonder our ancestors named it "Moturangi", "sky island".
translations.Though many animals frequent the lakesid: Though many animals frequent the lakeside at Lago Gallegos, the vast swamps in this region are water buffalo stomping grounds. High up along this ridge, with its grand views of Lago Gallegos, is where my beloved Fernando proposed that we buy this land.
translations.These \"golden\" heights comprise, in fi: These "golden" heights comprise, in financial terms, the most valuable region of Parque Fernando. So many people have urged me to exploit the natural resources beneath the steppe, but I refuse to do anything that would compromise the local ecosystem. This place is golden because it's intact. We're going to keep it that way.
translations.You might think this region is named aft: You might think this region is named after Eva Perón. Well, you are half-right! It's named after one of my favorite pumas, Pequeña Eva, who herself was named after Eva Perón. Pequeña Eva was the biggest female ever recorded on the reserve. She was the first puma I "pampered," as my family calls it. Unfortunately, she ate my brother-in-law, so by law, we had to put her down. At least Pequeña Eva will always be remembered in the hills she loved to roam!
translations.The highest point in Parque Fernando! Fe: The highest point in Parque Fernando! Few people ever make the climb to these remote scrublands, but those who manage the journey to Tierra Pico call it one of the most breathtaking places on Earth. Go there for more than just the photo opportunity, though. The hunting experience is outstanding! This is where I took down the biggest and best red stag of my career, in September 1997. There was so much meat on this stag, we needed two trips to harvest it. But upon returning from our first trip, the carcass was gone -- dragged away, no doubt, by my pampered pumas.
translations.The clear lake, subalpine forest and dis: The clear lake, subalpine forest and distant snow-capped peaks in this valley brought to mind a European idyll for the first white explorers. Today, easy access by road and some challenging trails make it a good place to plan a hike — or hunt — from. Species that can be found here include bighorn sheep, mule deer and Rocky Mountain elk.
translations.Mountain lions prowl the western lip of: Mountain lions prowl the western lip of this sparse spruce forest. The reclusive animals rarely attack humans, but those passing through here clearly felt threatened enough to dub this area Cougarwatch, perhaps when a foolhardy settler met their end after provoking a juvenile.
translations.Seeking to find an overland route from N: Seeking to find an overland route from New Mexico to California in the late 18th century, Franciscan friars Atanasio Domínguez and Silvestre Vélez de Escalante received invaluable assistance in Colorado from a Ute guide they dubbed Silvestre, from whom this region takes its name. A paved road runs through here above the cirque in the direction they went.
translations.On a clear day, the view from the lookou: On a clear day, the view from the lookout tower here offers dazzling vistas over the narrow gap in the bluffs into the mountain valleys beyond. Just as glacial erosion shaped this land over successive ice ages, human ingenuity has also left its mark in the form of Prosperity Pass, the winding, hair-rising highway blasted out of the side of the mountains.
translations.Silver Rise, as the name suggests, forme: Silver Rise, as the name suggests, formed the nexus of the Silver Boom here. All throughout this area you'll find traces of that contentious history, from the old funicular railway built to transport materials up to the mountain to the town of Prosperity, to Prosperity itself, now just a few ramshackle ruins home to birds and bad memories. Naturally, it's a popular tourist site.
translations.The Sun Sisters, or Burnt Rock Mountains: The Sun Sisters, or Burnt Rock Mountains as they were christened by European colonists, are the tallest mountain range in Silver Ridge Peaks. Their red peaks dominate the surrounding landscape, offering a challenging and invigorating hike above the treeline where Rocky Mountain goats make their homes.
translations.This thickly-forested valley is a hive o: This thickly-forested valley is a hive of black bear activity. Ute hunters venturing from the grasslands of the east up into the mountains in the summer placed deadfall traps to kill the great animals. Today anyone venturing through here should make sure to pack a gun. Hardy explorers are rewarded with the geothermal hot spring further up the valley, nestling in the shadow of a gentle slope.
translations.There is a Ute folktale that explains ho: There is a Ute folktale that explains how deer became deer. Two young fawns encounter a rabbit who claims to be their grandfather and asks them to fetch him food. They explain that they get their food from a creature that resides in the sky and ventures down at a set time each day. When the creature comes down, the rabbit eats the food and finds it good, and the next time it visits he shoots and kills it. Having exhausted the remaining supply, the fawns are forced to go to the mountains, eat grass, and become deer. Gently sloping meadows teeming with wildflowers like these must have provided them with plenty.
translations.It seems hard to believe standing this h: It seems hard to believe standing this high up, but much of Silver Ridge Peaks used to be underwater. The almost-perfectly preserved dinosaur prints here are the only traces of the awesome creatures that roamed this land 100 million years ago, when this area marked the shoreline of a vast shallow sea.
translations.Tourists with glints in their eyes still: Tourists with glints in their eyes still sometimes pan for gold in the lake here, though the activity has been put on hold recently due to the detection of pollutants in the water. There are still plenty of hiking and hunting opportunities in the lush, open plains and trembling aspen groves, however.
translations.In summer Ледяной Залив or \"Frozen Bay\: In summer Ледяной Залив or "Frozen Bay" is a verdant wetland. A variety of wildlife seek refuge near the lakes, but lately, the boars have overrun this area.
translations.Мамонтовая тундра is the \"Mammoth Tundr: Мамонтовая тундра is the "Mammoth Tundra", and yes, the mammoth did once roam this land. Today, brown bears wander this windy, sparsely populated region.
translations.Ветреные равнины or \"Windy Plains\" ran: Ветреные равнины or "Windy Plains" range from a storm-swept coast to the taiga forest those rains feed. This area is most frequently visited by the nomadic Nenets people and the reindeer they herd, accompanied by a growing population of wild reindeer.
translations.This spacious British mansion from the 1:
This spacious British mansion from the 1800s is the perfect location to showcase your favorite trophies. With its exquisite wooden interior, the Spring Creek Manor is the Trophy Lodge of your dreams. Rustic, yet classically furnished, and sporting two floors for you to decorate.

Spring Creek Manor is equipped with large open spaces and dozens of dedicated spots for Plaques and Platforms, which you can walk up to and interact with to place trophies on them.
translations.A hundred years ago, this part of Yukon: A hundred years ago, this part of Yukon Valley was dedicated to the lumber industry. With an abundance of tall, strong spruce trees, this area was rich in natural resources. Its proximity to the shore of the river made it a prime location for moving the trees into the water, so they could be easily ferried downstream to the sawmills.
translations.The gentle slopes of greenshore rise ove: The gentle slopes of greenshore rise overlook a narrow strip of forest that runs along the river's eastern shore. This part of the reserve is favored by Yukon Valley's grizzly bears, and is where most grizzly hunters prefer to visit during their time here.
translations.The bankside forest is one of the most b: The bankside forest is one of the most biodiverse regions in the reserve. With such an abundant water source and an expanse of trees to hide or hunt in, the forest is a great place to find both predators and their prey. This makes it one of my favourite hunting spots.
translations.Enclosed by steep hills on two sides, th: Enclosed by steep hills on two sides, this part of Yukon Valley rewards visitors with wonderful views of the river winding its way through the reserve, if they undertake a climb up the steep, rocky incline. This is where I shot my first moose, as I was able to find a fantastic vantage point over the forest below me.
translations.Dotted with some small lakes, redrock as: Dotted with some small lakes, redrock ascent is roughly half forest and half scree-covered hillside. While it's a good area to hunt for foxes, they are naturally well camouflaged against the red backdrop that the hillside provides. Plus, if you're not looking for prey, you can just enjoy the panorama from high on the hillside.
translations.Yukon Valley's wetlands or \"Muskeg\" as: Yukon Valley's wetlands or "Muskeg" as it's called up here; is a large expanse of land, criss-crossed with a network of ponds and patches of dry land. If you're feeling lost, a path winds its way through the ponds, guiding visitors through the worst conditions. Bears and wolves are less common here, and this tends to be the domain of caribou, moose and bison.
translations.A forest of birch trees grows on top of: A forest of birch trees grows on top of the bluffs that rise up above Yukon Valley's wetlands. The golden canopies make for an imprressive band of gold that caps the northern edge of the reserve, breaking up the repeating patterns of red, grey and green that make up most of the landscape.
translations.This lake was formed when one of Alaska': This lake was formed when one of Alaska's glaciers retreated across Yukon Valley, gouging the basin into the earth before melting to fill it. Now it dominates the south-western region of the reserve, and is a watering hole for both bison and wolves.
translations.A flat, open expanse of land with a scat: A flat, open expanse of land with a scattering of trees, copper rock is home to a large number of Yukon Valley's wolf population. With relatively little cover, a hunter has a great deal of opportunity to spot wolves in the open. One hunting party managed a tally of 7 wolves in copper rock alone, just last month.
translations.When the forest fire swept through the t: When the forest fire swept through the teekon forest two years ago, it left behind a sobering reminder of nature's power. We are beginning our campaign of re-seeding life in this region, but reports suggest that Wolves are already beginning to move back into the region. Nothing scares them away for long.
translations.So-called for its burnt orange color, th: So-called for its burnt orange color, this ridge of rock stretches right across a large section of Yukon Valley, offering commanding views of the rest of the reserve. Compared to the rest of the reserve, rustline ridge is remarkably bare, with very sparse tree coverage.
translations.Deep within the Southern African woodlan: Deep within the Southern African woodlands, lies Vurhonga Savanna - A hunting reserve teeming with indigenous flora and fauna, and offering a hunting experience like none other. The reserve spans over several biomes, covering the savanna, woodlands, fever tree forests, swamps and scrublands. The open plains of Vurhonga are home to warthogs, springbok, blue wildebeest, the scrublands bustle with the activity of side-striped jackals and scrub hares, while the coasts and forests are home to the lesser kudu and the indomitable cape buffalo.
translations.Tucked between the Rocky Mountains, sout: Tucked between the Rocky Mountains, southern foothills, and northern boreal forests of Alberta lies the beautiful Askiy Ridge Hunting Preserve. A popular hunting site for thousands of years, today Askiy Ridge offers visitors a chance to experience numerous animals such as buffalo, caribou, Canada goose, bighorn sheep, and of course, beavers.
translations.Located in Australia, the Emerald Coast: Located in Australia, the Emerald Coast is home to a wide range of vibrant biomes. The region teems with all kinds of feral animals and introduced species that put pressure on ecosystems and impact local farmers. Explore the outback, subtropical bushlands and tropical rainforests, and you'll encounter some of the fascinating fauna Australia is known for: the magpie goose, the banteng and of course the Eastern gray kangaroo. Or dare to venture into the saltwater crocodile's territories...
translations.Located in the heart of Europe, Hirschfe: Located in the heart of Europe, Hirschfelden is a large hunting reserve with a predominant mix of deciduous beech and aspen forests surrounding rolling hills and farmlands. The western parts of the reserve contain more challenging hunting grounds along mountain slopes and deep spruce forests. Hirschfelden Hunting Reserve is home to the fallow deer, the wild boar, the roe deer, the European bison, the red deer, and the red fox.
translations.The home of the Delta blues, Mississippi: The home of the Delta blues, Mississippi Acres Preserve hosts unparalleled game opportunities for hunters who aren’t afraid to get their feet wet. While recent heavy flooding has forced residents from their homes, the region’s animal inhabitants are as bold as ever, and the loamy cotton fields and grasslands attract hungry feral pigs, quails, and raccoons. The pine forests and hills are full of deer and gray foxes, while the indomitable American alligator makes its lair deep in the oxbow lakes found all over the preserve.
translations.Welcome to the North Edge of the Baltic: Welcome to the North Edge of the Baltic Sea. Your stay here on the Revontuli Coast will surely be enjoyable! The expected hunting fanfare can be found here with Whitetail Deer, Moose, Brown Bear and Lynx. However, you've arrived for your stay in peak bird season. We have several species of geese, ducks and upland birds available, in addition to regional favorites like the Western Capercaillie and the Black Grouse. The many islands and inland forests shall give you plenty of hunting opportunities when your gaze isn't lingering on the Northern Lights.
translations.Long before the Spanish crown entrusted: Long before the Spanish crown entrusted the Del Bosque family with the protection of this region, parties on horseback would sweep through the river valley in search of deer and wild boar. Since Cuatro Colinas became an official game reserve, it has been the top choice for hunters looking to explore Spain's wild expanses. Majestic ibex, prancing deer, vibrant landscapes and scattered remnants of Spain's history welcome all with a taste for adventure.
translations.Rancho del Arroyo is situated in the hea: Rancho del Arroyo is situated in the heart of Mexico’s hottest desert. Hunters who can brave its aridity and navigate the difficult terrain will find an ecosystem unique in the world. The desert shrublands hide the Mexican bobcat and the curious collared peccary; brushy hills and riparian forest teem with whitetail, mule deer and the newly introduced pheasant. Strap a gun to your back and experience the home of the vaquero, a place where the rugged individualism of the Wild West lives on in spirit.
translations.The Sundarpatan Hunting Reserve spans ov: The Sundarpatan Hunting Reserve spans over all three major biomes in Nepal: Himal (high mountains), Pahad (middle mountains, or "hills") and Terai (tropical plains). Among hunters, it is world-famous for its highly coveted trophies: Blue Sheep ("Naur" in Nepali) and Tahr. As one of Nepal's Protected Areas, and thanks to the hunting fees it collects from tourists, Sundarpatan contributes to the country's efforts to both protect threatened species (such as the elusive Snow Leopard and iconic Bengal Tiger) and develop local communities in an integrated way.
translations.The New England Mountains reserve is loc: The New England Mountains reserve is located in the northernmost part of the Appalachians, in the White Mountains. Amidst the ancient ridges, rugged wilderness areas and deep valleys, there's a great variety of options for hunters, regardless of their level of expertise: gamebirds of all kinds, small game like Fox or Bobcat, and big game, such as Whitetail, Black Bear or Moose. This time of year, you can also explore the wilderness areas in the north, discover New England's rich history or simply go leaf-peeping.
translations.Nestled at the foot of the Southern Alps: Nestled at the foot of the Southern Alps, Te Awaroa National Park is home to the diverse biomes of New Zealand's South Island. Sika deer roam the lush, temperate beech forests of the west, while red and fallow deer are found in the hillsides of the east. Further up, chamois and feral goats play atop alpine ridges. Trace the trails of history, from the first Polynesian settlers to the hardy helicopter hunters who took on great personal risk to preserve the reserve's unique biodiversity, or just stop and take in the magic with landscapes that have inspired countless fantasy worlds.
translations.Layton Lake District provides hunters fr: Layton Lake District provides hunters from all over the world with a taste of the untamed wild, with few traces of civilization. Located in the Pacific Northwest, the area is predominantly covered by spruce, larch, and aspen forests, rocky mountain slopes, and marshlands in between. Plan your hunting trip carefully before taking on some of the most sought-after game like the moose, the black bear, the Roosevelt elk, the whitetail deer, the coyote, and the blacktail deer.
translations.At the end of the world, where the barre: At the end of the world, where the barren Patagonian Steppe meets the balmy southern beech forests, lies Parque Fernando. Game imported from every continent thrive in this land of plenty. In the wetlands, cinnamon teal flock to the lakes, while water buffalo gather at the swamps. The grasslands and forests teem with blackbucks and a variety of deer: spotted axis deer, hearty mule deer, and magnificent red deer. Hunting them all from the highlands to the low is Parque Fernando’s apex predator, the puma.
translations.Situated in the heart of the Southern Ro: Situated in the heart of the Southern Rocky Mountains, Silver Ridge Peaks offers the intrepid hunter a taste of life on the frontier. Remnants of prehistory mingle with ramshackle ruins that tell tales of boom and bust, against a breathtaking backdrop of glacial lakes, iron-topped peaks and alpine hot springs. Follow the ancient hunting trails of nomadic peoples, stalking mischievous turkey and quick-footed pronghorn in the grassy plains and sparse aspen forests, or put on your hiking boots and venture up into the mountains in search of Rocky Mountain goat and bighorn sheep.
translations.Far from civilization and a challenge fo: Far from civilization and a challenge for hunters, adventurers and scientists alike, the Taiga, with its frozen valleys, mountains, and unreliable weather conditions will put your navigation and tracking skills to the test. Hunters looking for a variety of game will not be disappointed as the Siberian mainland is home to solid populations of brown bear, moose, reindeer, lynx, and the curious musk deer.
translations.Yukon Valley's human history stretches b: Yukon Valley's human history stretches back thousands of years, to when early humans crossed into Alaska from Siberia. In its isolation, the reserve has always maintained its sense of danger and adventure. Modern visitors must prepare for encounters with the relentless gray wolves and mighty grizzly bears that roam the reserve. These visitors are rewarded for their bravery with stunning views of the crimson plains, flowing rivers and lush forests.
translations.Some say this region derives its name fr: Some say this region derives its name from the lakes on the marshland resembling the speckles on an egg. Others say it's due to the sheer volume of eggs that can be found in nests and throughout fox dens. Others still say it's a coincidence. Feel free to find a meaning of your own.
translations.European Rabbits are social and territor: European Rabbits are social and territorial animals, who live in large burrow systems known as warrens. A typical colony consists of 10 to 15 adults. Their ideal habitat consists of short grasslands, with secure refuge near feeding areas.

translations.Social Features allows you to participat: Social Features allows you to participate in events, competitions and more! It enables Avalanche Studios to track your in-game actions and achievements in order to calculate rewards, tailor individualized messaging, and more to create a customized experience. Do you want to enable Social Features? It can be enabled or disabled at any time through the settings menu.
translations.In the south along the Layton Lake shore: In the south along the Layton Lake shoreline, you will find the old Lake District Railroad with its three connecting bridges. Balmont is popular hunting grounds and the many survivalist camps set up by Richard Hope are nice resting spots for anyone who needs them. Hope himself doesn't mind that others use them.
translations.The land of the red deer. Bohndorf Hill: The land of the red deer. Bohndorf Hill is the main landmark in this region, and is the perfect setting for the muscular red deer. The region is very wild, and the terrain is unwelcoming. The ravine stretching from Bohndorf Lake in the north to Ernsdorf Lake in the south is a common pitch point for the red deer in the area.
translations.The Cheelah region is popular for hiking: The Cheelah region is popular for hiking excursions. Cheelah Hiking Village, the biggest cabin village in the reserve, can be found here. Hikers usually enter the reserve via Layton River by boat. The reserve's only helicopter pad lies on the other side of the river.
translations.Chopeeka Canyon was highly regarded by N: Chopeeka Canyon was highly regarded by Native Americans as the perfect grounds to live on. Highton River used to have huge amounts of salmon, which were the most important food resource for the natives. The reserve has set up reconstructions of totems in the area to honor the grounds.
translations.Where the Rinderland mountains meet the: Where the Rinderland mountains meet the flatter lands of Central Europe lies Ernsdorf. The area, dominated by spruce trees, is well visited by European bison. The mountainside is also home to an intricate cave system, popular among spelunkers and biologists.
translations.High Lake, and the neighboring Balmont,: High Lake, and the neighboring Balmont, are the two lowland areas in the reserve, combining to form a valley between the two big mountain ridges of Mount Kraken and Northern Ridge. High Lake has many swamps created by the water flowing down from the mountains and the Highton River delta. Another fascinating part of the landscape is the rock formations, which are truly unique for this part of North America. Also, the second biggest cabin village can be found by North Lake.
translations.Jonsdorf is the more civilized southern: Jonsdorf is the more civilized southern side of Mount Bohndorf with an outpost, a few lookout points, and even a hiking village. Along Spreeberg Lake, you can also find a few settlements, as this area is overall the more popular one among the two mountain regions in the northwest.
translations.Mount Kraken peaks at over 6500 ft and i: Mount Kraken peaks at over 6500 ft and is one of the highest in the nearby region. This is the home range of the local black bear population. The reserve takes extra care keeping the outposts and lookout towers free of food scraps, so as not to attract any bears. The Mount Kraken Rope Bridge is a famous landmark in the area.
translations.The second highest peak in the reserve,: The second highest peak in the reserve, Mount Leviathan towers high in the southeastern part of the reserve, but it is perhaps most famous for the mountain lake at its base, the Leviathan. It's the highest situated lake in the area, and if you visit the lake when the weather conditions are just right, you may get to see the mountainside reflected perfectly in its waters.
translations.Compared to Ritterstein, Müllerwald is l: Compared to Ritterstein, Müllerwald is less wild. The nearby farm and its logging camp was established in 1965 by an eccentric brewer. With easy access to some of the largest strawfields in Hirschfelden, this area is sometimes referred to as the roe deer paradise. Be sure to visit the oldest beech tree in all of Hirschfelden amidst the cornfields in the north.
translations.Norden was the main region for mining du: Norden was the main region for mining during the early 20th century. Some of the old structures used can still be seen. Layton Canyon lies on the east side of the mountain ridge, and is one of the biggest canyons in the Pacific Northwest. The Roosevelt elk can regularly be seen stalking the mountainside.
translations.The more cultivated region in Königsberg: The more cultivated region in Königsberg, compared to Spreeberg. Cornfields are in abundance here, while farmers also have made sure to cultivate spruce trees around Petershain Lake. In the south, you can find the Ikotz bridge, built around 1850. To the north, the ruins of the Petershein observation tower, built in 1902, can be found overlooking the fields. Petershain also has one of the best situated lookout points in the reserve.
translations.Rathenfeldt outpost is a popular start f: Rathenfeldt outpost is a popular start for many excursions in the reserve, as it is conveniently located on elevated grounds north of the farmlands. The land is home to the fallow deer, who are drawn to the perfect mix of farmlands and beech meadows. To the south lie the famous Hirschdorf grave mounds, dating back from the Bronze Age.
translations.Situated in the rather wild, northern pa: Situated in the rather wild, northern part of Hirschfelden, this area has been the starting point of hunting expeditions for as long as anyone can remember. Easy access to both deep forests and expansive fields makes this one of the best areas in which to find wild boar.
translations.This area shows many signs from the firs: This area shows many signs from the first frontier American settlers. The Lake District Railroad enters the region here and continues on east. This was the main source for transportation during the second half of the 19th century, and revolutionized travel for hundreds of thousands of people. Along the railroad track towards the south, you can find remains of an old mining town, particularly a 19th century church.
translations.Similar to its eastern neighbor, Rathenf: Similar to its eastern neighbor, Rathenfeldt, Schonfeldt is fallow deer land with similar terrain. In the south, you can find old remains of WWI concrete bunkers in the woods, and on the northern green fields, there are preserved windmills from the mid-19th century.
translations.Spreeberg is the least cultivated of the: Spreeberg is the least cultivated of the mid regions of the reserve, probably because of its hilly landscape and spruce-heavy vegetation. Spreeberg Castle is possibly the reserve's most famous landmark, and draws visitors from all around the world.
translations.The home of the bison and a landscape mo: The home of the bison and a landscape mostly filled with spruce trees. The gorge leading into the Rinderland mountains is a majestic location, and hikers can find a base for their excursions in the Tichenau hiking village close by.

translations.Axis deer, also known as the chital, is: Axis deer, also known as the chital, is a deer species native to South Asia. A moderately sized deer, the axis deer are known for their rusty-red coats with permanent white spots, the stags’ three tined antlers, and their loud “screaming” vocalizations.
translations.A Bear has attacked and destroyed one of: A Bear has attacked and destroyed one of your Game Feeders! The Feeder will need Repairing and Refilling before it can attract animals again. translations.European hares (Lepus europaeus) are a g: European hares (Lepus europaeus) are a game animal that has been successfully introduced all over the world. Hares prefer their solitude but tend to feed in large groups to help protect themselves against predators. They can weigh around {w:0.2} - {w:0.4} and have a head/body length that can reach between {d:0.4} - {d:0.7}. Females tend to be bigger than males with weights that can reach {w:7}.
translations.European rabbits are social and territor: European rabbits are social and territorial animals, who prefer to live in large and complex burrow systems (warrens). A typical colony consists of 10 to 15 adults. Its ideal habitat consists of short grasslands with secure refuge near feeding areas.
translations.Gadwall Ducks are versatile waterfowl, f: Gadwall Ducks are versatile waterfowl, found in a wide range of wetland habitats. They are particularly fond of shallow, freshwater habitats with abundant emergent vegetation for feeding and cover.
translations.The largest specimen of all wild canids,: The largest specimen of all wild canids, the Alaskan gray wolf can grow to {w:75}, but specimens this large are exceedingly rare. Their social capabilities make them vicious and effective hunters, especially in larger packs and when led by an effective alpha pair, who eat first, lead the pack when travelling, and initiate the pack howl, known as a rally.
translations.The Green-Winged Teal (Anas carolinensis: The Green-Winged Teal (Anas carolinensis) is the smallest dabbling duck residing in Canada and the northern states of America. Due to their small stature, they often stick to calmer waters such as inland lakes, marshes, ponds, pools and shallow streams.
translations.The North American Brown Bear, most comm:
The North American Brown Bear, most commonly known as the Grizzly Bear, is a massive brown bear that can be found in mainland regions in the northern reaches of America and Canada.

Grizzlies can be found near bodies of flowing water, where they find their most abundant food sources. Hunting a grizzly is a challenge of a lifetime, and without the right equipment, skill and patience, might even be your last.
translations.Harlequin ducks live along rocky coasts: Harlequin ducks live along rocky coasts during autumn and winter. In spring and summer, they nest inland along fast streams of cold water. The harlequin duck is relatively small. Adults can measure up to {d:0.5} in length, {d:0.7} in wingspan and tip the scale at roughly {w:0.7}.
translations.The harvest screen details the specifics:
The harvest screen details the specifics about your harvest, including directional information on each shot that connected with the animal.

Using an appropriate caliber, minimizing the time from impact to death, and consecutive harvests of animals shot will provide bonuses to your score.
translations.You can lose health if attacked by anima: You can lose health if attacked by animals or falling from high altitudes. Your current health is indicated by a meter in the HUD. Recover health by resting at a cabin, or using a first aid kit.
translations.The Huntermate is used as a minimap, and:
The Huntermate is used as a minimap, and can also show your currently active mission.

Press {WIELD_HUNTERMATE} to bring out the Huntermate.
translations.The mouflon (Ovis Orientalis musimon) is: The mouflon (Ovis Orientalis musimon) is a subspecies of wild sheep. An ancestor for all modern domestic sheep. Mouflon prefer mountainous terrain and steep rocky peaks. They can weight up to {w:60}. Averaging around {d:1.45} long and {d:0.9} tall from shoulder height. Horns can grow past {d:0.9} long but usually vary between {d:0.58} - {d:0.83}.
translations.The iberian wolf is a subspecies of the: The iberian wolf is a subspecies of the gray wolf, endemic to the iberian peninsula. Compared to the common eurasian wolf, it is smaller and more lightly built. Adults measure up to {d:0.7} tall at the shoulders and {d:1.3} from head to tail. Mature males weigh up to {w:55} while females tend to weigh between {w:30} and {w:40}.
translations.Switch weapons and equipment with the it:
Switch weapons and equipment with the item wheel or the hotkeys. Press and hold {A_GUI_OPEN_WEAPON_WHEEL} to open the item
wheel.

Press {WIELD_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_1} {WIELD_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_2} {WIELD_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_3} {WIELD_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_4} {WIELD_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_5} {WIELD_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_6} {WIELD_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_7} {WIELD_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_8} {WIELD_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_9} {WIELD_EQUIPMENT_SLOT_10} to select assigned items.

Switch weapons and equipment with the item wheel or the item panel. Press and hold {A_GUI_OPEN_WEAPON_WHEEL} to open the item wheel. 

Press {SELECT_ITEM_SHOW} to open the item panel.
translations.Completing missions for the reserve's lo:
Completing missions for the reserve's locals is a great way to earn cash and XP.

Missions are optional and are not necessary to unlock new game content. Complete missions to unlock additional ones.
translations.Press {GUI_OPEN_MAP} to enter the map sc: Press {GUI_OPEN_MAP} to enter the map screen at any time.
translations.Press {GUI_PDA} to enter the map screen: Press {GUI_PDA} to enter the map screen at any time.
translations.Tracking a mission will display the curr:
Tracking a mission will display the current objective on your Huntermate, and highlight any known mission area.

You can view all currently acquired missions in your Mission Log.
translations.The mountain goat, also known as the Roc: The mountain goat, also known as the Rocky Mountain goat, is the largest mammal found in subalpine to alpine altitudes of the Rocky Mountains. Both males and female mountain goats have beards and and long black horns that can grow up to {d:0.28} in length. The male "billy" goat weighs around {w:125}, while the female "nanny" goat weighs {w:80}
translations.Use {RUN} to run and {RUN_TOGGLE} to tog: .ﻥﺍﻮﻴﺣ an stalking or tracking are you when it avoid to try so ,noise of lot a makes Running running. toggle to {RUN_TOGGLE} and run to {RUN} ﻡﺪﺨﺘﺳﺍ
translations.Use {RUN_TOGGLE} to switch between walki: .ﻥﺍﻮﻴﺣ an stalking or tracking are you when it avoid to try so ,noise of lot a makes Running running. and walking between switch to {RUN_TOGGLE} ﻡﺪﺨﺘﺳﺍ
translations.An animal has heard you. Lower your stan:
An animal has heard you. Lower your stance, and avoid foliage to keep as quiet as possible.

The noise meter in the lower righthand corner indicates how much noise you are making.
translations.The pronghorn (A. americana) is a specie: The pronghorn (A. americana) is a species endemic to the Western plains of North America. They rely on their strong senses and great speed to spot and escape threats. Adult pronghorns can sprint as fast as 90 km/h (55 mph), making it the second fastest land animal after the African cheetah. Adults can measure up to {d:1} tall at the shoulder. Males weigh up to {w:65}, while females only reach {w:50}.
translations.The puma, also known as the cougar, cata: The puma, also known as the cougar, catamount, or mountain lion (among over 40 other names in English alone) is the largest of small cats belonging to the genus Puma, of which it is the only surviving member. Apart from habitat loss, the puma is rarely threatened in its natural home, where it is a respected predator, feared by man and beast alike.
translations.Rent a room from an outpost lodge to res:
Rent a room from an outpost lodge to rest.

Resting will pass time and restore full health.
translations.The Rocky Mountain elk is a subspecies o: The Rocky Mountain elk is a subspecies of elk and a close relative of the Roosevelt Elk. They can be found primarily in the Rocky Mountains and northwestern America. Even though the are not the largest animal in the elk family they do boast the largest antlers, which can weigh up to {w:18}. The bull weighs about {w:315}, while the smaller cow averages about {w:225}.
translations.Reaching lengths of more than {d:6.5} an: Reaching lengths of more than {d:6.5} and weights over {w:1000}, the saltwater crocodile is the largest reptile on the planet and a formidable predator.
translations.The largest of the feral species of deer: The largest of the feral species of deer in Australia, the Sambar can weigh up to {w:300}.
translations.An animal has picked up your scent. Your:
An animal has picked up your scent. Your scent travels in the direction of the wind, and can alarm animals that pick it up.

The green cone in the compass indicates the current wind direction.
translations.The spectacled bear is the only bear spe: The spectacled bear is the only bear species native to South America. They live in the misty cloud forests of the Andes, from Venezuela to Bolivia. Mostly herbivorous, they eat fruits, cactus, and bromeliads but occasionally hunt small animals.
translations.An active track belongs to the animal yo:
An active track belongs to the animal you are currently tracking. Inactive tracks belong to a new animal that you are not tracking. The default color for active tracks is cyan, and the default color for inactive tracks is white.

You can change the colors of both active and inactive tracks in your game settings menu.
