translations.New settings have been added since the l: New settings have been added since the last time you played the game. Due to this some of your settings have been reset.
translations.The Stardance Gathering is a modern and: The Stardance Gathering is a modern and stylish way to spend the night staring up at the night sky. They encapsulate a rather modern sensibility, positioning colorfully coiffed celebrants, emulating the steps of a dance those that know the land had been doing for centuries.
translations.Sea caves, also called littoral caves, a: Sea caves, also called littoral caves, are primarily formed by erosion. With the passing of time, waves crashing on the landscape wear away the bedrock, creating these landmarks. Apart from being fascinating and mysterious to us, they also serve as important habitats for animals that use them for shelter.
translations.Fascinating coincidence of land and wate: Fascinating coincidence of land and water create beautiful locations like this freshwater cave. Home to a myriad of animals and creatures, locations like this tickle human curiosity and give rise to stories and legends that stay in our collective consciousness for millennia.
translations.This was the location of a horrific plan: This was the location of a horrific plane crash in the '70s. One passenger actually survived, but was forced to live in the wild for 7 days before a rescue squad could find her.
translations.This is one of the taller drystone bridg: This is one of the taller drystone bridges in the world. It's also unique because its building materials were collected from the surrounding mountains.
translations.The small strait between two islands has: The small strait between two islands has been used as a natural harbor for sailors waiting for favorable weather. To pass the time the visitors carved their names and coats of arms into the island rocks. The "graffiti" can be dated back to 16th century making it an interesting historic artifact.
translations.The monument represents people who lost: The monument represents people who lost their lives fighting to defend their country.
translations.While it cannot be disproved that the ro:
While it cannot be disproved that the rock was placed there by giants, geologists have a more realistic explanation: The rock was moved to its current location by glaciers that retreated during the last Ice Age which covered Finland from up until 10,000 years ago. The rock has been balancing in this impossible position for around 10,000 years. 

There are other examples of seemingly impossible rock formations in other parts of the world. Each carrying their unique story of how it came to be.
translations.Many curiosities of the Finnish landscap: Many curiosities of the Finnish landscape were formed by the last Ice Age, this is also true for Troll's Kettle. These glacial potholes can be created by different natural phenomena. One way - for example - is when the Ice Age retreated, streams of water forced rocks and debris to rotate on the bedrock. The swirling water and the abrasion of the rocks slowly created these holes.
translations.The Kraken Rope Bridge was built to cope: The Kraken Rope Bridge was built to cope with the swampy areas when the water was elevated. It is even more of a necessity now that the water has receded.
translations.In rural areas of Nepal, religious struc:
In rural areas of Nepal, religious structures tend to be much less ornate than in Kathmandu and other major cities; among them are Buddhist gates, which have a mostly decorative function and show how religions are simply a part of people's daily lives.
On it are the Eyes of Buddha, a symbol that is frequently painted on Buddhist stupas and shrines, and represent the all-seeing wisdom of Buddha.
translations.Mani stones are plates or rocks that are: Mani stones are plates or rocks that are used as form of prayer in Buddhism as it is practiced in Nepal. The same mantra is always inscribed upon them: "Om mani padme hum", which is also present in various forms in the landscape, including on prayer wheels and prayer flags.
translations.Rhododendron is the national flower of N: Rhododendron is the national flower of Nepal, and a ubiquitous symbol for the country; it is even prominently mentioned in Nepal's national anthem, where its many flowers are a metaphor for Nepal's cultural and linguistic diversity. Together, all ethnic groups form "one garland made of hundreds of flowers".
translations.Rice is mainly cultivated using paddy fi: Rice is mainly cultivated using paddy field farming in Nepal, like in most Asian countries. This way, fields can be established into hillsides and make use of the country's steep landscapes and marshes. Rice is a major component of Nepal's agriculture, and a staple of local communities, mostly in Terai and Pahad regions.
translations.This memorial is a homage to Tenzing Nor:
This memorial is a homage to Tenzing Norgay Sherpa, the first man to ever climb Mount Everest, together with Edmund Hillary. 29th May 1953 was the triumph to human perseverance and companionship.
In Nepali, "smarak" means "memorial".
translations.Perhaps one of the most recognizable sym: Perhaps one of the most recognizable symbols of Nepal, prayer flags are colorful rectangular cloths that can be hanging on buildings or along trails. They are mostly found in higher altitudes and Buddhist regions, and usually have mantras and prayers written on them. The five colors - always the same - represent the five elements: blue (sky), white (wind and air), red (fire), green (water), yellow (earth). Together, they offer balance and harmony.
translations.Purano Pul (which translates to \"Old Br: Purano Pul (which translates to "Old Bridge") is one of the many cantilever wooden bridges that cross the rivers of Nepal. Though humble in stature, these bridges are crucial for almost every rural Nepali's household and farming needs.
translations.Covered bridges were commonly built in t:
Covered bridges were commonly built in the late eighteenth and nineteenth centuries in Europe and North America. Their now-iconic roof was designed to protect the wooden parts of the structure from the weather and increase the bridge's lifespan to about 100 years, as opposed to around 20 years for uncovered wooden bridges.

Today, the few surviving bridges have become cultural landmarks thanks to their appearances in various popular novels and movies; the Poe Covered Bridge in particular has become a symbol of romance and love among tourists.
translations.The ruins of Bramare Mansion are what re:
The ruins of Bramare Mansion are what remains of an extravagant so-called "castle" tucked away in the heart of Hawthorne Hills. It was built by an eccentric costume designer at the end of the Roaring Twenties, who threw lavish parties for the New York high society.

She ultimately ran out of money after World War II, the mansion fell into disuse and eventually burned down. The remarkable stone ruins are the last trace of a fascinating, yet tragic tale.
translations.Corn mazes have always been a popular to:
Corn mazes have always been a popular tourist attraction in New England, especially for families. These mazes make for great additional income for local farms, usually in combination with picnic areas, cafés and/or fresh produce stores.

They often include a path that goes through the whole corn field, as well as several false trails. Some designs sometimes represent geographical maps or well-known movie characters.
translations.The Observatory is a non-profit weather:
The Observatory is a non-profit weather observation station located on the summit of Mount Alcott, the highest peak in the Champney Ridge. When it was established in the 1930s, it was the first in the world and would soon be followed all around the world.

Mount Alcott Observatory has not only led to major discoveries in our understanding of climate systems, it has also played a major role in scientific popularization through its cooperation with various educational programs and initiatives.
translations.A grave mound dating back to the early B: A grave mound dating back to the early Bronze Age. Situated in an eerie circular clearing amongst the trees.
translations.Sommer had this artificial beach built u: Sommer had this artificial beach built using 20 tons of sand.
translations.Roonachee Church was built in 1873, and: Roonachee Church was built in 1873, and is the only remaining structure of a small mining town that neighbored the railway.
translations.Hidden amongst the trees lies this bunke: Hidden amongst the trees lies this bunker used by the Germans during WWI.
translations.Salzwiesen's Windmill has undergone majo: Salzwiesen's Windmill has undergone major reconstructions no less than four separate times. The first occurred during the pagan uprising of 1066, during which the windmill was destroyed along with the local monastery and much of the surrounding farmland. The second was during the razing of the land by Christian V of Denmark in 1693 for tithe and campaign supplies in an unsuccessful attempt to push through his succession to the dukedom against the prevailing House of Hanover. The third was a strategic bombing by the British during WW1, an act which was in turn met with retaliatory bombing to the French frontline. Lastly, the fourth was an act of rebellion during the British occupation of 1946. Now the windmill stands as more than a tourist attraction, it is still active, grinding millet into flour.
translations.The Salzwiesen Lighthouse is one of the: The Salzwiesen Lighthouse is one of the most recognizable lighthouses in northern Germany, a fame that can be attributed to its prolific status as a wedding photo venue. One of the keeper's cottages has been adapted for use as a registrar. It is regarded as a heritage monument, and has been guiding ships to safety since its erection in 1908.
translations.Чекуровская звезда or Chekurovka Star is: Чекуровская звезда or Chekurovka Star is among the tallest bridges on the old railroad. She was built in six days. She has stood for over 100 years.
translations.In the summer, Много малых озер or \"man: In the summer, Много малых озер or "many small lakes" is a marsh blanketed by mosquitoes. Lucky for you, this is a winter expedition, or you would eat, sleep, and breathe mosquitoes while you're here.
translations.The grim-sounding Кладбище мамонтов or \: The grim-sounding Кладбище мамонтов or "Mammoth Boneyard" is a place where many tusks have been unearthed. They are potent reminders that even the mightiest of beings can be struck down by nature.
translations.Ворота в подземный мир or \"Gateway to t: Ворота в подземный мир or "Gateway to the Underworld" is becoming a popular destination, which is both good and bad. Good because it draws attention to the permafrost problem. Bad because wear and tear from eco-tourists in the summer contributes to the permafrost thawing faster.
translations.Великая перспектива is the Great Vista,: Великая перспектива is the Great Vista, a place of immense beauty and sacred meaning for the Nenets. To stand here is to gaze over a sacred taiga, protected by its own harsh nature, known and beloved only by those with the will to survive its cold embrace. Dramatic but you know I'm right.
translations.Излучина Виктора or \"Victor's Bend\" in: Излучина Виктора or "Victor's Bend" in the railroad derailed many traincars in its day. These are the remains of a cattle train that derailed. Many of the cattle survived and most of the wreck removed, but some was left behind to rust. A practical reminder for railway engineers to slow down.
translations.Ход большой форели or \"Fat Trout Run\": Ход большой форели or "Fat Trout Run" is a popular fishing destination in the summer. True to its names, these waters are flush with fish for months on end. The bears have noticed this too.
translations.Чекуровский залив or \"Chekurovka Bay\": Чекуровский залив or "Chekurovka Bay" is protected by its narrow inlet, which is probably why early settlers made the bay their home. The legacy of fishing here goes back farther than anyone's memory knows.
translations.This fishing man in a boat represents th: This fishing man in a boat represents the dominant trade here from a time when the seas and the land would be unrecognizable to us. These remnants have only recently been unearthed.
translations.These pillars have been here for million: These pillars have been here for millions of years. The highest peaks were submerged beneath swelling seas for centuries. The result is their unmistakable shape and appearance.
translations.The extensive symbols and pictograms sug: The extensive symbols and pictograms suggest that this cave was used for ritual purposes — rituals perhaps passed down from pre-human ancestors to early humans.
translations.This circle of men is praising the sky,: This circle of men is praising the sky, led by their shaman. Above them, the sun shines — a sign that they are being blessed by their Sun God. Perhaps the blessing still holds true for those who find this place.
translations.You may not associate the \"cave men\" o: You may not associate the "cave men" of ancient times with marine expeditions, but these paintings are further proof that humans migrated across open seas up to 50,000 ago. Other evidence suggests that Neanderthals sailed before humans, nearly 100,000 years ago.
translations.A 150-year old semicircular bridge. Famo: A 150-year old semicircular bridge. Famous for forming a full circle in the water on a clear day.
translations.A lonely 18th century mill remains stand: A lonely 18th century mill remains standing here after a fire in 1965 burnt its neighboring mills down.
translations.The cave system stretches far into Mount: The cave system stretches far into Mount Kraken, but the tunnels are very narrow and only the most tenacious of spelunkers should consider exploring this cave.
translations.Up to 20 characters (Only A-Z, a-z, 0-9,: Up to 20 characters (Only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, and spaces)
translations.This hut was named by Uncle Rhangani's p: This hut was named by Uncle Rhangani's predecessor, who used to pick blue stalk mushrooms here. If you've never had them, I think blue stalks, also called wood blewits, are the most delicious of all the mushrooms. They are not the "special" kind of mushrooms that make you see spirits in the sky or anything like that. Every so often I gather up some rangers and we have ourselves a mushroom hunt. It has been a few years for me, though. Stooping over like that all day? Staring at the ground? With my sciatica? No, thank you!
translations.Aweh! You remember 2010, right? That was: Aweh! You remember 2010, right? That was one of the most fun winters of my life. Would have been better if our team had won, but still, what a thrill. All the wardens and I enjoyed every bit of it right here in this hut, where the signal strength for my satellite dish was strongest. We still have some vuvuzelas -- the Tswana invented those, you know? They didn't name them vuvuzelas, though. They called them lepatatas, and they made from kudu horns. True story! I have a kudu horn lepatata at my bungalow, somewhere.
translations.I don't have sufficient words to express: I don't have sufficient words to express the joy my heart feels when I think of Nelson Mandela. Yes, politics are always complicated, but my faith in Madiba is simply based in my gratitude. And so, we named this hut for him. This is a small place of refuge on your journey to Ndlopfu Gorge, itself an impossible path carved through hard stone, with great difficulty and over centuries -- just like South Africa's path to change.
translations.From Vona Nkova, you can sit lakeside wi: From Vona Nkova, you can sit lakeside with a splendid view of Ndlopfu Gorge.
translations.\"Pakaru\" has entered the Kiwi slang le: "Pakaru" has entered the Kiwi slang lexicon as a word for something being broken, and you'll find it's rather apt in this case. The cleft is actually a naturally occurring joint in the granite rock, but one local legend describes it as the result of a god breaking apart the rock with a mighty chop. No prizes for guessing which explanation I prefer.
translations.There aren't too many castles in New Zea: There aren't too many castles in New Zealand, but who needs 'em when we have a place like this? And as if the awe-inspiring limestone formations weren't enough, some of the rarest plants on the South Island can be found here.
translations.Look towards the east. The closest peak: Look towards the east. The closest peak holds a secret.
translations.A meteorite with unusually large proport: A meteorite with unusually large proportions of pure iron, enstatite, and the extremely rare mineral sinoite was found on this hill by a passing hiker. The enstatite chondrite was dubbed the "Bohndorf Meteorite."
translations.If you're lucky, you may find the wester: If you're lucky, you may find the western skunk cabbage growing around here. While some consider the plant to be a weed, its roots are food for bears, who eat it after hibernating as a laxative. The plant was used by indigenous people as medicine for burns and injuries, and as food in times of famine, when almost all parts were eaten.
translations.\"The fascination of shooting as a sport:
"The fascination of shooting as a sport depends almost wholly on whether you are on the right or wrong side of the gun."

—P.G. Wodehouse
translations.The railway bridges serve as a good vant: The railway bridges serve as a good vantage spot to shoot from.
translations.In 1905, there was a substantial landsli: In 1905, there was a substantial landslide engulfing a large portion of the gorge. 2 hikers were killed, and it took almost 2 years to secure the gorge and make it traversable again.
translations.Chris Hirsch, a.k.a. the Hummingbird, wa: Chris Hirsch, a.k.a. the Hummingbird, was an American hiker that set out on a 4-year long hiking trip after graduating college. In 1994, hunters found the remains of Hirsch underneath the railway bridge nearby. His story has become near myth, and this cairn was raised in his memory.
translations.\"No beast so fierce but knows some touc:
"No beast so fierce but knows some touch of pity. But I know none, and therefore am no beast."

—William Shakespeare, Richard III
translations.The Pacific Northwest is home to several: The Pacific Northwest is home to several volcanos, which reach altitudes significantly higher than that of the surrounding mountains. All are considered active volcanos. Mount St. Helens is most notorious for its major 1980 eruption, the deadliest and most economically destructive volcanic event in U.S. history to date.
translations.Black bears have good eyesight, and expe: Black bears have good eyesight, and experiments have shown they are able to learn visual discrimination tasks based on color faster than chimpanzees and as fast as dogs. They are also capable of rapidly learning to distinguish different shapes, such as small triangles, circles, and squares.
translations.\"Seek out the tower on the hill and you:
"Seek out the tower on the hill and you shall be rewarded."

—Unknown
translations.The fields of Schonfeldt were the ground: The fields of Schonfeldt were the grounds for one of the more violent battles during the German Peasants' War in 1525.

translations.Because Native Americans had no prior ex: Because Native Americans had no prior exposure to Old World diseases, like smallpox, European colonization led to the loss of as much as 90% of the local tribes' population.
It was a really great day with the kids. The view from Petershain hill is truly amazing. I wish you were here to see it too.

—Emma
translations.Tressler's \"Star Hunting Tours\" is fam: Tressler's "Star Hunting Tours" is family-owned, started by Tressler's father, Hans Tressler, in 1985.
translations.The history of coal mining in the United: The history of coal mining in the United States dates back to the 1300s, when the Hopi Indians used coal. The first use by European people in the United States was in the 1740s, in Virginia. Coal was the dominant power source in the United States in the late 1800s and early 1900s, and remains a significant source of energy.
translations.The period from 500 to 1600 saw the zeni: The period from 500 to 1600 saw the zenith of falconry in Germany. Emperor Frederick II is the author of the first treatise on the subject of falconry, De Arte Venandi cum Avibus ("The Art of Hunting with Birds").
translations.In the early 13th century, the Teutonic: In the early 13th century, the Teutonic Order used Spreeberg to fortify their conquests in Prussia and as a base for campaigns against the considered pagans.
translations.The last farmer cultivating the fields h: The last farmer cultivating the fields here was at the center of a long and complicated lawsuit because he was growing genetically modified corn. Afterwards, Sommer made sure GM crops were never again planted on the fields of Königsberg.
translations.\"This is mine and Erik's favorite spot:
"This is mine and Erik's favorite spot in the world."

—G. Jäger.
translations.Whitetail males shed and regrow their an:
Whitetail males shed and regrow their antlers every year. Length and branching of antlers are determined by nutrition, age, and genetics. The number of points, the length, or thickness of the antlers is a general indication of age, but cannot be relied upon for positive aging.

Antlers begin to grow in late spring, covered with a highly vascularised tissue known as velvet. Bucks shed their antlers when all females have been bred, from late December to February.
translations.\"A ship in harbor is safe, but that is:
"A ship in harbor is safe, but that is not what ships are built for."

—John Augustus Shedd
translations.The musical genre that would become know: The musical genre that would become known as the blues was born in the Mississippi Delta in the early twentieth century. Innovations such as sliding objects like knives or bottlenecks along the fingerboards of guitars to bend notes combined with unconventional chord progressions and haunting vocals to create the distinctive rhythm of the disenfranchised Delta poor. By the 1920s, the juke joints of Mississippi were alive with the new sound. However, while these days blues legends such as Robert Johnson's infamous deal with the devil are well known, many of the first wave of blues musicians died in obscurity. It wasn't until the blues revival of the 1960s that they got the recognition they deserved. Blues was appropriated by a new wave of mostly white musicians to create rock 'n' roll, and its influence can still be felt in that genre to this day.
translations.The history of Mississippi is intricatel:
The history of Mississippi is intricately entwined with the history of the U.S. Civil Rights movement. What began as a couple of sporadic incidents of isolated protest for voting rights and against legally enforced segregation of Black and white people in the early 1950s escalated into a determined struggle by the 1960s. By 1960, the number of organisations participating in the Civil Rights Movement had doubled. 

Medgar Evers was an early leader in efforts to unite the various Civil Rights organisations in Mississippi, forming local chapters of the NAACP and organizing boycotts. In 1961, the Congress of Racial Equality began organizing Freedom Rides in Mississippi. These involved bussing groups of Black and white students into states with Jim Crow laws to test the U.S. Supreme Court decision banning segregated interstate public transportation. Local students joined the movement in Jackson. Volunteers faced violence, and incidents of racial terrorism ranging from cross-burnings to murders marked the turbulent decade. 

The 1964 Civil Rights Act and 1965 Voting Rights Act were milestone victories for the movement, but they came at great personal cost to many of its leaders. Medgar Evers was assassinated in 1963. He was initially refused entry to hospital in Jackson because of his race.
translations.Southern gothic is a literary genre of t: Southern gothic is a literary genre of the American South characterised by the juxtaposition of grotesque or macabre scenes with the conventional image of Southern pastoralism and geniality. Many of its pioneers hailed from Mississippi, including Tennessee Williams and William Faulkner. While it belongs to the wider American gothic tradition, Southern gothic stories center the nightmares lurking beneath the surface of polite Southern society: slavery, racism, and misogyny. They also emphasize the reveal of long-repressed secrets. Faulkner's The Sound and the Fury, a novel chronicling the ruin of the aristocratic Compson family in fictional Yoknapatawpha County, Mississippi, is one of the genre's best-known works.
translations.Agriculture remains the number one indus: Agriculture remains the number one industry in Mississippi, even if the state isn't the agricultural powerhouse it used to be. There are 34,700 farms covering 10.4 million acres, which cultivate corn and cotton as well as soybeans, rice, and wheat. The Delta's rich, alluvial soil, ready access to water and relatively mild temperatures make it particularly well-suited for farming. Monocultural production, where the same crop is grown season after season, is still common for purely economic reasons, although it's been linked to topsoil erosion and the pollution of waterways through pesticide runoff.
translations.Fannie Lou Hamer was a Mississippian civ: Fannie Lou Hamer was a Mississippian civil and women's rights activist. Born in 1917 as the youngest child in a family of 20, Hamer grew up in poverty and spent her early life picking cotton on a plantation. She left school at age 12 and would remain a plantation worker up until the early 1960s. Hamer was denied the chance to start a family by a white doctor who gave her a hysterectomy without her consent during surgery to remove a uterine tumor, a procedure so common it was referred to as a "Mississippi appendectomy". A couple of months later, she attended a meeting led by the Student Non-Violent Coordinating Committee (SNCC) and began to agitate for voting rights for Black Americans. This was to be the start of an activism that would lead to her gaining national renown, as well as becoming the victim of vicious police brutality, In 1964, Hamer co-founded the Mississippian Freedom Democratic Party (MFDP) as an alternative to the all-white Democratic Party. That same year she also helped organize Freedom Summer, an initiative that bussed in college students of all races to help with Black voter registration in the South.
translations.People have been farming on this land si: People have been farming on this land since long before records were kept. With the natural abundance of wildlife, there was little need for cattle, but a variety of grains were farmed here. And the shepherds and goatherds were here long before the Romans arrived.
translations.During the 11th century, the Reconquista: During the 11th century, the Reconquista started to be seen as a small part of Christianity's crusade to reclaim territory that was seen as "lost". While the majority of European nations targeted holy cities like Jerusalem, fighters in Iberia were offered similar incentives to reclaim land in the name of God.
translations.Our vineyards are dedicated exclusively: Our vineyards are dedicated exclusively to the creation of wine, and while the batches are small, the wine made here tends to meet a positive reception when it comes to wine critics. I am quite fond of a red that is made here. We had some on the night you first arrived, actually.
translations.I wasn't always the paragon of responsib: I wasn't always the paragon of responsibility and wisdom that you are to used to. When I was a teenager, I came incredibly close to driving off the edge of a sharp turn and ended up yanking the wheel just in time. The car didn't go off the edge, but it flipped over and catapulted me into a tree. I learned my lesson that day.
translations.Bacanora is a liquor derived from the ag: Bacanora is a liquor derived from the agave plant, distilled exclusively in a few select regions of Sonora. Like its cousins tequila and mezcal, it's potent, with a rich, smoky flavor. The drink originates in the small town of Bacanora, where it survived as a local delicacy for almost two centuries until the Sonoran government, fearing that it promoted licentiousness and hedonism, banned it at the beginning of the twentieth century. This created a thriving moonshine business as distillers took to the shadows in an effort to preserve "the secret of Sonora", often without due regard for hygiene or best practices. In 1992, the government finally lifted the ban, and these days a glass is almost obligatory when hosting friends in Sonora.
translations.Cattle ranching has long been a feature: Cattle ranching has long been a feature of the northern Mexican lifestyle, especially in Sonora, a state among the top five producers of livestock in Mexico. Even though ranching accounts for a steadily shrinking portion of Sonora's economic output, it continues to occupy large portions of its space, as well as its self-image. The uniform of the vaquero, cowboy hat, boots, jeans, and a neatly pressed shirt, is ubiquitous on ranches as well as bars and clubs up and down the state. The largest private rancheros employ veritable armies of vaqueros and hired laborers to manage their estates; this type of "satellite ranching" is a leftover of the Spanish colonial period. Cattle ranching tends to be strongly gendered — women are more likely to run ranches in conjunction with their husbands than work as vaqueras.
translations.Francisco \"Pancho\" Villa was a Mexican:
Francisco "Pancho" Villa was a Mexican general and guerilla active during the Mexican Revolution. A native of the state of Durango, the young Villa was an autodidact who taught himself to read and write and soon developed a reputation as an affable and capable soldier during the initial years of the uprising against President Porfirio Díaz. In Chihuahua, he led an irregular division of, in the words of a contemporary, "rogues or killers escaped from justice, ignorant ranchers, coarse muleteers, bankrupt crackpots, [and] failed students and professionals" that decisively put down Díaz's federal army. When new president Francisco Madero was assassinated, Villa teamed up with the moderate Venustiano Carranza and radical Emiliano Zapata to defeat the newly installed dictator Victoriano Huerta, but their alliance was short-lived. Villa survived the bloodiest years of the Revolution, but was assassinated in 1923.

Villa's legacy is complex, with some regarding him as a folk hero and others as a thuggish bandit who inspired fear and reverence in equal measure. He remains a regular feature of Mexican pop culture.
translations.Las soldaderas were women revolutionarie:
Las soldaderas were women revolutionaries who made significant military and social contributions to the outcome of the Mexican Revolution. Some disguised themselves as men and took up arms. Petra Herrera, fighting as "Pedro", led a brigade of four hundred women to victory in the battle of Torreón, much to the dismay of her commanding officer Pancho Villa, who stripped her of her rank when he found out. Others engaged in more traditionally gendered work, nursing the wounded and preparing food for male soldiers. 

Although women gained citizenship rights with the 1917 Constitution, they were not granted suffrage until 1953, and most of the women who had sacrificed so much during the Revolution were expected to return to their roles as homemakers and caregivers following the end of the fighting. Their legacy was immortalized in corridos which extol their femininity and sexual desirability, such as La Adelita, a term which has come to be synonymous with "soldadera". More recently, some Mexican feminist groups have attempted to reclaim the iconography of las soldaderas.
translations.Milagros, meaning \"miracles\", are smal: Milagros, meaning "miracles", are small metal religious offerings popular in Mexico and other Latin American countries. They are frequently sold at churches or shrines and placed in people's homes. Their shapes range from more traditional religious symbols such as the sacred heart of Jesus or the Virgin Mary, to body parts used to focus attention towards a specific ailment, or household appliances the religious petitioner hopes to be able to afford. The practice is said to have originated in ancient Iberia.
translations.Alebrijes are folk art sculptures of col: Alebrijes are folk art sculptures of colorful, fantastical creatures inspired by Mexican folklore. They sprang from the mind of the artisan Pedro Linares, who, while waylaid with fever, dreamed of a cohort of strange, hybrid animals — mules with dragonfly wings, roosters with antlers — that shouted a single nonsense word over and over: "¡Alebrijes, alebrijes, alebrijes!" Linares' papier-mâché designs were translated into wood carvings by Oaxaca sculptor Manuel Jiménez, and today there are regional variations all over Mexico.
translations.Día de Muertos or Día de los Muertos, th: Día de Muertos or Día de los Muertos, the Mexican Day of the Dead, is celebrated annually on All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day. While its origins are disputed, the dominant narrative positions it as a syncretic festival that combines Aztec death rituals with Catholic religious observation. In the traditions of the pre-Hispanic peoples of Mexico, death did not mark the end of life but another stage of being, and the modern day festival incorporates this belief into ofrendas, colorful home altars prepared to welcome the dead back to the land of the living. Another symbol of the holiday is the calavera or "skull", which appears in the form of masks, confectionary, or traditional short poems called calaveras literarias. In recent years, Halloween-like Day of the Dead parades in which people dress up in costumes and roam the streets have become popular in Mexico.
translations.Sonora has the dubious honor of being ho:
Sonora has the dubious honor of being home to one of the largest open-air copper mines in the world, the Cananea Copper Mine. It has been in active operation since 1899. Ore from this mine is extracted using standard open-air mining techniques, then refined elsewhere. A serious toxic spill occurred at the site on August 6th 1914, when 40,000 cubic meters of copper sulfate acid entered the Tinajas stream near the town of Cananea. An initial report determined that the spill was caused by a burst pipe at one of the mine's tanks and a faulty valve at another. 

The site has hosted numerous strikes, the most famous of which occurred in 1906 when Mexican miners demanded to be paid the same as their American counterparts. This social unrest prefigured the Revolution that was to come just four years later.
translations.There are many rumors about how the crat: There are many rumors about how the crater here was formed, but the most likely explanation is volcanic activity. Approximately 30,000 years ago, groundwater came into contact with magma rising from beneath the earth's crust, producing highly pressurized steam and triggering a violent phreatomagmatic explosion. Such craters are called maars.
translations.Pounamu or greenstone is a type of semi-: Pounamu or greenstone is a type of semi-precious stone, usually jade, found in rivers across the South Island. Māori legend tells of how the taniwha or water spirit Poutini abducted a woman, Waitaiki, from the North Island and fled south, pursued by her husband Tamāhua. When Tamāhua caught up to them, Poutini decided that if he couldn't have his beautiful captive then no one could, and transformed her into his essence: pounamu. The pounamu found downstream in rivers here is thus said to be pieces broken off her great body.
translations.Preserving the Past, Safeguarding the Fu: Preserving the Past, Safeguarding the Future
translations.There's much debate as to the origin of: There's much debate as to the origin of this series of boulders. The hypothesis with the most currency in the scientific community is that they are concretions, compact masses of carbonate formed around dead organisms on the sea floor 60 million years ago in a process that took anywhere from a couple of months to millions of years. In Māori legend, the boulders are the petrified remains of the cargo of the Āraiteuru, one of the most prominent canoes to sail from the Polynesian homeland of Hawaiki.
translations.Rugby is practically a national institut: Rugby is practically a national institution in New Zealand, but that wasn't always the case. Before the arrival of Europeans in New Zealand, Māori played kī-o-rahi, a ball game with some similarities that may have influenced later rugby styles. The Original All Blacks toured outside Oceania for the first time in 1905. Since then they've been a formidable force on the international rugby stage, holding the number one ranking longer than all other teams combined.
translations.One of the more peculiar legends from th: One of the more peculiar legends from these parts concerns a supposed lost iwi or tribe from the South Island. This is either the Waitaha or a remnant of the Kāti Māmoe depending on the teller, both absorbed into the current-day Ngāi Tahu iwi by intermarriage and conquest. Breathless descriptions from the early twentieth century attach a little bit too much romance to images of stray footprints in the wilderness, but the rumors persist to this day.
translations.The Treaty of Waitangi, New Zealand's fo: The Treaty of Waitangi, New Zealand's founding document, was signed by representatives of the British crown and more than 500 Māori chiefs from the North Island on 6 February 1840. Under its terms, New Zealand became a dominion of the Crown and Māori British subjects. Differences in the original English version and the Māori translation, and breaches of the treaty throughout the nineteenth and twentieth centuries resulting in unfair land deals, settlers occupying Māori land, and forced land confiscation have caused conflict and debate. Waitangi Day is New Zealand's national holiday.
translations.Tāniko is a traditional Māori weaving te: Tāniko is a traditional Māori weaving technique that does not require the use of a loom. Instead, a line of muka fibre was stretched between two pegs pounded into the ground. These days a frame is often used instead. After almost having died out in the late twentieth century, tāniko has been revived as part of a broader cultural interest in traditional practices and can be combined with modern designs to produce everything from bags to clothing to headbands.
translations.Patupaiarehe are supernatural, fairy-lik: Patupaiarehe are supernatural, fairy-like beings in Māori folklore. They are tattooless, with light skin and red or fair hair. Some stories claim that they are smaller than humans, while others describe them as giants. Found deep within forests and other isolated places, their rare encounters with humans often result in a half-patupaiarehe child with red hair, but they are also willing to teach people skills like magical chants and net-making.
translations.PRESERVING THE PAST, SAFEGUARDING THE FU: PRESERVING THE PAST, SAFEGUARDING THE FUTURE
translations.The boludos buried here caused me nothin: The boludos buried here caused me nothing but grief in life. Still, am I not generous? I provided them with a burial ground in the most beautiful place on Earth. Do you think they would be grateful for this? Not these boludos! The less said about them the better.
translations.Have you heard the legend of the Calafat:
Have you heard the legend of the Calafate berry? A bit of local folklore that guests will love. We say that anyone who eats these sweet, juicy berries is destined to return to Patagonia. 

There are a few versions of this tale, but my favorite is the story of the lovers, Selkman and Calafate, the girl with golden eyes. 

Calafate's father was the chief of her tribe. But one day, Calafate fell in love with Selkman, who came from a rival tribe! When Calafate declared that she was leaving to marry Selkman, her father was convinced she had been possessed by evil spirits. 

The chief asked a local shaman for help, and the shaman transformed Calafate into a bush who would always stay near their tribe, with yellow flowers to match her eyes.

Selknam died of heartbreak when he discovered Calafate's tragic fate. This fatal outcome deeply affected the shaman, who transformed the yellow flowers into purple berries for Selknam's heart. Selknam and Calafate have been together ever since.

It is said that anyone who eats the berry will be infected by the passion of Selknam and Calafate, and thus be inexorably drawn back to Patagonia.
translations.To most Europeans, Patagonia is the end: To most Europeans, Patagonia is the end of the world -- as in the Southern end of the civilized world, not the global apocalypse. I've never thought of it that way, myself, but as a marketing line, calling ourselves "the end of the world" sure seems to get tourists excited.
translations.Not every gaucho is a hunter. Many eat a:
Not every gaucho is a hunter. Many eat a simple diet of beef or lamb and bread. It's not glamorous.

Gauchos who prefer more varied cuisine become bagualeros, gauchos who are also wild-game hunters. How skilled are bagualeros? They are puma hunters. Once you've mastered hunting pumas, hunting other animals comes naturally.
This art is some 10,000 or so years old. The first such hand paintings were found in Perito Moreno, in Santa Cruz. We don't know who left them, but they were gone by about 700 ACE. They may have been ancestors of the Tehuelche. Whoever they were, their art tells us they were hunters. They used bolas to take all sizes of animals down by the legs. And they were proficient enough with their bolas that they still found time to develop their art and geometry. Champions!
translations.The brilliant red flowers of embothrium: The brilliant red flowers of embothrium are often called "Chilean firebrush" by English speakers. As a girl I liked to spot hummingbirds pollinating them. They are vivacious, passionate flowers -- just like the people of Patagonia!
translations.The infamous Irish dramatist and wit Osc: The infamous Irish dramatist and wit Oscar Wilde visited these parts during the height of the Silver Boom in 1882. In Leadville he delivered a lecture on aesthetics at the local opera house, described the bemused miners as "the best dressed men in America", and declared his fondness for a sign reading "Please do not shoot the pianist. He is doing his best", saying that it was recognition that "bad art merits the penalty of death".
translations.Legends have it that the mines around he: Legends have it that the mines around here are inhabited by creatures called Tommyknockers, little figures dressed in miners' garb who commit random acts of mischief. The "knocker" in their name comes from the knocking on mine walls they were said to do, either to warn of an impending collapse or to bring it about, depending on your attitude towards them.
translations.This 290 million-year-old, 700-ton hunk: This 290 million-year-old, 700-ton hunk of red sandstone makes for a popular photo opportunity. Erosion has gradually stripped away the layers at its base, leaving the formation perched precariously on its tiptoes. Its less famous cousin was removed and shattered in 1936 after its wobbling was deemed a danger to the public, and it seems like it's only a matter of time until a similar fate befalls Balanced Rock, either because of the forces of nature or vandals trying to topple it.
translations.While plans are still nascent, Silver Ri: While plans are still nascent, Silver Ridge Peaks has unparalleled potential to offer intrepid travelers a large variety of outdoor and extreme sports activities, from kayaking and rock-climbing in the summer to snowboarding and skiing in the winter. In the meantime, hiking trails continue to be available to the public. The most demanding trails up into the mountains tend to be accessible from late spring to September, but some at lower elevations are open year-round.
translations.The colonisation and expansion of the Un: The colonisation and expansion of the United States were carried out with a series of bloody wars and massacres across three centuries. In the mid- to late- 19th century, the U.S. government instituted policies which in Colorado forced Native Americans who had lived for centuries as nomadic hunter-gatherers to move en masse to reservations to take up farming, own property, and give up their language and culture. Resistance was quashed in massacres such as the one at Sand Creek, where an estimated 150 to 500 civilians were slaughtered.
translations.Fresh rabbits yielding better than befor: Fresh rabbits yielding better than before. Good for trapping.
translations.Tracked a lynx here last night. Think I: Tracked a lynx here last night. Think I scared him off good.
translations.The woods here are haunted. Spirits of d: The woods here are haunted. Spirits of dead hunters. Men of reckless abandon. I hope they died with full bellies.
translations.There is silence here. And snow. But no: There is silence here. And snow. But no game. Today at least. Tomorrow, I will take my chances again.
translations.I couldn't get a fire on before the snow: I couldn't get a fire on before the snow starting falling and nearly froze to death last night! But I didn't. Now the taiga knows who is boss, ha-ha!
translations.The Nenets are nomads who, for at least: The Nenets are nomads who, for at least 1,000 years, have migrated across the peninsula, thousands of kilometers, herding the reindeer which are the lifeblood of their entire community.
translations.The Nenets shamans, or tádyebya, build t: The Nenets shamans, or tádyebya, build these sacred sites for a variety of purposes. Sometimes they praise the natural world, or Num', their greatest of gods. The shamans mediate between the gods, the ancestors, and the Nenets. They sing songs to connect and communicate with spirits, they bless sacred reindeer and sacred sleds, they bless the sacrifice of animals, and they counsel the community on spiritual matters.
translations.The Nenets do not fear the Gateway to th: The Nenets do not fear the Gateway to the Underworld the same way that some locals do, but its appearance does cause concern among them. Most importantly, if the permafrost thaw creates a crater like this one — or even larger — that substantially deters the Nenets' migration route, they would be forced to make drastic, disruptive changes to their traditional way of life.
translations.Here, so close to the Lena Pillars, the: Here, so close to the Lena Pillars, the Nenets honor a sacred land. Perhaps it was carved by the hands of Num' or the pantheon of gods below him. It has always been here, a relic of a world even older than the Nenets. A reminder of an ancient sea-basin gone dry, but perhaps soon to be filled again.
translations.From the notes of c, Documentary Consult:
From the notes of c, Documentary Consultant--
Expeditionary Journal Day 1: 
Excellent weather for expedition. Sunny skies. Unseasonably warm. Lots of thaw, so good thing we brought waterproof boots.

Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 2: 
The coasts here are embattled by wind and rain. Quickly becoming a muddy trip. Food is plentiful. Spirits are high.

Ustinova Expeditionary Journal Day 9:
Tensions among crew boiled over this morning. Group is splitting in two — one group will follow Alena, and another will follow Yuri Poloz. Alena knows the land better. I will continue on with her.

translations.Our arroyo isn't always as dry as the na: Our arroyo isn't always as dry as the name Cauce Muerto, "Dead Riverbank", suggests. Violent summer deluges, las aguas, flood it in mere hours, if they come; precipitation in the desert is a welcome relief, not an expectation. Luckily, desert dwellers are good at waiting, and know exactly how to make the most of things when the rains do finally arrive. Once the banks have flooded, expect to see spadefoot toads taking every chance they have to breed in the ponds that have sprung up, or sparrows nesting for the first time since the previous thunderstorms.
translations.A \"potrero\" is an open range where wra: A "potrero" is an open range where wrangled horses are kept. Horse-racing is still something of an institution in these parts, and there are plenty of local corridos about legendarily fast steeds descended from mustangs. Hang around long enough and you'll definitely hear someone belt out El Moro de Cumpas after one too many glasses of bacanora.
translations.This is what I got Robbo to celebrate ou:
This is what I got Robbo to celebrate our 30 years of friendship - oh gosh, how time flies.

It's a silly little stuffed kangaroo, nothing too special about it. Except its name. My husband Eric and I saw this silly little stuffed kangaroo as we were walking past a prezzy shop in Brisbane a few months ago, and we knew it would be the perfect present to get Robbo riled up.
Thanks a lot for delivering it to him!

You should see the impressive collection of stuffed animals Robbo has at home. Roos, salties, magpie geese, the whole Aussie ecosystem is there. I have to admit though, half of that probably came from me...
translations.I cant sleep. an old lady out by the cam: I cant sleep. an old lady out by the campsite gave me some candy. she told me theres witches here. she said they footsteps scorch the grass and they make horrible screams, like their on fire. Brian told ghost stories. Tai started crying, said she heard noises. what about the others? their all over the place. Im SCARED!!
translations.There is a small padlock key in the holl: There is a small padlock key in the hollow of the rock
translations.For Aunt Betty's 60th bash tomorrow - yo: For Aunt Betty's 60th bash tomorrow - you're welcome!!!
translations.Runebergintorttu is a popular Finnish pa: Runebergintorttu is a popular Finnish pastry that is normally eaten on Runeberg day on 5th of February. It has received its name from a Finnish priest, lyricist and epic poet Johan Ludvig Runeberg. There are many variants of the pastry, but the most common one is made with almonds and breadcrumbs that are drenched in rum and garnished with raspberry jam and icing.
translations.The rocks used in saunas are usually eit: The rocks used in saunas are usually either Diabase, Olivine or ceramic stones specially manufactured for saunas. These types of rock can withstand high temperature variations without cracking. They absorb and release moisture evenly over time without giving off any odor. The rocks are also cut into the correct size to fit the heating unit.
translations.NEWSPAPER ARTICLE - VISTA ESPAÑA UNDER I: NEWSPAPER ARTICLE - VISTA ESPAÑA UNDER INVESTIGATION
translations.A torn photograph of two men standing in: A torn photograph of two men standing in a cactus patch. In the background is a distinctly shaped hill and a small shrine. The date on the back reads "septiembre de 1916" — September 1916.
translations.This bridge was called \"Long Bridge\" i:
This bridge was called "Long Bridge" if I remember correctly. It's one of the more spectacular views on that scenic railroad they have here.

TREV convinced me to go on that excursion 20 years ago, but I must say I preferred the view from down there, looking up towards the bridge. Away from all the noise, you know.
translations.If you ever need any help or general inf: If you ever need any help or general information, your Codex is a great place to start.
translations.I love hunting Eastern Wild Turkeys. I d: I love hunting Eastern Wild Turkeys. I don't know, there's something special about the gobble and the chase.
translations.The colors of these ducks are just gorge: The colors of these ducks are just gorgeous. One of the great wonders of nature if you ask me.
translations.When I was a kid I thought these ducks w: When I was a kid I thought these ducks were always cracking each other up and having a great time together. Still sounds a bit like that now, if I'm honest.
translations.If you're looking for Bobwhite Quails, y: If you're looking for Bobwhite Quails, you need to be more organized in your approach and be ready when they flush.
translations.I used to collect the plumage of the Rin: I used to collect the plumage of the Ring-Necked Pheasant, Dad and I had them framed over my bed back home.
translations.Your best chance to hunt Raccoons is at: Your best chance to hunt Raccoons is at night.
translations.Many people don't know it, but Coyote hu: Many people don't know it, but Coyote hunting is the most common form of predator hunting.
translations.The Whitetail has a large number of soun: The Whitetail has a large number of sounds and bleats. If you spend enough time studying them, you'll start to hear subtle differences between individuals.
translations.You may not be a student, but we can all: You may not be a student, but we can all use a refresher. Reading your codex will help you plan and prepare more effectively.
translations.What a premium location for a sleepy war: What a premium location for a sleepy warden!
translations.Walls and a roof, what more could you as: Walls and a roof, what more could you ask for?
translations.See? It's not just our tribe's history i: See? It's not just our tribe's history in this place. It's EVERY tribe. All of humanity. These are among the oldest known paintings in history. I bet you can find more of them. Take photos when you do -- they may be worth something.
translations.That's unmistakably lesser kudu. But the: That's unmistakably lesser kudu. But there's nothing "lesser" about these antelope. They are sweet, peaceful souls. Laidback and a bit shy, so you'll have to work for them.
translations.Mhungbye, the side-striped jackal, stick: Mhungbye, the side-striped jackal, sticks to the woods and the scrub, scavenging from other predators, or negligent campers. Unless fruit is in season! When there's fruit, that's all Mhungbye eat. Consider them "gentle" predators.
translations.Homgonyi -- the blue wildebeest -- were: Homgonyi -- the blue wildebeest -- were born to run! And they can run in herds of thousands. Unfortunately, they are not the healthiest animals. Diseases like foot-and-mouth spread quickly among them. So do parasites. We must keep a watchful eye over our fleet-footed friends.
translations.Do your hips ache? Do your legs hurt? Mi: Do your hips ache? Do your legs hurt? Mine do. Don't drive that ATV too fast or you'll be busted up too. Then I'll have to seek YOUR replacement.
translations.[changing tune] Eish! Guess I should kee: [changing tune] Eish! Guess I should keep you humble. After all, can't have you turning out like your Brother. Look up "humble" in a thesaurus and his face is pictured as an antonym. If he tried your job for one day, I bet he'd wind up at the bottom of a chasm like Baden.
translations.That… is a morbid thought. What was I--o: That… is a morbid thought. What was I--oh, righ! [clear throat] We are all proud of you, what you've done for Vurhonga, and for the local community. Thank you, Grandchild. Happy hunting. Be humble.
translations.Watch yourself! No one's coming to rescu: Watch yourself! No one's coming to rescue you out here if you get hurt, and there's no hospital for miles. You did bring a first aid kit... right?
Tents are a home away from home for me. Nothing like a simple fire, some food in your belly and a sleeping bag to crawl into after a long day in the bush.
translations.I've already shot some great bucks aroun: I've already shot some great bucks around here. Why don't you set up the tower, climb up, and see what you can find?
translations.I've been using this tower as a glassing: I've been using this tower as a glassing spot.
translations.Not afraid of a little manual labor, I h: Not afraid of a little manual labor, I hope? This blind should be a great spot to spy on animals when it's all set.
translations.Hunting's all about patience. Set up the: Hunting's all about patience. Set up the blind and wait for the animals to come to you.
translations.Nothing like a gentle summer rain to inv: Nothing like a gentle summer rain to invigorate you after a hard day's hunt. Just watch the sky — I got struck by lightning in my backyard as a kid and it is not fun.
translations.I cut one out, thinking nothing of the l: I cut one out, thinking nothing of the little scrape on my hand. A few weeks later, it had festered into an open wound. The lesson? Leave dead things alone, or at least wear gloves.
translations.I'm more of a visual thinker, but I'll f: I'm more of a visual thinker, but I'll fill you in on what you need to know about this place. Just, um, excuse my writing style.
translations.This is one of the only places in northe: This is one of the only places in northern Mexico you can hunt pheasant. There's more than enough scrub for them to hide in, so you've gotta be tactical: cut off their escape routes and they'll flush every time.
translations.The whitetail here are prize-winning, an: The whitetail here are prize-winning, and there's not as much competition as over the border. I've seen some racks out here.
translations.I was obsessed with bobcats as a kid, li: I was obsessed with bobcats as a kid, like "wanted one as a pet" obsessed. I know better than to think I could catch one now, of course. But a man can dream...
translations.Coyotes are adaptable; they'll live anyw: Coyotes are adaptable; they'll live anywhere and eat anything. Must be why they're shapeshifters in so many myths.
translations.The antelope jackrabbit was made for shr: The antelope jackrabbit was made for shrublands. They can be a bit tricky to spot among the creosote bushes, but they're skittish, so listen for the thumping of their paws.
translations.Bet you don't think of mountains like th: Bet you don't think of mountains like this when you think "Mexico", no? This place is full of surprises.
translations.You wanna give flushing lessons here? I: You wanna give flushing lessons here? I mean it!
translations.Home sweet home! You know, you almost fe: Home sweet home! You know, you almost feel like family now. Almost.
translations.Flushing's fun, no? Allows you to get pr: Flushing's fun, no? Allows you to get pretty tactical. Looking forward to seeing how your technique improves.
translations.That's one for the books! I hope you get: That's one for the books! I hope you get what I meant when I said our whitetail were prize-winning now.
translations.Las equipatas — the winter rains. We ten: Las equipatas — the winter rains. We tend to get pretty gentle weather this time of year; nothing like the deluges come summer.
translations.Our marble quarry closed a long time ago: Our marble quarry closed a long time ago, but for a time, the very rock beneath you sustained local families, including my own.
translations.Are you familiar with the Reconquista? I: Are you familiar with the Reconquista? It is a period of almost eight centuries, ending in the formation of the nation of Spain.
translations.These towers are built on military tower: These towers are built on military tower foundations that are centuries old. During the Reconquista, they changed hands several times.
translations.While we are most famous for our wildlif: While we are most famous for our wildlife, Cuatro Colinas' olives have a very good reputation in culinary circles.
translations.When the crusades began, the pope offere: When the crusades began, the pope offered indulgences to anyone willing to claim this land for God.
translations.The winery in town has won a few awards: The winery in town has won a few awards with wine from our grapes.
translations.Many of these towers were outposts for t: Many of these towers were outposts for the castles that were built here once the Christians took over.
translations.During the civil war, my great-grandfath: During the civil war, my great-grandfather was forced to leave the Castillo, and spent the night, hiding here.
I crashed on this stretch of road, once. I had to cancel a holiday due to a broken leg.
translations.After the civil war, many of the landown: After the civil war, many of the landowners moved to the city and hired crews to run their farms.
translations.These old towers have stood the test of: These old towers have stood the test of time remarkably well. Powerful memorials to our history.
translations.This was once seen as a \"holy well\", a: This was once seen as a "holy well", and pilgrims would come to be healed by it.
translations.It took a lot of men and a lot of dynami: It took a lot of men and a lot of dynamite to blast that road into existence.
translations.\"Prosperity.\" Tourists like to visit,: "Prosperity." Tourists like to visit, but the history of the place hangs over it like a stormcloud.
translations.Don't worry, it's boarded up tight and w: Don't worry, it's boarded up tight and we take readings every three months to make sure it's safe.
translations.My dad's not a big reader, but he loves: My dad's not a big reader, but he loves to tell people that Oscar Wilde visited Colorado during the silver boom.
translations.Every now and then we get requests from: Every now and then we get requests from film companies, looking to shoot out there. Once, dad even got to be an extra!
translations.I used to love going there...to be hones: I used to love going there...to be honest, I still do. Everyone has a favourite dinosaur, right?
translations.My ancestors had plenty of run-ins with: My ancestors had plenty of run-ins with european explorers. A lot of them would have died without our help.
translations.I think my dad used to tell these storie: I think my dad used to tell these stories to keep people away from old mineshafts. It never worked, though.
translations.Colorado's famous for its hot springs. W: Colorado's famous for its hot springs. Who needs a hot tub when you've got this?
translations.A little bit of know-how and ingenuity c: A little bit of know-how and ingenuity can go a long way, out here in the Rockies.
translations.You want a real work out? See if you can: You want a real work out? See if you can run the incline. My calves are normally on fire by the time I reach half-way.
translations.In a place where all you can see are mou: In a place where all you can see are mountains, these ones have always stuck out to me. I like the color.
translations.These rattles are very special. They con: These rattles are very special. They contain quartz crystals that give off little bursts of light when they strike each other.
translations.I know that it's going to take time, but: I know that it's going to take time, but I'm hopeful that we'll draw in lots of visitors that want to do adventure sports.
translations.It's a difficult subject, even now. It's: It's a difficult subject, even now. It's not like it's hard to trace the lines from our past to the modern day.
translations.I've lost count of the number of marriag: I've lost count of the number of marriage proposals we've hosted here, but a large percentage happen here.
translations.Of course, Alaska has its own native big: Of course, Alaska has its own native bigfoot legend.
translations.If I ever get tired of keeping the peace: If I ever get tired of keeping the peace, maybe I'll start panning for gold, instead.
translations.Lingonberries. I hate 'em, but my wife c: Lingonberries. I hate 'em, but my wife can't get enough of 'em.
translations.I've worked hard to earn the respect, an: I've worked hard to earn the respect, and sometimes friendship of our native population.
translations.The Alaska railroad has been connecting: The Alaska railroad has been connecting city folk to the bush for a long time, now.
translations.I always get a shiver when people tell s: I always get a shiver when people tell stories about these guys.
translations.I honestly can't even picture the effort: I honestly can't even picture the effort it must have taken to get a bus out there.
translations.Even when the Yukon gold rush ended, som: Even when the Yukon gold rush ended, some stubborn folks stayed out here.
translations.Humans have lived in Alaska for countles: Humans have lived in Alaska for countless millenia. I wonder how this person spent their last day.
translations.We can limit the fires that are being st: We can limit the fires that are being started by people, but the lightning strikes where it wants.
translations.The rail bridge has been here just a lit: The rail bridge has been here just a little longer than I have.
translations.No love lost between me and some of thos: No love lost between me and some of those blokes -- and ladies -- but I've gotta admit that their efforts are the only reason why this place is still doing okay.
translations.There's a lotta meaning crammed into tha: There's a lotta meaning crammed into that word. We let the local iwi and hapū guide our conservation practices here at Te Awaroa.
translations.I wonder if these are the most studied r: I wonder if these are the most studied rocks in the whole world. Gotta be up there with Uluru and Balanced Rock.
translations.\"Where it be, there it be\", as the min: "Where it be, there it be", as the miners used to say. It was a bit of a mixed blessing if you ask me.
translations.I wish we didn't have to use 1080, but d: I wish we didn't have to use 1080, but desperate times and all that. Least we can do is make sure it's as painless as possible.
translations.The size of a chicken, flightless, and h: The size of a chicken, flightless, and hairy: no idea how they became an icon for New Zealand, but I sure do love those little critters.
translations.I'm not much for kitsch. Melanie used to: I'm not much for kitsch. Melanie used to have a whole room in her house crammed with this rubbish: toys, chilly bins, everything under the sun with a picture of a kiwi on it. I guess nostalgia sells?
translations.Isn't this just paradise on earth? I kno: Isn't this just paradise on earth? I know I'm biased, but... [sighs]
translations.We've had a few incidents here over the: We've had a few incidents here over the years, especially in the spring season when there's a lot of rain. I always tell 'em: leave the spelunking to the professionals.
translations.What do you think was running through th: What do you think was running through the head of the person who made this? A memory... a feeling she wanted to capture?
translations.Graduations, weddings, funerals, and eve: Graduations, weddings, funerals, and everything in between: marae are the heart of the community here.
translations.We got a little overly reliant on these: We got a little overly reliant on these tent-pole releases. Well, I say more tents and fewer releases... does that work? [laughs] Nah, you're right.
translations.This might surprise you, but I'm a prett: This might surprise you, but I'm a pretty big rugger fan. Nothing like a rainy Saturday night down the stands watching your local team get destroyed -- it's a Kiwi tradition!
translations.I don't really get why people fall over: I don't really get why people fall over themselves trying to get slightly different variations of the same photo. Can't they just stand back and enjoy it?
translations.Paikea escaped on the back of a whale, a: Paikea escaped on the back of a whale, and through twists and turns here we are today. Te Waipounamu -- that's the South Island to you, the place of greenstone... there's nowhere else I'd rather live.
translations.I'm not sure about this one... Sounds li: I'm not sure about this one... Sounds like some colonists spinning a yarn to make the place sound more exotic.
translations.A fraught history, eh? So much more than: A fraught history, eh? So much more than just a piece of paper.
translations.My kuia, bless her heart, was a mean tān: My kuia, bless her heart, was a mean tāniko weaver. She didn't pass it on, but these days there's a lotta local artisans combining those tried and true techniques with modern designs.
translations.We used to scare ourselves with stories: We used to scare ourselves with stories about them around the campfire, me and my brothers. Never know what's lurking in the bushes 'round here at night...
translations.Imagine the sound of that thing splittin: Imagine the sound of that thing splitting in two, rippling across the water. Boom!
translations.A drink so good they had to ban it. I re: A drink so good they had to ban it. I reckon there are more than a few vintages stashed away in the stockmen's houses, or under some palo verde somewhere in the desert.
translations.It's tough, life out here. The rancheros: It's tough, life out here. The rancheros with the big estates live it large in Hermosillo and rely on vaqueros to do the dirty work. At least my parents have no time for people like that.
translations.You heard the one about the jilted lover: You heard the one about the jilted lover? How about the downtrodden immigrants, or the lesbian teenager? Not my thing musically, but norteño has a way of surprising you.
translations.This is the only place in the world you': This is the only place in the world you'll find the saguaro cactus, and only in lowlands. It needs the summer monsoon to stock up on moisture.
translations.I've worked a lot with conservation orga: I've worked a lot with conservation organisations from across the border. Animals and plants — ecosystems — don't care about borders. Why should conservationists?
translations.The man, the myth. Did you know he invit: The man, the myth. Did you know he invited an American film crew to record his battles? He created his own legend, and now he'll be showing up in corridos until the end of time.
translations.I'm not sure if we've learned those less: I'm not sure if we've learned those lessons yet...
translations.In the north, traveling armies meant tra: In the north, traveling armies meant traveling families. Might as well take up arms; most of them were every bit as qualified as the men.
translations.My abuela used to collect these. She'd d: My abuela used to collect these. She'd dole them out on big occasions: the night before a test, a graduation. I probably still have a few lying around somewhere.
translations.They say that Mexico is a mestizo nation: They say that Mexico is a mestizo nation; indigenous people's history is Mexican history. I hope their future is Mexico's future too.
translations.I don't know what I think about these pa: I don't know what I think about these parades they've started doing. I'm not a traditionalist, but it's a bit... este... tacky, I guess?
translations.The three Cs: copper, cotton, cattle. We: The three Cs: copper, cotton, cattle. We're gonna be dealing with their effects around here for a long time.
translations.I don't know much about the battles or a: I don't know much about the battles or anything, just that it was a big damn loss. Hard to imagine the course of history if Mexico hadn't ceded all that territory.
translations.I know what you're thinking, but it wasn: I know what you're thinking, but it wasn't aliens. This is all geography's doing.
translations.Este... what can I say? We are in the bo: Este... what can I say? We are in the borderlands.
translations.They actually pay quite handsomely to se: They actually pay quite handsomely to set these up here.
translations.Ernsdorf marks the border between the Ri: Ernsdorf marks the border between the Rinderland mountains and the Hirschfelden farmlands. The main attraction here is the Ernsdorf cave, and we get a lot of spelunkers all year round. Make sure to check it out!
translations.Schonfeldt is not only known for its goo: Schonfeldt is not only known for its good hunting grounds. There are some old bunkers here from the Great War. We often get youngsters out here exploring them, so keep an extra eye out when you're hunting around there, okay?
translations.Norden used to be the site of a successf: Norden used to be the site of a successful mining operation, kicking off back during the Norden Peak copper rush of 1899. They used the railroad to ship out over a billion pounds of copper from Norden. The copper was mainly used for power lines, since a little thing called electricity was becoming all the rage in the early 1900s.

translations.Situated at the foot of the mountains wh: Situated at the foot of the mountains where the high Andes begin to descend. A transition zone with slopes, scattered forests and small ravines.
translations.Wide open grasslands exposed to constant: Wide open grasslands exposed to constant wind. Rolling puna plains with long sightlines and little natural cover.
translations.Rocky highland terrain scattered with bo: Rocky highland terrain scattered with boulders and sparse vegetation. A harsh landscape where pumas roam among the stone outcrops.
High Andean cliffs and steep ridgelines. Rugged terrain with dramatic views over the valleys below.
translations.A journal containing stories and hearsay: A journal containing stories and hearsay about cryptids, cross-referenced with legends and lore from all over Peru and other nearby countries. The book is written with equal parts ferocity and determination, with excerpts from confusing witness-recollections, blurry photos and marginal writing stating far fetched and unsettling conclusions…

translations.Bet you can already hear the tsetse's bu: Bet you can already hear the tsetse's buzzing and biting, tik-tik-tik-tik-tik. They are bad, bad bugs. Ever since the drought began and animals started clustering at fewer water sources, the tsetse flies have clustered with them. That means we have T&T, tstetses and tripanomisasis, a virus that forms Nagana in livestock and sleeping sickness in humans. There's no vaccine for sleeping sickness, and it can be fatal, but we have medication if you need it. If you brought fly spray, now would be a good time to apply it.
translations.Ndlopfu means \"elephant\". As Uncle Rha: Ndlopfu means "elephant". As Uncle Rhangani's story goes, this gorge was carved by the first elephant, Ndlopfu, dragging his trunk along the earth as he journeyed south to escape the summer heat. I've never heard anyone else tell that story, though, so the odds are Uncle Rhangani made it up.
translations.Ku Navela means \"wish\". Ku Navela Land: Ku Navela means "wish". Ku Navela Land is so bustling with life, so rich with natural beauty, it's an ideal place to connect with your spirituality, whatever that may be. I come here to praise the ancestors and pray, always at my favorite tree -- my Wishing Tree.
translations.By the middle of the 18th century, my fa: By the middle of the 18th century, my family's stewardship of this land was well established. Europe's lords and ladies would visit, with the ladies often being neglected while the lords would spend the whole day hunting. One Doña Emilia made a habit of ascending the tower here so she could observe the hunts through a telescope.
translations.The Roman Empire had a fascination that: The Roman Empire had a fascination that resulted in a huge industry, all across Europe. Our marble quarry dates back to the 14th century, when renaissance artists were being commissioned to create statues in marble. Many noble families across Europe own sculptures carved out of marble from our quarry.
translations.While the Spanish aristocracy have long: While the Spanish aristocracy have long been patrons of Cuatro Colinas, this patch of tree-covered land has always been reserved for hunts that included the regents of Spain. Nowadays, any hunter who wishes to follow in the footsteps of Spanish royalty may do so.
translations.Named for the meadows of beautiful lupin: Named for the meadows of beautiful lupine flowers where, someday, I hope to host my nephew Vicente's wedding. I have always loved the colors of the lupines, and the taste of the lupini beans they produce. But don't eat those lupinis raw! They have to be prepared correctly or they'll make you sick.
translations.The \"Wetlands\" or Заболоченные угодья: The "Wetlands" or Заболоченные угодья are a mosquito paradise… but only in the summer. Lucky for you!
translations.People have fished here at Рыбацкий зали: People have fished here at Рыбацкий залив for a thousand years. You won't have much luck this time of year, unless you brought a heavy saw onto the "Fisherman's Bay".
translations.Холм Зверолова or \"Trapper's Hill.\" So: Холм Зверолова or "Trapper's Hill." Someone looking for wild boars would have a lot of luck here. Why else would so many trappers come here over time?

The cost for using the sauna increases with each use temporarily, but is eventually reset after a period of time.
translations.A photo of what appears to be Faddie, Sc: A photo of what appears to be Faddie, Scotland's second most famous sea serpent.
translations.A photo of what probably isn't Faddie, S: A photo of what probably isn't Faddie, Scotland's second most famous sea serpent.
translations.A truly regional keychain inscribed with: A truly regional keychain inscribed with the name of a loved one.
translations.The island, locally known as Florians Ba: The island, locally known as Florians Bastion, was defended from the greater Pheasant population for many days and many nights. Eventually, the invaders breached the balustrade and flooded the clubhouse, as unfortunately the defenders had to go home for dinner. Expect to find embedded coastal marshlands and island patterns ripe for the plucking.
translations.These bluffs to Salzwiesen's south are a: These bluffs to Salzwiesen's south are a medley of meadows and forests as far as the eye can see and ear can hear. This is prime hunting territory for those that need cover, or a relaxing lullaby of foliage for those who need a break.
translations.The Green-Winged Teal is one of the smal: The Green-Winged Teal is one of the smallest dabbling ducks, and due to this, often sticks to calmer waters such as inland lakes, pools and shallow streams.
translations.Ring-necked pheasants are not great flye: Ring-necked pheasants are not great flyers, and only take to the air as a last ditch effort.
translations.This is it! The Rowdy that dented my car: This is it! The Rowdy that dented my car! A huge Pheasant with road rage! Get after it!
translations.The Black Grouse has distinct red bare s: The Black Grouse has distinct red bare skin over its eyes that plumps up during the courting ritual known as 'lek'.
translations.The Common Raccoon is an adaptable omniv: The Common Raccoon is an adaptable omnivorous land mammal native to North and Central America.

translations.Calburn Canyon, like its sister canyon C: Calburn Canyon, like its sister canyon Chopeeka, was valuable to the indigenous people because of its wealth of salmon, spruce, and larch trees. The indigenous people learned to eat the cambium of the larch specifically, and also extracted the sap from which they could create syrup.

translations.The American mink (Neovison vison) is a: The American mink (Neovison vison) is a small, semi-aquatic mammal with a sleek, elongated body measuring 46 to 71 cm (18 to 28 inches) in length.
translations.Animals can be scared if they see, smell: Animals can be scared if they see, smell, or hear you, and may start to flee. Fleeing animals will run until they feel safe. They will remain vigilant for a period of time afterwards, heightening their senses.
translations.Antelope jackrabbits live in the arid gr: Antelope jackrabbits live in the arid grasslands and shrublands of Northern Mexico and Arizona.
