Be careful with your placement of the Feeder, as any Bait that has been added to the Feeder will be lost if you pick it up again.
translations.Now that the Game Feeder is filled with: Now that the Game Feeder is filled with bait, it will begin to attract animals. Some Feeders will deplete when animals visit, others will dispense Bait constantly over time. When a Feeder becomes low on Bait or empty, be sure to top it up again to keep it active.

translations.Macropus Giganteus or the Eastern Gray K: Macropus Giganteus or the Eastern Gray Kangaroo is the heaviest and second largest marsupial endemic to eastern Australia.
translations.The Eurasian lynx is an elusive predator: The Eurasian lynx is an elusive predator that relies primarily on its excellent eyesight to hunt and detect threats.
translations.The Eurasian Pine Marten (Martes martes): The Eurasian Pine Marten (Martes martes) is a medium-sized omnivore from the Mustelidae family, known for its sleek, rich brown fur and distinctive yellowish throat patch.
translations.The European badger (Meles meles) favors: The European badger (Meles meles) favors environments like forests, meadows, and rural farmland, where it can excavate elaborate underground homes called setts.
translations.The New Zealand feral goats (Capra hircu: The New Zealand feral goats (Capra hircus), were brought onto the island in 1773 by early explorers, whalers, sealers and settlers who brought goats with them for food and bartering.
translations.Feral pigs are smaller and more muscular: Feral pigs are smaller and more muscular than domestic pigs and they have a longer snout that is flattened at the end.
translations.Foliage hides you from animals, but is n: Foliage hides you from animals, but is noisy to traverse. Foliage includes bushes, low-hanging trees, and more.
translations.The gemsbok (Oryx gazella) is the larges: The gemsbok (Oryx gazella) is the largest of the three members of the Oryx genus. Native to the dry plains, deserts and arid regions of southern Africa, the gemsbok lives in large mixed herds and follows a nomadic lifestyle, rarely staying in a territory long enough to overgraze it.
translations.The greater grison (Galictis vittata) is: The greater grison (Galictis vittata) is a sleek member of the weasel family found from southern Mexico to northern Argentina. Fast and agile, it hunts a wide variety of prey, including small mammals, birds, reptiles, and amphibians.
translations.The Hazel Grouse is a very small grouse: The Hazel Grouse is a very small grouse that can be found in mixed coniferous and deciduous forests across Northern Eurasia.
translations.Hunting stands and ground blinds are exc: Hunting stands and ground blinds are excellent for lure hunting. Animals will find it harder to detect you in one of these structures.
translations.The jaguar is a muscular, stocky big cat: The jaguar is a muscular, stocky big cat known for its incredible strength, it can crush prey with a single bite. Jaguars are solitary and territorial, usually hunting at night.
translations.Often found near the grassy fields by wo: Often found near the grassy fields by woodlands, the Javan Rusa sports a brown coat with a reddish hue during the summer half-year.
translations.Press {JUMP} to jump. Jumping causes sud: Press {JUMP} to jump. Jumping causes sudden increases in noise and visibility.
translations.The Mexican bobcat is a solitary, adapta: The Mexican bobcat is a solitary, adaptable predator about twice the size of a house cat.
translations.The Nilgai (literally meaning \"blue cow: The Nilgai (literally meaning "blue cow" in Nepali) has slim legs, a sloped back and is adorned with a mane. It stands as the largest antelope in Asia.
translations.Making noise will scare away animals. Ke: Making noise will scare away animals. Keep an eye on the noise meter.
translations.The North American beaver's long, dark-o: The North American beaver's long, dark-orange, visible incisors grow continuously throughout its life and are worn down through daily use.
translations.The elegant northern pintails are often: The elegant northern pintails are often found swimming through wetlands and lakes with their slender necks and long, pointed tails held high.
translations.The ocelot is a sleek, medium-sized wild: The ocelot is a sleek, medium-sized wild cat native to the Americas. Preferring tropical forests, scrublands, and savannas, the ocelot hunts small mammals, birds, and reptiles at night.
translations.Ring-necked pheasants are not adept flye: Ring-necked pheasants are not adept flyers and take to the air only as a last ditch effort to escape immediate danger.
translations.Press {FIRE_RIGHT} when the preview is w: Press {FIRE_RIGHT} when the preview is white to deploy the remote electronic caller. Hold {AIM} before placing it to change its orientation.
translations.Running increases your heart rate, which: Running increases your heart rate, which will make it harder to keep a steady aim.
translations.The common raccoon is an adaptable omniv: The common raccoon is an adaptable omnivorous land mammal native to North and Central America.
translations.Both male and female reindeer grow antle: Both male and female reindeer grow antlers, with the size being typically larger on the males.
translations.The Rock Ptarmigan is closely related to: The Rock Ptarmigan is closely related to the slightly larger Willow Ptarmigan, and occupies the same natural range in the Arctic and subarctic regions of Eurasia and North America.
translations.The Side-Striped Jackal (Canis Adustus): The Side-Striped Jackal (Canis Adustus) is a mostly nocturnal, opportunistic omnivore found predominantly in Tropical Africa. It prefers the moist, wooded areas of east, west and central Africa and stays away from the rainforests of the same regions.
translations.The snow goose is a migratory waterfowl: The snow goose is a migratory waterfowl found in wetlands and agricultural fields across North America.
translations.The South American tapir (Tapirus terres: The South American tapir (Tapirus terrestris) is a large, stocky herbivore with a short trunk-like snout used to grasp leaves and fruit. Found across much of tropical South America, it prefers humid forests, swamps, and riverbanks.

translations.Learn about the residents of Springbok C: Learn about the residents of Springbok City by spotting male and female springbok.
translations.I kid, but the problem is real. The sava: I kid, but the problem is real. The savanna can't sustain Springbok City. Fewer plants will thrive. The topsoil will erode. Birds that nest in the vanishing shrubs will flee. And if we don't get relief from this drought, the smaller animals competing for grazing areas will die.
translations.On that, your codex has plenty of helpfu: On that, your codex has plenty of helpful information, but in Africa, the world is your classroom. Why only read about springbok when you can see them for yourself? Find a male and a female, one of each, and spot them. Observe them.
Excellent specimen of a male springbok. During the mating season, you'll see guys like him locking horns, vying for territory.
translations.She's a beauty. Nice find! Both male and: She's a beauty. Nice find! Both male and female springbok have horns, and the females are only a smidge smaller than the males, so you'll have to learn to tell them apart.
translations.Okay, one down. Now find a springbok of: Okay, one down. Now find a springbok of the opposite sex.
translations.And, if you really want to show off, get: And, if you really want to show off, get within 50 meters of a springbok and spook them. Springbok are territorial. The ones who see a human threat dominating their territory will lead others away. You'll need to have an expert approach.
translations.Well done! You can give the springbox he: Well done! You can give the springbox herd an extra push by hunting them periodically. And don't forget to spook them! You'll know you have mastered your approach when you can get within 50 meters before spooking them.
translations.Spook 3 springbok in Vuxa while within {: Spook 3 springbok in Vuxa while within {d:50} of them
translations.Oooooh, Boss, that's a proper spook! See: Oooooh, Boss, that's a proper spook! See, I told your Brother you could stick the approach to a springbok. That cynic thinks your success is a fluke, so I'm making a bet with him. If you can spook two more springbok to prove your Brother wrong, I'll share my winnings with you.
translations.That's the style, Boss! Spook one more s: That's the style, Boss! Spook one more springbok to make your Brother pay up.
translations.Assess the wildebeest herds. Spot three: Assess the wildebeest herds. Spot three wildebeests without causing a stampede. And take notes!
translations.As the herd slowly starves it will becom: As the herd slowly starves it will become volatile and the risks of mass stampedes increase. Not good, Boss! The danger of stampede makes hunting these wildebeests especially high risk.
translations.And what do we do in high risk situation: And what do we do in high risk situations? We make preparations! Start by spotting a few wildebeest, bulls or cows, it doesn't matter. What matters is noting where they spend time. Accustom yourself to their behaviors.
translations.The wildebeest are born runners. Calves: The wildebeest are born runners. Calves fall out of their mothers and in a few minutes [swish sound] -- they're off running with the herd. Spot a few more before they bolt.
translations.Aweh, you are tracking wildebeests like: Aweh, you are tracking wildebeests like an old pro -- like me, of course!
translations.But! A wildebeest stampede will crush yo: But! A wildebeest stampede will crush you like a tsetse. So, shoot from a safe distance, at least 150 meters or more.
translations.Shoot from any closer and you are a mamp: Grandchild. ,safe it Play !mampara a NOT you're But mampara. a are you and closer any from ﻰﻠﻋ ﺭﺎﻨﻟﺍ ﻖﻠﻃﺍ
translations.I was not joking about hunting the wilde: I was not joking about hunting the wildebeest from a safe distance. A Senior Warden can't take such unnecessary risks. Try again.
translations.You must have some kind of death wish. G: You must have some kind of death wish. Get back at least 150 meters before you shoot wildebeest. If not for your safety, then for the sanity of your Grandfather.
The safe shot is the professional shot. One down, two to go.
translations.Excellent. The wise hunter listens more: Excellent. The wise hunter listens more often than he shoots, and you listened to me on this one, Grandchild. Well done!
translations.Some numbers of the herd will move this: Some numbers of the herd will move this time around, but they will keep breeding, so from here, continue to apply hunting pressure. Keep their numbers manageable.
translations.Take a look at the lazy jackals and \"pr: each. of one Spot Vupeladyambu. in hares scrub "prolific" and jackals lazy the at look a ﺬﺧ
translations.So, between motivating lazy jackals and: So, between motivating lazy jackals and pressuring happy scrub hares, you've got work to do.
translations.Lazy, lazy side-striped jackal. The jack: Lazy, lazy side-striped jackal. The jackal thrives when it is competing within the food chain, not when it's the apex.
translations.That's one half of this devilish duo ove: That's one half of this devilish duo overrunning the plateau. Now find the other.
translations.That takes care of both parties, and con: That takes care of both parties, and confirms that the reports of their activity are true.
translations.Ah, back at the scene of your peril. Tru: Ah, back at the scene of your peril. Truly, it is a wonder you didn't break both your legs in the fall. Further proof of your Noyi lineage. Now use that magic to fix the bridge instead of falling off it.
translations.Fixed! If it was that easy, why didn't y: Fixed! If it was that easy, why didn't you just do that before? At least now you can use this pathway.
translations.Our search parties have yet to recover B: Our search parties have yet to recover Baden's remains. I know it's gruesome, but could you sniff around the Plateau?
translations.While you are at the bridge, perhaps you: While you are at the bridge, perhaps you could take one more look around for Gustav Baden's remains? We've had multiple search parties out looking for him with no luck.
translations.Maybe since you were lucky enough to fix: Maybe since you were lucky enough to fix the bridge, you'll be lucky enough to solve the mystery of what happened to that poor, deluded HooTuber.
translations.See anything Baden-related? Maybe more o: See anything Baden-related? Maybe more of that jacket?
translations.That's enough time spent on Baden's case: That's enough time spent on Baden's case for us. Hopefully the police pick things up from here. You need to deal with the animals here in Vupeladyambu. Start with the jackals.
translations.You may be scaring the jackals, which is: You may be scaring the jackals, which is good, but this jackal is too damaged to qualify for the study. Try again.
translations.This jackal is a perfect candidate for t: This jackal is a perfect candidate for the study. Bring in two more like this.
translations.It's easy to make a mess of such a littl: It's easy to make a mess of such a little rascal. Make sure you're working with the right tools.
translations.Five in a row, just like Grandfather tau: Five in a row, just like Grandfather taught you!
translations.It might seem like you're spoiling a par: It might seem like you're spoiling a party for all the horny hares and fat jackals, but this isn't some hip bar in Joburg. It's the bush. Life out here may seem like a struggle, but those who can handle the struggle, survive. You can handle it, too, Grandchild. That's why I'm so proud you're succeeding me.
translations.Accustomed to the 470 yet? You better be: Accustomed to the 470 yet? You better be, it could save your life!
translations.Eish, that's sloppy work, Grandchild! Ar: Eish, that's sloppy work, Grandchild! Are you trying to give me a heart attack? Study your codex. Adjust your shot placement. Shoot for the quick kill.
translations.Wardens like us, traditionalists, we do: Wardens like us, traditionalists, we do not hunt for trophies. But with these alphas defending the herd, they simply do not feel threatened enough to move along.

translations.Every part of North America seems to hav: Every part of North America seems to have its own "bigfoot" legend, and Alaska is no different. The legend of the "tornit" wild men has its roots in native Alaskan folklore, where a tornit broke a human's prized kayak, prompting the man to kill the tornit out of vengeance and grief. It's said that ever since that killing, the tornits have avoided human contact, explaining why reported sightings are so few and far between.
translations.The Lingonberry has long been a part of: The Lingonberry has long been a part of the native Alaskan diet, partly due to how well it lends itself to being stored for extended periods, either frozen, buried in an underground cache or as a preserve. As well as being a valuble food resource, native Alaskans also value its medical properties, citing it as a cure for the cold, coughs or indigestion.
translations.The \"Urayuli\" are said to be ten-foot-: The "Urayuli" are said to be ten-foot-tall, furry, ape-like creatures with glowing eyes. Though generally seen as benevolent, legend has it that they are the transformed bodies of lost children that went missing in the woods. This is made all the more unsettling by their eerie wailing.
translations.Alaska's unique combination of vast size: Alaska's unique combination of vast size and harsh weather conditions has always made transportation a problem. The Alaska Railroad hasn't expanded much in the last 100 years, but as a vital route for both people and cargo, the Alaska Railroad is a symbol of mankind's determination in the face of overwhelming natural obstacles.
translations.The legend of the \"Kushtaka\" speaks of: The legend of the "Kushtaka" speaks of a race of shape-shifting supernatural creatures who can take on the form of otters. Stories conflict regarding the nature of these creatures, and where some say they are benevolent creatures who will attempt to save a soul from drowning or freezing, other sources state that they will lure people to the water's edge to kill them, or to turn them into Kushtaka's as well.
translations.The Yukon has hosted humanity for millen: The Yukon has hosted humanity for millenia. Roughly eleven thousand years ago, the body of a young child was burned to ash inside a family hearth. This funeral site formed part of an archaelogical dig in 2012, where the hearth and its contents were uncovered, along with the body of a young woman and a 5-year-old boy. The results of this dig are still being used to help historians understand the dynamics of our pre-historic ancestors.
translations.That is a beautiful reindeer. Aim for th: That is a beautiful reindeer. Aim for the heart, lungs — try not to cause unnecessary damage.
translations.So… The police picked up Georgy and he —: So… The police picked up Georgy and he — he confessed to the hoax, but he didn't mean to hurt anyone. He had good intentions. He— He was trying to scare our expedition away, actually. To make sure nobody else got hurt. [deep breath] This is all my fault. Sorry, you are busy working. I should let you get to it.
translations.Anyway, thank you. You're helping this e: Anyway, thank you. You're helping this expedition do so much good for the Nenets community. It is rare for an outsider to make such contributions. I feel… like I don't deserve it.
translations.Care for a little more local insight? Ne: Care for a little more local insight? Nenets can recognize the face of every reindeer in their herd, even among thousands of animals. Their clothing, their food, their tools — it all comes from the reindeer. Some reindeer are so sacred, they will never be slaughtered.
translations.How I wish I could be there with you… No: How I wish I could be there with you… Not in a romantic way! We are close, but not that close! I mean I wish I could be out of this office. To be in the wild, trekking and climbing… Izvini! I am being sentimental. Let me give you some peace in this beautiful place.
translations.That reindeer is dead... Gutted... But n: That reindeer is dead... Gutted... But not eaten? Lynx do not kill for sport. Maybe there was a lynx, but it was scared off before it could eat? By what, I don’t know. See if there are tracks nearby.
translations.A dead lynx, too? That can only mean one: A dead lynx, too? That can only mean one thing… Do you see other tracks nearby?
translations.That cabin looks like a good place to wa: That cabin looks like a good place to wait it out. The storm should blow over in about 8 hours — take that time to rest.
translations.Okay! The storm is over and we’re back t: Okay! The storm is over and we’re back to the slightly more tolerable version of sub-zero weather.
translations.What happened to getting the photo? You': What happened to getting the photo? You're usually better at following instructions! Anyway…
translations.What happened here? With that many shell: What happened here? With that many shells, that much damage, these maniacs must have been firing in every direction from inside here. But at what?! Are they drunk? Or -- MAYBE they're being hunted by the Eloko… Get out of there.
translations.What are those pictures of? A ghost jack: What are those pictures of? A ghost jackal?! No. Not again. Your Brother thinks Gustav found his fungi and it inspired these drawings. But I think we are dealing with something well beyond fungi… A restless spirit who does not want Gustav Baden to journey further along.
translations.Hmm. I may be superstitious and traditio: Hmm. I may be superstitious and traditional. But… These aren't field notes. These are the ramblings of a mad man! I don't know what kind of dung Baden went digging in, but a person in this state of mind, unfamiliar with this terrain, interacting with a jackal is a bad idea, ghost or no ghost.
translations.Of course the sky is belching, right whe: Of course the sky is belching, right when we’re trying to save this mampara from himself. Hurry, Grandchild. And be careful! Mind your step up there. Mind the Ghost.
translations.Grandchild? Hello? What happened? Grandc: Grandchild? Hello? What happened? Grandchild! Little Brother, get a drone out there and find your sibling! I don't care about the weather! Grandchild, listen to me… We're going to find you. You will be okay. You HAVE TO be okay…  Please, ancestors, protect your Grandchild, the noyi hunter who came home to honor you!
translations.Grandchild? If you can hear this, I'm so: Grandchild? If you can hear this, I'm sorry for everything. This Ghost Jackal… that bridge… it's all my fault. I've failed you.
translations.Grandchild, you're moving again! If you: Grandchild, you're moving again! If you can hear me, you're close to a cave… That cave is where the jackals kept their den. I don't know what the Ghost Jackal wants from you, but I tell you this…
translations.…so we always have a chance to be redeem: …so we always have a chance to be redeemed in their eyes.
translations.Keep your eyes on the horizon. The view: Keep your eyes on the horizon. The view there is--Mm! Spectacular…
translations.But… I called you here so I could retire: But… I called you here so I could retire, and there's no taking that back! Obviously the job is yours, so... Congratulations, Senior Warden! Now YOU get to deal with your Brother and his HooTubers and his spiritual skepticism. Congratulations!
translations.Doctor Dana is… an acquired taste. To he: Doctor Dana is… an acquired taste. To her, there's a wrong way, and then there's her way. Now that you're Senior Warden, I guarantee she's going to test you, to find out which way YOU do things.
translations.Hola, qué tal? ¡Escucháme! Welcome to Pa: Hola, qué tal? ¡Escucháme! Welcome to Parque Fernando! We’ll keep this brief, before my nieces’ pendejitos act up again.
translations.Are you in a hurry? Don’t get me wrong,: Are you in a hurry? Don’t get me wrong, you’re welcome to run free here. It’s just... unorthodox to hear a hunter crashing through the brush instead of taking a slow and stealthy approach.
translations.Oye, deja eso! Si la insultaste, debes p: Oye, deja eso! Si la insultaste, debes pedirle disculpas… No me mandés fruta!
translations.The winds here shift at a moment’s notic: The winds here shift at a moment’s notice, so you should always pay attention to which way the wind is blowing. Like Fernando once told me, "He who spits in the wind gets what he deserves." Poetic, sí?
translations.¿Como andas? Do you hear or see any sign: ¿Como andas? Do you hear or see any signs of life around you?
translations.Stretch your legs out. I'll start you of: Stretch your legs out. I'll start you off with some routine responsibilities. You can do these in any order, I don't care, as long you do the jobs well. I try not to micro-manage… Well, not *too* much.
translations.We have a saying here, \"The truth is in: We have a saying here, "The truth is in the milanesa." Which is to say, proof is in action. And so far, you are proving worthy of your reputation. ¡Bravo!

translations.The capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris): The capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris) is the largest living rodent. Native to South America, capybaras are excellent swimmers and move easily through the water thanks to their partially webbed feet.
translations.The Grant caribou is a large, robust sub: The Grant caribou is a large, robust subspecies found in the boreal forests of western Canada and parts of Alaska. With a thick fur coat and long legs, they are adapted for cold climates and varied terrain. Grant caribou are migratory, traveling long distances between summer and winter ranges, primarily in search of lichen.
translations.The chamois is a challenging hunt, posse: The chamois is a challenging hunt, possessing extremely keen senses.
translations.\"Atypicals\" are animals which exhibit: "Atypicals" are animals which exhibit unusual growth in one or both antlers, and deviate significantly from the typically expected shapes and patterns. These deviations can be genetic, but are often also caused by injury or issues with nutrition. Examples of deviations can include double beamed antlers, stunted or spiked antlers, and antlers that are bent in an abnormal direction. Some hunters prize Atypicals as rare trophies, while others may just target them for the good of the herd.

translations.The codex is a section in the pause menu: The codex is a section in the pause menu screen that provides you with a lot of information about your profile, statistics, information about the world, and tutorials for the game. If you'd like to view a tutorial again, you can always find it in the codex's tutorials section.
translations.Press {FREELOOK} to toggle freelook on o:
Press {FREELOOK} to toggle freelook on or off. With freelook enabled, use {LOOK_UP} {LOOK_DOWN} {LOOK_LEFT} {LOOK_RIGHT} to rotate your view without moving your hunter.

You can use freelook while automatically walking using {AUTOWALK}. 

Freelook is automatically toggled off by jumping, reloading, or interacting with various objects. Toggling freelook off will return your view to the center of the screen.
translations.Press {HEADLAMP} to turn your headlamp o:
Press {HEADLAMP} to turn your headlamp on. You'll need it to find tracks when hunting at night.

Nighttime begins at 19:00 and ends at 05:00.
translations.When hunting, it is always important to:
When hunting, it is always important to take your stance into consideration. There are three stances: standing, crouching, and prone.

Use {JUMP} to stand, {CROUCH} to crouch, and {PRONE} to go prone. 

Crouching and going prone will make you less visible to animals.

translations.Collared peccaries or “Javelinas” are sm: Collared peccaries or “Javelinas” are small, bulky, short-legged mammals in the Tayassuidae family which includes animals such as pigs, boars and hogs.
translations.Some commands are naturally executed mor: Some commands are naturally executed more often. These are called context sensitive commands and can be called without entering the command wheel.
translations.The graceful vicuña is the smallest of t: The graceful vicuña is the smallest of the South American camelids, found high in the windswept Andes. It moves in small herds led by a male, always alert for predators, and flees quickly when threatened.
